01. The ML System Design Interview Framework, Master Architecture, and Portal Index

Problem 01 does not ask you to design one product. It covers the reusable answer template, a generic production ML system you can adapt to any prompt, and an index of the prep portals with what each one teaches. Later chapters fill this template in for specific problems.

Company tags

Company What is reported about the MLSD round Source
Meta Onsite with 1-2 ML system design rounds (E5/E6 often 2), usually ranking or recsys, e.g. news feed, Marketplace [9] [35] [36]
Google Design rounds at L5+ include content ranking and recommender scaling; reported prompts include YouTube recs, Gmail spam, YouTube copyright detection [10] [33]
Amazon Covered by IGotAnOffer as a source of real MLSD questions [8] [11]
Apple Has a dedicated MLE interview guide that includes ML design [12]
OpenAI / Anthropic Newer question banks lean toward LLM systems (e.g. "Design ChatGPT") [13] [14] [37]
Google, LinkedIn, Snap, Coupang, Stitch Fix Khang Pham reports MLE offers from these five; his question material draws on Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Google, Microsoft, Snap, LinkedIn interviews [17]
LinkedIn, Airbnb, YouTube Used as the basis for Khang Pham's case studies (LinkedIn feed ranking, Airbnb search ranking, YouTube recommendation) [17]

Portals and books that cover the framework itself: Exponent / Aced [3][4], ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu) [15], Educative Grokking MLSD [5] and Khang Pham's course [6][17], Hello Interview [7], IGotAnOffer [8], alirezadir/AIMLInterviews [1][2], Chip Huyen [18][19][20][21], Patrick Halina [23], Babushkin & Kravchenko (Manning) [22], interviewing.io / Prepfully mocks [34][35], DesignGurus [38], Interview Kickstart [39].

Requirements & scale (the template you fill in for every prompt)

Dimension What to pin down in minutes 0-8 Typical default if the interviewer stays vague
Business goal What gets better: engagement, revenue, safety, cost Pick one primary metric and 1-2 guardrails [1]
Functional Inputs, outputs, surfaces, personalization yes/no "Return top-K items per request" (assumption)
ML objective Classification / regression / ranking / retrieval / generation Pointwise P(engage) ranker (assumption)
Users DAU, requests per user per day 100M-1B DAU for FAANG-scale prompts (assumption)
Catalog Number of candidates 1M-10B items, so retrieval must be ANN (assumption)
QPS Peak online requests 10k-100k QPS; Uber Michelangelo reported >250k pred/s [28]
Latency End-to-end p99 100-200 ms total, model scoring 10-50 ms (assumption)
Freshness How fast new items, users and features take effect Features within minutes, retrain daily (assumption)
Data Labels available? Logging exists? Privacy limits? Implicit feedback from logs [1]
Constraints Cost, on-device, interpretability, fairness, regions Server-side GPU or CPU serving (assumption)
Is ML needed? Heuristic baseline first "Launch without ML is fine" (Rule #1) [31]

The canonical answer template (what every portal converges on)

DIAGRAM 0: The 45-60 minute answer flow with time budget (synthesised from [1][3][5][7][15])

  0-8 min             8-15 min            15-25 min           25-35 min
+----------------+  +----------------+  +----------------+  +----------------+
| 1 CLARIFY      |  | 2 FRAME AS ML  |  | 3 DATA &       |  | 4 MODEL        |
| goal, scope,   |->| inputs/outputs,|->| FEATURES       |->| baseline ->    |
| scale, latency,|  | objective,     |  | sources, labels|  | advanced, loss,|
| constraints    |  | metrics        |  | features       |  | training       |
+-------+--------+  +----------------+  +----------------+  +-------+--------+
        ^                                                           |
        |                                                           v
        |           45-55 min           40-45 min           35-40 min
        |           +----------------+  +----------------+  +----------------+
        |           | 7 MONITOR      |  | 6 SERVE        |  | 5 EVALUATE     |
        |           | drift, alerts, |<-| batch/online,  |<-| offline + A/B  |
        |           | retrain cadence|  | ANN, latency   |  | metrics,       |
        |           |                |  | budget, rollout|  | guardrails     |
        |           +-------+--------+  +----------------+  +----------------+
        |                   |
        +-------------------+  feedback loop: new data, failures, retraining
  55-60 min: wrap up -- summarize, name trade-offs, say what you'd do next

Step-name mapping across portals

Generic step ByteByteGo 7-step [15] alirezadir 9-step [1] Educative 6-step [5] Chip Huyen [18] Hello Interview [7]
Clarify Clarifying requirements Problem formulation Problem scoping / clarify Project setup Problem framing (5-7 min)
Frame as ML Frame problem as ML task Problem formulation + Metrics Problem formulation Project setup Problem framing
Architecture (inside serving) Architectural components (MVP) System architecture Serving High-level design
Data Data preparation Data collection & preparation Data strategy Data pipeline Data & features
Features Data preparation Feature engineering Data strategy Data pipeline Data & features
Model Model development Model dev & offline eval Model design + trade-offs Modeling Modeling
Evaluation Evaluation Metrics + online testing Offline & online eval Modeling (debug) Evaluation
Serving Deployment & serving Prediction service + deployment Deploy under constraints Serving Inference
Monitoring Monitoring & infrastructure Scaling, monitoring, updates Monitoring & iteration Serving (maintain) Deep dives
  • The ByteByteGo labels come from the book's Chapter 1 framework. The other columns paraphrase the cited pages.
  • alirezadir orders the steps differently: metrics come 2nd and the MVP architecture 3rd, before any data work, so the interviewer sees the whole box diagram early [1].
  • Hello Interview says its steps are "guideposts, not hard rules": if the interviewer pulls you off course, follow them [7].

DIAGRAM 3: Model architecture (the generic two-stage model pair)

DIAGRAM 3: Two-tower retriever + multi-task ranker, the default answer for recsys, feed, ads and search prompts [27]

       RETRIEVAL: TWO-TOWER                         RANKING: MULTI-TASK DNN
+-------------------+ +-------------------+  +-------------------------------------+
| user feats: id,   | | item feats: id,   |  | user | item | context | cross feats |
| history, demo,    | | text/img emb,     |  +------------------+------------------+
| context           | | category, age     |                     | embeddings + dense
+---------+---------+ +---------+---------+                     v   normalization
          |                     |            +------------------+------------------+
          v                     v            | feature interaction: DCN cross /    |
+---------+---------+ +---------+---------+  | attention over user history / FM    |
| user tower (MLP)  | | item tower (MLP)  |  +------------------+------------------+
+---------+---------+ +---------+---------+                     | shared bottom/MMoE
          | u (d=64-256)        | v                 +-----------+------------+
          +------> dot(u,v) <---+                   |           |            |
                      |                             v           v            v
  loss: sampled softmax with in-batch          +--------+  +--------+  +----------+
  negatives; v precomputed into ANN index      | P(clk) |  | P(like)|  | E[dwell] |
                      |                        +---+----+  +---+----+  +----+-----+
                      v                            | BCE       | BCE        | Huber
       top ~1k candidates ---- fed to ranker       +-----------+------------+
                                                               v
                                    final score = w1*P(clk) + w2*P(like) + w3*E[dwell]
                                    (weights tuned online: the "value model")
Problem family Swap DIAGRAM 3 for Output
Recsys / feed / ads / search two-tower + multi-task ranker (above) ranked list
Moderation / fraud / spam multimodal encoder + classifier heads P(violation) per policy
Visual / semantic search image or text encoder + ANN (single tower) top-K neighbors
ETA / pricing / forecasting GBDT or DNN regressor continuous value
RAG / LLM assistant retriever + reranker + LLM generator grounded text

  • Other public platforms with the same shape: Google TFX (data validation -> trainer -> model validation -> serving, used for Google Play) [29], Meta FBLearner Flow (workflows, feature store marketplace, per-model inference containers) [32].
  • Sculley et al. explain why the diagram is mostly not the model: glue code, data dependencies, hidden feedback loops and configuration debt [30].

Data & labels (generic checklist)

Item Options Interview tip
Label source Natural (click, purchase), explicit feedback, human annotation, programmatic/weak, transfer learning, active learning [1] Say which label you use and why it matches the business goal
Positives / negatives Engaged vs impressed-not-engaged; random or hard negatives for retrieval Do not use non-impressed items as negatives in a ranker
Label delay Conversions arrive late; spam reports late Use attribution windows and delayed-feedback correction
Bias Position bias, exposure bias, selection bias Log position, use exploration traffic, IPS weighting
Split Time-based train/val/test; no user leakage Random splits leak the future
Imbalance Downsample negatives, class weights, focal loss Recalibrate after downsampling
Privacy PII, consent, regional retention; human annotation exposes data [1] Mention it as a constraint; weak labels or on-device reduce exposure [1]

Features

Group Examples Freshness / store
User demographics, locale, long-term interests, embeddings Batch daily, online KV
Item category, text/image embeddings, age, quality score Batch on create/update
Context time, device, surface, session state Request time
User-item cross past interactions with author/category, similarity Streaming (minutes)
Aggregates / counters CTR over 1h/1d/7d windows, popularity Streaming + batch backfill
Representations one-hot, hashing, learned embeddings, normalization, bucketization [1] Shared feature store [28]
Training-serving skew log features at serve time; same transform code Rule: reuse code offline and online [31]

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Option Pros Cons
0 Heuristic / popularity / rules Ships in days, strong baseline No personalization [31]
1 Logistic regression + crosses Fast, calibrated, interpretable Manual feature crosses
2 GBDT (XGBoost/LightGBM) Strong on tabular data, little tuning Weak on sparse IDs and raw text/images
3 Two-tower DNN (retrieval) Scales to billions of items with ANN No late user-item interaction
4 Deep ranker (DCN, DLRM, attention over history) Learns interactions, uses embeddings GPU cost, latency
5 Multi-task / MMoE One model, several objectives Tuning the task weights
6 Pretrained / LLM components Cold-start, semantics Cost, latency, hallucination

Loss functions

Task Loss
Binary engagement / classification Binary cross-entropy (weighted or focal for imbalance)
Multi-class / policy labels Softmax CE, or multi-label sigmoid BCE
Retrieval embeddings Sampled softmax with in-batch negatives, contrastive, triplet
Learning to rank Pairwise (RankNet, BPR), listwise (LambdaRank, softmax)
Regression (ETA, dwell) MSE, MAE, Huber, quantile loss for intervals
Multi-task Weighted sum of per-head losses

Offline metrics

Task Metrics
Classification ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, precision/recall@threshold, log loss, calibration (ECE)
Retrieval Recall@K, hit rate@K
Ranking NDCG@K, MAP, MRR
Regression MAE, RMSE, MAPE
System p50/p99 latency, throughput, cost per 1k predictions [1]
Always Slice metrics: new users, regions, cold items, protected groups

Online metrics & A/B testing

Item Generic answer
Primary metric CTR, session time, conversion, revenue, task success [1]
Counter metrics direct negative feedback: hides, reports [1]
Guardrail metrics unsubscribes, latency, crash rate (assumption)
Rollout shadow -> canary -> A/B with control/test split and null hypothesis [1]; ramp 1% -> 5% -> 50% -> full (assumption)
Alternatives multi-armed bandits [1]; interleaving for ranking (assumption)
Pitfalls novelty effect, network effects, sample-ratio mismatch, peeking
Decision ship if primary is significantly up and guardrails are flat

Serving & latency budget (typical 200 ms p99, assumption)

Component Budget Technique
Gateway + auth 10 ms
Feature fetch 10-20 ms KV store, batched multi-get, caching
Retrieval (ANN, several sources) 20-30 ms HNSW / IVF-PQ, parallel fan-out
Filtering 5 ms Bloom filters for already-seen items
Ranking ~500 candidates 30-60 ms GPU batching; compression: quantization, pruning, distillation, factorization [1]
Re-rank / policy 5-10 ms Rule engine, MMR diversity
Slack / network 50 ms Timeout falls back to cached or popular results
Mode choice batch / online / hybrid / on-device [1] Precompute for stable users, online for context; on-device when memory, compute, energy or privacy dominate [1]

Monitoring

Layer What to watch Action
System QPS, p99 latency, errors, GPU utilization Autoscale, alert
Data Missing or null features, schema changes, feature drift (PSI/KL) Data validation gate [29]
Model Prediction distribution, calibration, online AUC once labels arrive Roll back to the previous registry version
Business Primary KPI, guardrails, per-slice metrics Experiment review
Retraining Scheduled (daily/weekly) or triggered by drift Continual training [1]

Failure modes

Failure Symptom Mitigation
Training-serving skew Offline AUC up, online flat Log features at serve time, share transform code [31]
Feedback loop Popular items get more popular Exploration slot, debiasing [30]
Label leakage Offline metrics too good Point-in-time joins, time-based splits
Cold start New users or items get no exposure Content features, popularity priors, explore
Data drift / seasonality Gradual metric decay Drift alerts, frequent retraining
Stale features / pipeline outage Sudden drop in metrics Freshness SLAs, default values, fallback model
Optimizing a proxy CTR up, satisfaction down (clickbait) Multi-objective value model, guardrails
Latency blow-up Timeouts at peak Candidate caps, distillation, fallbacks

Interviewer follow-ups (reported or likely across portals)

  • Why ML at all? What heuristic baseline would you launch first? [31]
  • How exactly do you turn the business goal into a training label and loss? [1][15]
  • Which offline metric correlates with your online metric, and what if they disagree?
  • How do you build negatives, and how do you handle class imbalance?
  • How do you avoid data leakage when you join labels and features?
  • How do you handle position bias and the feedback loop created by your own recommendations?
  • Cold start for new users and new items?
  • Walk through the latency budget. What do you cut if p99 doubles?
  • Batch vs online prediction: which features are precomputed and which are real-time?
  • How do you design the A/B test? Which guardrails? How long do you run it? [8]
  • How do you detect performance drift after deployment, and when do you retrain? [8]
  • How would the design change at 10x scale, or on-device?
  • The model is too big for the latency or device budget: quantize, prune, distill or factorize? [1]
  • Which predictions are batch-precomputed, which online, and why not hybrid? [1]
  • Real labels are scarce: weak supervision, transfer learning or active learning? [1]
  • Fairness, privacy and policy constraints: where do they enter the pipeline?
  • What would you build next with another quarter?
  • (GenAI rounds) How would the design change if an LLM generates the output? [14]

Portal comparison

Portal / resource Steps Signature emphasis Format Notes
ByteByteGo, Aminian & Xu (2023) [15] 7 Problem -> ML task framing; 10 case studies with 211 diagrams Book + online course Blind reviewers call the framework decent but some find it shallow [25]
alirezadir AIMLInterviews [1][2] 9 Most granular checklist; MVP architecture as its own step; bandits, shadow and canary rollouts Free GitHub Updated for GenAI and agentic design in 2026 [2]
Educative Grokking MLSD [5] 6 Clarify -> data strategy -> model -> offline/online eval -> deploy -> monitor; fraud detection as the running example Paid course, mock interviews Separate Khang Pham course: feed, ads, Airbnb search [6][17]
Exponent / Aced [3][4] 6 Treats the interview as "convincing the team to launch"; rubric module Course + video mocks Time budgets per step (~8 min to define the problem) [3]
Hello Interview [7] 5-6 Timed delivery; problem framing 5-7 min; deep dives driven by the interviewer Free guide + paid mocks Steps are guideposts, not hard rules [7]
Chip Huyen [18][19][21] 4 Project setup -> data -> modeling -> serving; 27 open questions; production MLOps depth Free booklet, O'Reilly book, Stanford CS 329S The ml-interviews-book points to a separate resource for design [19]
Patrick Halina [23] ~5 Compact; heavy stress on clarifying first Free blog Blind calls it one of the best compact resources [24]
Babushkin & Kravchenko (Manning, 2025) [22] 16 chapters Design-doc-driven: problem -> research -> loss/metrics -> baseline -> error analysis Book Closer to real industry design docs than interview scripts

02. Design a Video Recommendation System (YouTube Home Feed)

Prompt as usually given: "Design the ML system that fills the YouTube home page with personalized videos for each logged-in user." Variants: "watch next", Reels/Shorts/TikTok short-video feed, Netflix-style rows.

Company tags

Company (reported) Where it was reported Notes
Google / YouTube interviewing.io mock [6], Blind [13] ML SWE loop; follow-ups on RNN serving throughput and monitoring [13]
Meta Blind [12][14], LeetCode Discuss [15], Hello Interview community [8] Rec/ranking is the standard Meta ML-design round; Reels/TikTok-style variant [8]
Coupang 1point3acres [16] "YouTube recommendation, from metrics to pipeline"
TikTok / ByteDance Codemia [17], Hello Interview [8], Jointaro [27] Short-video variant; real-time training (Monolith) [24]
Netflix-style variant (practice framing, not a reported loop) Chip Huyen exercises [29], AIMLInterviews [10] Rows/titles; "when does a user stop watching a show"

Portals that cover it

Portal Treatment Link
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu, MLSDI ch. 6) Full chapter, hybrid filtering, multi-source candidate gen; newsletter deep dive [1][2]
Educative "Grokking the ML System Design Interview" 5-lesson case study (framing, data, retrieval, ranking, serving) [3][4][5]
interviewing.io Google mock, 2B users / 10B videos / < 1 s [6]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Surface Home page, logged-in user, no query [1][10]
Business goal Engagement (watch time, completed views) + satisfaction (likes, surveys) [1][20][22]
Relevance label Explicit like OR watched >= ~50% of video [10]
Users 2B users (interviewing.io); 100M DAU (AIMLInterviews) [6][10]
Catalog 10B videos (interviewing.io); 100M (AIMLInterviews); "tens of millions" in YouTube retrieval paper [6][10][21]
End-to-end latency ~200 ms (AIMLInterviews); < 1 s (interviewing.io) [10][6]
Retrieval budget < 10 ms over > 1B videos to a few hundred [4]
Peak QPS ~2B DAU x ~10 home loads/day / 86,400 x 3 peak ~ 700k QPS typical assumption
Candidates per stage ~1e9 -> ~1e3 (retrieval) -> ~1e2 (ranking) -> ~20-50 shown [19] + typical
Signals "> 80 billion signals" (YouTube) [23]
Freshness New uploads recommendable within minutes-hours typical assumption
Non-functional Diversity, safety/policy, cold start, multilingual, fairness [10][7]

Latency budget (target p99 ~200 ms server-side) [10]

Step Budget Notes
Gateway + feature fetch 15-25 ms Online KV store, batched multi-get
Candidate generation 10-30 ms Parallel sources; ANN < 10 ms [4]
Filtering ~5 ms Bloom filter of watched ids
Light ranker 10-20 ms ~1k items, CPU
Heavy ranker 40-80 ms ~200 items, GPU/TPU batched
Re-rank + policy ~10 ms Greedy diversification
Logging async Never on critical path

Diagram 3 - Model architecture

Figure 2.3a - Retrieval: two-tower with sampled softmax (logQ correction) [19][21]

        USER / QUERY TOWER                         VIDEO TOWER
 +-----------------------------------+   +-----------------------------------+
 | watch history ids -> emb -> avg   |   | video_id emb                      |
 |   or seq. encoder (last ~50)      |   | channel_id emb, topic/tags emb    |
 | search tokens -> emb -> avg       |   | title text emb (BERT, frozen)     |
 | geo, lang, device, gender, age    |   | duration, upload age, language    |
 | example_age (0 at serve time)     |   | popularity counters (log)         |
 +-----------------+-----------------+   +-----------------+-----------------+
                   v                                       v
          +-----------------+                     +-----------------+
          | MLP ReLU 1024-> |                     | MLP ReLU 1024-> |
          | 512 -> 256      |                     | 512 -> 256      |
          +--------+--------+                     +--------+--------+
                   | u (256-d, L2 norm)                    | v_i (256-d)
                   +------------------+--------------------+
                                      v
                        +----------------------------+
                        | s(u,v_i) = <u, v_i> / tau  |
                        | in-batch softmax, subtract |
                        | log q(i) (sampling prob.)  |
                        +-------------+--------------+
                                      v
             TRAIN: cross-entropy vs next watched video (positives)
             SERVE: v_i precomputed -> ANN index; u computed per request

Figure 2.3b - Ranking: multi-task MMoE + shallow position-bias tower [20]

 inputs: user feats | video feats | user x video cross | context (time,
         device); ids -> embeddings, counts -> log/normalize
                                |
        +---------------+-------+-------+---------------+
        v               v               v               v
 +------------+  +------------+  +------------+  +------------+
 | Expert 1   |  | Expert 2   |  | Expert 3   |  | Expert N   |   shared MLP experts
 +------------+  +------------+  +------------+  +------------+
        |               |               |               |
        +---------------+-------+-------+---------------+
                                |   all expert outputs go to every gate
        +---------------+-------+-------+---------------+
        v               v               v               v
 +------------+  +------------+  +------------+  +------------+
 | gate_click |  | gate_watch |  | gate_like  |  | gate_neg   |   softmax over experts
 +------------+  +------------+  +------------+  +------------+
        |               |               |               |
 +------------+  +------------+  +------------+  +------------+
 | tower+head |  | tower+head |  | tower+head |  | tower+head |   per-task MLP tower
 | P(click)   |  | E[watch]   |  | P(like/shr)|  | P(dismiss) |
 | sigmoid    |  | wLR / reg. |  | sigmoid    |  | sigmoid    |
 +------------+  +------------+  +------------+  +------------+
        |               |               |               |
       (+)<-+          (+)<-+           |               |   engagement heads get
        |   |           |   |           |               |   a position-bias logit
        |   +-----------|---+-----------|---------------|---< SHALLOW TOWER
        |               |               |               |   (position, device);
        |               |               |               |   train only, dropped
        |               |               |               |   at serving
        +---------------+-------+-------+---------------+
                                v
 final score = w1*P(click) + w2*E[watch] + w3*P(like) - w4*P(dismiss)
 (weights w_k tuned by online A/B, not by offline loss)

Diagram 4 - Real system: YouTube (2016 -> 2019) vs. ByteByteGo textbook

Figure 2.4 - How the reference solutions map to YouTube's published system [19][20][21][25]

 YouTube 2016 (Covington et al.) [19]        YouTube 2019 additions [20][21]
 +-----------------------------------+       +-----------------------------------+
 | Candidate gen = extreme multiclass|       | Retrieval = two-tower ("NDR"),    |
 | softmax over millions of videos;  | ----> | streaming item-frequency estimate |
 | serve with nearest-neighbour      |       | -> logQ-corrected in-batch softmax|
 +-----------------+-----------------+       +-----------------+-----------------+
                   v                                           v
 +-----------------------------------+       +-----------------------------------+
 | Ranking = weighted logistic regr. | ----> | Ranking = MMoE multi-task         |
 | positives weighted by watch time  |       | (engagement + satisfaction) +     |
 | -> odds ~ expected watch time     |       | shallow tower for position bias   |
 +-----------------------------------+       +-----------------------------------+

 ByteByteGo / AIMLInterviews textbook answer [1][10]
 +-------------+   +--------------+   +-------------+   +--------------+
 | CandGen x N | ->| Scoring      | ->| Re-ranking  | ->| Home feed    |
 | two-tower,  |   | heavier model|   | region/age, |   | (top-k)      |
 | popular,    |   | (DNN / DCN)  |   | fresh, dedup|   |              |
 | trending    |   | more feats   |   | clickbait   |   |              |
 +-------------+   +--------------+   +-------------+   +--------------+

 Short-video variant (TikTok / Monolith) [24]: same funnel, but ONLINE training
 (minutes) + collisionless hash embedding tables; watch completion dominates.

Production details most portals omit

Detail (YouTube) Why it matters in the interview Source
Train candidate gen on all watches, incl. embedded/off-surface plays, not only rec impressions Surfaces new content; avoids learning only from the recommender's own exposure [19]
Fixed number of training examples per user Stops heavy users dominating the loss [19]
Predict the next watch from past history (no future context), not a random held-out watch Avoids label leakage; matches asymmetric co-watch behaviour [19]
example_age feature, set to 0 at serving Lets the model learn the freshness preference instead of stale averages [19]
Streaming item-frequency estimation (hashed arrays) feeding logQ In-batch negatives over-penalise popular items without it [21]
Ranker trained continuously on streaming logs; shallow tower for selection/position bias Implicit feedback is biased by what was shown and where [20]
User surveys ("valued watch time"), borderline-content demotion Watch time alone is not satisfaction; responsibility guardrail [22]

Data & labels

Label / signal Definition Use Pitfall
Click Impression -> play Ranker head Clickbait; position bias
Watch time Seconds watched (or fraction) Ranker head; wLR weight [19] Biased toward long videos
Completed / >50% watched Binary relevance Retrieval + ranker positive [10] Short videos inflate
Like / share / subscribe Explicit positive Satisfaction head Sparse
Dismiss / "not interested" / dislike Explicit negative Negative head Sparse, high value
Survey ("was this worth your time?") Satisfaction Satisfaction head [22] Very sparse, needs weighting
Implicit negative Shown, not clicked Ranker negatives Not a true negative [9]
Random negatives Sampled from corpus Retrieval negatives Needs logQ correction [21]

Features

Group Examples Encoding
User id, age, gender, geo, language, device Embeddings / one-hot / bucketize [10]
User history last N watched ids, search tokens, liked channels Avg pooling or sequence model (Transformer/GRU)
Video id, channel, topic, tags, duration, upload age, language Embeddings; BERT for title/desc; CBOW for tags [10]
Video content frame / audio embeddings Pretrained encoders (cold start)
Video stats views, CTR, avg watch % (1h/1d/7d windows) log-normalize; streaming counters
Cross user watched this channel?, #times this video shown to user, time since last watch of channel Numeric; strongest ranking features [19]
Context time of day, day of week, device, network One-hot / embeddings
Freshness example_age (training), 0 at serving Numeric [19]

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Baseline Better Advanced Tradeoff
Retrieval Popular/trending by region Matrix factorization (WALS) Two-tower DNN + ANN [1][10] MF: fast, no side features, cold start fails; two-tower: features, cold-start users, costlier [10]
Retrieval (alt) Item-item co-watch Graph / sequence (next-video) Generative/semantic-ID retrieval Coverage vs. freshness
Ranking Logistic regression / GBDT Wide & Deep, DCN [5] MMoE / PLE multi-task [20] Capacity vs latency; negative transfer between tasks
Re-rank Rules (dedup, caps) MMR diversity Slate/RL optimization, bandit explore Engagement vs. diversity
Cold start Popular in locale Content-tower embeddings Explore budget / bandits [10] Short-term loss vs. learning

Loss functions

Model Loss
Two-tower retrieval Sampled / in-batch softmax CE with logQ correction [21]; alternative: BCE with random negatives
2016 candidate gen Sampled softmax over millions of classes (+ importance weighting) [19]
2016 ranker Weighted logistic regression (positives weighted by watch time) [19]
Multi-task ranker Sum_k lambda_k * L_k: BCE for click/like/dismiss, regression or wLR for watch time [20]
Position bias Shallow tower logit added in training, removed at serving [20]

Offline metrics

Stage Metric
Retrieval Recall@k (k=100..1000), hit rate of next watch, coverage
Ranking AUC / log-loss per head, nDCG@k, mAP, Precision@k [9][10]
List Diversity (intra-list distance), novelty, freshness share
Slices New users, new videos, languages, regions, devices
Counterfactual IPS / off-policy estimates on logged random traffic

Online metrics / A-B

Type Metric
Primary Total watch time per user/day, # completed videos [10]
Engagement CTR, sessions/day, session length
Satisfaction Likes, survey score, dismiss rate, dislikes (guardrail) [20][22]
Long-term D7/D28 retention, return visits (holdouts for weeks)
Guardrails Latency p99, borderline/harmful exposure, creator diversity
Method User-randomized A/B, interleaving for rankers, long-term holdbacks

Monitoring

What How
Feature drift / missing features Per-feature null rate, PSI vs. training distribution
Train/serve skew Log served features; compare to offline recompute
Prediction calibration Predicted vs. observed CTR per bucket and slice
Business KPIs Watch time, CTR, dismiss rate dashboards with alerting
Index freshness Age of ANN index, % of new uploads retrievable
Infra QPS, p50/p99 latency per stage, timeouts -> fallback to cache/popular

Failure modes

Failure Symptom Mitigation
Clickbait CTR up, watch time / satisfaction down Optimize watch + satisfaction, not clicks [1][10]
Feedback loop / filter bubble Narrowing topics, popularity bias Explore slots, diversity re-rank, logQ correction [21]
Position bias Top slots over-learned Shallow bias tower [20], randomization data
Cold start (new video) Never surfaced Content embeddings, fresh-upload candidate source, explore
Cold start (new user) Generic feed Demographic/context features in user tower, onboarding topics
Long-video bias Watch-time objective favors long videos Normalize by duration, completion-rate labels [10]
Stale model Trends missed Hourly warm-start / online training [24]
Harmful/borderline content Policy risk Classifier demotion in re-rank stage [10][22]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why not just optimize CTR? What happens to clickbait, and how do you define "relevant"? [1][10]
  • Watch time vs. completion vs. satisfaction: how do you combine heads into one score, and who sets the weights? [20]
  • Matrix factorization vs. two-tower: when is MF enough? How does each handle new users? [10]
  • How do you choose negatives for the two-tower, and why is in-batch sampling biased? [21]
  • Why hold out the next watch instead of a random watch, and why cap examples per user? [19]
  • How do you serve retrieval in < 10 ms over 1B videos (ANN choice, sharding, index refresh)? [4]
  • How do you handle cold start for a video uploaded 5 minutes ago? [10][18]
  • How do you correct for position and selection bias in logged training data? [20]
  • How would you optimize prediction throughput if the user model is an RNN/Transformer? [13]
  • How do you monitor the system and detect a silent quality regression? [13]
  • How do you ensure diversity and avoid filter bubbles without hurting watch time?
  • Offline AUC went up but online watch time went down - why? (skew, proxy-metric mismatch)
  • How fresh does the model need to be? Batch daily vs. hourly vs. online training [24]
  • Videos vs. ads on the same surface: how would scope change the design? [12]
  • How do you evaluate long-term effects (retention) vs. short-term A/B wins?
  • How would you adapt this to Shorts/Reels/TikTok (no click, swipe-based feedback)? [8][30]

Portal comparison

Portal Objective / label Candidate generation Ranking Distinctive emphasis
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu) [1] Relevance = like or partial watch; warns against pure clicks Multiple sources incl. two-tower, popular, trending Heavier model on fewer candidates Clean 3-stage funnel, MF vs. two-tower tradeoff
AIMLInterviews (alirezadir) [10] Like or >=50% watched CF two-tower chosen over MF; popularity + trending FFN or DCN; multi-task option Free; detailed feature encoding table, re-rank rules
Educative Grokking [3][4][5] Engagement vs. satisfaction conflict Two-tower + contrastive negatives + ANN (<10 ms, >1B videos) Wide & Deep / DCN, re-ranking lesson Retrieval latency/recall/index-freshness tradeoffs
interviewing.io (Google mock) [6] Maximize engagement Two-stage, 2B users / 10B videos Ranking stage within < 1 s Real interviewer pressure, scale reasoning
Hello Interview [7][8] Watch time vs. satisfaction Retrieval stage, CF vs. content, embeddings Two-stage pattern Pattern-based reuse across rec problems; TikTok variant
YouTube papers [19][20][21] Expected watch time -> multi-objective Softmax -> two-tower w/ logQ wLR -> MMoE + bias tower The production ground truth all portals mirror

03. Design a Short-Video Feed (TikTok For You / Instagram Reels / YouTube Shorts) with Real-Time Signals

Company Evidence Ref

YouTube / Google (Shorts) Indicative only: YouTube video rec is the canonical prompt in prep repos, and the reference designs are Google papers; no first-hand Shorts interview report found [6] [7] [21] [22]

Requirements & scale

Category Requirement Source / note
Functional Infinite vertical feed, one full-screen video at a time, autoplay; next video personalised instantly from in-session actions [13] [17]
Functional Signals: watch time / completion, replay, like, share, comment, follow, skip, "not interested" [3] [4]
Functional Diversity: no two consecutive videos with same sound or creator; integrity filtering [3] [4]
Functional Cold start: new users (onboarding, device/locale priors) and new videos (small-audience exploration pools) [16] [19]
Non-functional p99 serving latency < 50-100 ms for ranking [17] [16] (typical)
Non-functional Freshness: model reacts to new interactions in minutes (online training) [1]
Scale ~1B DAU; feed requests ~millions/s; ~1T views/day [16] [19] (prep-site assumptions)
Scale Corpus: 100M to billions of videos; tens of millions eligible for retrieval [8] [21] (typical)
Funnel sizes Retrieval ~1e4 -> light rank ~1e3 -> heavy rank ~100-500 -> serve ~10 per page [4] [6] (typical)
Out of scope Upload/transcoding/CDN (classic SD), ads auction, monetization [17]

Other real systems to name-drop: Instagram Explore/Reels 4-stage funnel (retrieval -> first-stage ranking -> second-stage MTML ranking -> final re-ranking) with two-tower + caching [4]; Facebook Reels UTIS survey-alignment model feeding both retrieval and late ranking [5]; Kuaishou TWIN lifelong-sequence ranker [9], D2Q duration-debiased watch time [10], on-device re-ranking [12]; Meta HSTU generative recommender [11].

Often missed (vs. real systems)

Item Why it matters Ref
Upload-time content understanding (multimodal emb, near-dup / re-upload detection, safety classifiers) Makes a new video rankable before it has interactions; blocks harmful items pre-ranking [3] [27]
New-video traffic pool (staged exposure, promote on early engagement) Item cold start and creator fairness; gated by early finish/like rates [3] [16]
On-device re-ranking of the prefetched page Reacts to a skip within the same page without a server round trip [12]
Survey / satisfaction model as an extra objective Counters watch-time-only optimisation; used in retrieval and late ranking [5]
Lifelong user sequence (GSU/ESU, TWIN) Long-term interests beyond last 50-100 items within latency [9]
Value-model weight tuning by online experiments Head weights are product decisions, not learned end-to-end [4] [7]
Fault tolerance of online training (PS snapshots, rollback) Monolith reports daily PS snapshots suffice despite real-time updates [1]

Data & labels

Label Definition Notes
Watch time ms watched (capped, incl. replays) Biased toward long videos -> duration-quantile (D2Q) or watch_ratio [10]
Completion / "effective view" watched >= X% or >= N s recsysml: count of videos watched > ~10 s ~ watch time for short videos [17]
Skip swiped away < 1-3 s Strong, dense negative; short-video equivalent of non-click
Like / share / comment / follow binary per impression Sparse; shares weighted heavily (Reels) [4]
Negative feedback "not interested", report, hide Counter-metric and hard-negative label [21]
Survey "how well does this match your interests" 1-5 Debiased; aligns to true interest [5]
Retrieval positives engaged (finish or like) items; negatives = in-batch + random log-Q correction for popularity [8]

Features

Group Examples Freshness
User static id emb, locale, language, device, age bucket daily
User sequence last 50-100 watched ids + watch ratio; lifelong (1e4-1e6) via GSU/ESU search [9] real-time / daily
Session (real-time) videos this session, skips in last 5, current topic streak, dwell seconds
Video content multimodal emb (frames, audio, ASR, caption, hashtags, sound id) at upload
Video stats CTR/finish rate 1h/24h/7d, age since upload, duration minutes (stream)
Creator creator emb, follower count, user-creator affinity hourly
Context hour, weekday, network type, position in session request time
Cross user-topic affinity, user-sound affinity, two-tower score request time

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
Retrieval Popularity + item-item CF Two-tower ANN (log-Q), multi-source; transformer seq retriever Recall vs. freshness of item index
Light ranking Logistic regression on counters Distilled small DNN / two-tower dot Latency on ~5k items
Heavy ranking GBDT on hand features MMoE/PLE multi-task DNN + DCN + target attention over long seq [7] [9] Accuracy vs. GPU cost
Watch-time head Weighted logistic (YouTube 2016) [6] D2Q quantile / tree-based progressive regression [10] [28] Duration bias handling
Freshness Daily batch retrain Online training, minute-level sparse sync [1] Stability vs. reactivity
Next-gen Separate stages Generative recommender (HSTU) over action sequence [11] Compute; infra maturity

Loss

Component Loss
Retrieval Sampled softmax / in-batch softmax with log-Q correction [8]
Binary heads (finish, like, share, follow, skip) BCE per head, sum_i lambda_i * L_i (task weights tuned / uncertainty-weighted)
Watch time Weighted logistic (watch-time-weighted positives) [6] or regression on duration-conditioned quantile [10]
Position / autoplay bias Shallow bias tower added during training only [7]
Survey alignment Calibrated regression on debiased survey score [5]

Offline metrics

Stage Metric
Retrieval Recall@K, hit rate@K on next-watched videos
Ranking heads AUC / GAUC (per-user), normalized entropy, calibration (pred/actual)
Watch time MAE / XAUC on watch time, per-duration-bucket
List nDCG@K, diversity (unique creators/topics per 10), coverage of new videos
Slices new users, new videos, low-activity regions, long vs short videos

Online metrics / A-B

Type Metrics
North star Total watch time / DAU, retention (D1/D7), sessions per user
Engagement Effective views, finish rate, likes/shares/comments per view, follows
Session Session length, session success rate [17]
Guardrails Skip rate, "not interested"/reports, integrity violations, creator diversity, new-creator exposure, latency/QPS
Long-term Holdouts (weeks) for retention; survey-based satisfaction [5]
Method User-level randomisation; watch for network effects on creators; interleaving for ranking sensitivity

Serving & latency budget (typical, p99 ~100 ms)

Step Budget Technique
Feature fetch (user + session) 10 ms online KV (Redis-like), co-located cache
Retrieval (parallel sources) 15 ms HNSW/ScaNN ANN, precomputed item emb
Filtering 5 ms Bloom filter of seen ids, policy flags
Light ranking ~5k 10 ms CPU small DNN, precomputed item side
Heavy ranking ~500 35 ms GPU batch inference, item-feature cache, fp16/int8
Re-rank + response 10 ms rules + diversity (MMR/DPP)
Prefetch n/a return 8-10 videos; client prefetches next page while user watches

Monitoring

What Signal
Data Event lag in Kafka, joiner drop rate, feature null rate, train/serve feature skew
Model Per-head calibration, AUC drift on fresh traffic, embedding norm explosions in online training
Business Watch time, skip rate, report rate by region, creator concentration (Gini)
System p50/p99 latency per stage, PS sync delay, ANN index age, GPU utilisation

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Filter bubble / feedback loop Explore slots, diversity re-rank, creator/sound dedup [3], survey alignment [5]
Clickbait / long-video bias in watch time Multi-objective value model, D2Q debiasing [10]
Item cold start (new uploads) Content emb in item tower, fresh-upload pool with traffic boosting, bandits
User cold start Onboarding interests, locale/device priors, popular-in-region
Online training instability (bad batch, bot traffic) Anomaly filters, rollback to last good checkpoint, dense sync slower than sparse [1]
Embedding table blow-up Frequency filtering + expiring embeddings [1]
Train/serve skew Log features at serving time and join (Fig 3.2)
Viral spike / hot item Item-feature cache, real-time counters, rate-limit boosting
Harmful content amplification Integrity filter before ranking + post-rank policy layer [4]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you define "engagement" for a feed with no clicks (autoplay)? Watch time vs. completion vs. effective views? [17]
  • How do you remove duration bias from watch-time labels? [10]
  • How would the next video change based on a skip that happened 2 seconds ago (session features vs. online training vs. on-device re-rank)? [1] [12]
  • How do you combine 5+ predicted objectives into one score, and how do you tune the weights? [4] [7]
  • Walk through two-tower training: negatives, popularity bias, log-Q correction, index refresh cadence. [8] [23]
  • How do you handle cold start for new users and for a creator's first video? [16] [19]
  • How do you avoid filter bubbles and ensure creator diversity? [3]
  • How would you model a user's lifelong history (10^5+ items) within latency? [9]
  • What happens if the online trainer ingests bot traffic or a corrupted batch? [1]
  • How do you detect and fix training/serving skew?
  • Offline metrics improved but online watch time dropped: what do you check?
  • How would you measure long-term satisfaction rather than short-term engagement? [5]
  • How do you scale to ~1B users / millions of QPS; what is cached? [16] [20]
  • Concept/data drift: how do you monitor and when do you retrain? [20]
  • (Meta variant) Optimise for comments instead of watch time: what changes? [14]
  • How do you treat re-uploads / near-duplicates and creator originality in ranking? [3]
  • Would you re-rank on the device, and what model and features fit there? [12]
  • How do you give a new video its first few hundred impressions, and when do you stop? [3] [16]

04. Design a Personalized News Feed Ranking System (Facebook / LinkedIn / Twitter Home Timeline)

Prompt as usually given: "When a user opens the app, rank the unseen posts from friends, follows, groups and recommended sources so the feed maximizes meaningful engagement." Variants: Twitter/X "For You" timeline, LinkedIn homepage feed, Instagram feed, comment ranking under a post, "compare ranking objectives for a feed".

Company tags

Company (reported) Where it was reported Notes
Meta IGotAnOffer Meta MLE guide [25], Prepfully Meta MLE bank [26], PracHub "comment ranking for a news feed" [14], Blind [28] Feed / ranking is the standard Meta ML-design round; comment-ranking variant balances engagement, spam/toxicity and freshness [14]
LinkedIn PracHub "personalized feed + compare ranking objectives" [13] Follow-up: pointwise vs. pairwise vs. listwise LTR [13]; Khang Pham uses "LinkedIn Feed Ranking" as a case study [7][6]
Twitter / X (case study, not a verified interview tag) Educative "Feed Based System" uses the Twitter feed as its worked example [3]; Khang Pham repo lists "Twitter timeline ranking" as reading under Adtech, linking [21] [7] Use as the real-system reference (Figure 4.4), not as evidence that X asks this question
Generic FAANG / big tech Exponent question bank [2], AlgoMaster [10], techinterview.org [11], Analytics Vidhya 2026 [12] Exponent page is a question listing; company tag details were not retrievable in this run

Portals that cover it

Portal Treatment Link
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu, MLSDI ch. 10 "Personalized News Feed") Full chapter; ads between posts, engagement goal; click/like/comment/hide/block actions [1]
Educative "Grokking the ML Interview" (Feed Based System, Twitter) 9 lessons: metrics, architecture, tweet selection, features, training data, ranking, diversity, online experiments [3]

Educative / Khang Pham "Machine Learning System Design" Feed Ranking System Design lesson (LinkedIn-style) [6][7]
alirezadir AIMLInterviews (GitHub) Free full write-up: 2B DAU, 200 ms, multi-task NN, dwell + skip heads [8][9]
Exponent "Design personalized news ranking system" question [2]
AlgoMaster, techinterview.org, Analytics Vidhya, PracHub Guides and reported prompts [10][11][12][13][14]
Hello Interview Recsys pattern page (applies directly) [27]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Surface Home feed on app open / refresh; no query; user_id + context in [1][9]
Timelines served X home-mixer serves For You (ranked) plus Following and Lists (reverse-chron) [18]
Business goal Maximize engagement (ads are interleaved, so engagement -> revenue) [1][9]
Output Ranked list of unseen posts from friends/follows + recommended sources [9][3]
Users 5B total, 2B DAU, ~2 refreshes/user/day (AIMLInterviews); Meta "more than 2B" users [9][15]
Avg / peak QPS 2B x 2 / 86,400 ~ 46k avg; x3 peak ~ 140k QPS typical assumption from [9]
Candidate inventory Hundreds of millions of posts; LinkedIn retrieves ~2,000 from hundreds of millions [22]
Candidates per stage ~1e8 pool -> ~1-2k retrieved -> ~500 light-ranked -> ~50 shown per page [22][33] + typical
End-to-end latency 200 ms (AIMLInterviews); 100-200 ms (PracHub); < 200 ms (techinterview.org) [9][14][11]
Features ~6,000 features hydrated per candidate in Twitter home-mixer [18]
Freshness New posts visible within seconds-minutes; engagement counters streamed [9] + typical
Non-functional Integrity/safety filters, diversity, creator fairness, privacy, cold start [9][11][5]

Figure 4.3 - Shared-bottom multi-task ranker with per-action heads

 INPUTS (per user, post candidate)

 | User        | | Author      | | Post        | | User-author  | | Context     |
 | id emb,     | | id emb,     | | text emb    | | affinity,    | | device,     |

 | history agg | | health      | | emb (CLIP), | | P(interact), | | position,   |
 |             | |             | | age, counts | | 2-hop feats  | | network     |
 +------+------+ +------+------+ +------+------+ +------+-------+ +------+------+
        +---------------+---------------+---------------+----------------+
                                        | concat (sparse emb + dense)
                                        v
                     +-----------------------------------------+
                     | FEATURE INTERACTION / SHARED LAYERS     |
                     | DCNv2 / MaskNet / transformer blocks    |
                     +--------------------+--------------------+
                                          | shared representation
     +-------------+------------+---------+---+-------------+-------------+
     v             v            v             v             v             v
 +--------+   +--------+   +---------+   +--------+   +----------+   +---------+
 |P(click)|   |P(like) |   |P(cmnt)  |   |P(share)|   |P(hide /  |   |E[dwell] |
 |sigmoid |   |sigmoid |   |sigmoid  |   |sigmoid |   | report)  |   |regress. |
 +---+----+   +---+----+   +----+----+   +---+----+   +----+-----+   +----+----+
     +------------+-------------+------------+-------------+--------------+
                                          | calibrated probabilities
                                          v
                     +-----------------------------------------+

Table 4.1 - X Heavy Ranker heads and value-model weights (Apr 5, 2023) [19]

Head (predicted P) Weight Head (predicted P) Weight
reply_engaged_by_author +75.0 retweet +1.0
reply +13.5 fav (like) +0.5
good_profile_click +12.0 video_playback50 +0.005
good_click +11.0 negative_feedback_v2 -74.0
good_click_v2 +10.0 report -369.0

In-network candidates (~50% of the feed) come from the Earlybird search index with its own light ranker [17]; TwHIN supplies three 200-d embeddings and aggregates use 50-day and short-term windows [20].

Data & labels

Signal Type Label use Note
Click / expand Implicit, abundant P(click) head Noisy; clickbait risk [1]
Like / react Explicit P(like) Weight: share > comment > like > click [9]
Comment / reply Explicit, sparse P(comment) Strong "meaningful interaction" signal [15][19]
Share / retweet Explicit, sparse P(share) Virality
Dwell time Implicit Regression head Covers passive users [9]
Skip (dwell < t) Implicit negative P(skip) Passive-user negative [9]
Hide / block / report Explicit negative Negative-weight heads Twitter report weight -369 [19]
Non-engaged impression Negative All heads = 0 Downsample; imbalance [9]
Surveys ("worth your time?") Explicit Eval / auxiliary Satisfaction metric [9]

Features

Group Examples Freshness
User id embedding, demographics, locale, history aggregates (CTR, likes) daily batch
Post content text embedding (BERT), image/video embedding (CLIP/SimCLR), hashtags, age, media type at post time
Post engagement like/comment/share counts and velocity (30 min, 1 day) streaming
Author follower count, author health/quality, posting rate daily
User-author affinity connection type, past reactions, real-graph P(interact), 2-hop batch + stream
Graph / embeddings SimClusters, TwHIN, two-tower embeddings daily
Context device, time of day, day of week, network, position request time

Sources: [9][20][15].

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
Retrieval Reverse-chron in-network + rules Two-tower ANN, graph walks, LLM dual encoder (LinkedIn LLaMA-3 retrieval, ~2k from 100s of M) [22] Recall vs. infra cost
Light ranker Logistic regression Small DNN / GBDT Cheap pre-filter of ~1k
Heavy ranker Independent per-action LR / GBDT Shared-bottom multi-task DNN; DCNv2, MaskNet, transformer (LinkedIn Feed-SR) [19][22] Accuracy vs. GPU cost
Objective Single P(click) Multi-task + value model weights Avoids clickbait; weights become a product lever
LTR Pointwise Pairwise / listwise (LinkedIn follow-up) [13][8] Pointwise simplest; listwise better ordering
Re-rank Hard rules Diversity-aware (MMR/DPP), integrity demotion Engagement vs. diversity

Loss

Head Loss Note
Binary actions Binary cross-entropy Sum over tasks, optional task weights [9]
Dwell time MAE / MSE / Huber Huber robust to long tails [9]
Calibration Post-hoc isotonic / Platt Needed because value model sums probabilities
Imbalance Negative downsampling + log-odds correction Recalibrate after sampling

Offline metrics

Metric What it checks Source
ROC-AUC per task Discrimination per head [9]
Normalized cross-entropy / log loss Calibrated probability quality typical
nDCG@10, mAP, MRR Ranking quality of value-model order [8][11]
Calibration (pred / actual) Value-model correctness typical
Slice metrics New users, new creators, regions [5]

Online metrics / A-B

Type Metrics Source
Primary Time spent, sessions/DAU, meaningful interactions (comments, shares) [9][22]
Secondary CTR, like/comment/share rates [8][9]
Counter / guardrail Hide, report, unfollow rates; ad revenue; latency [8][5]
Satisfaction In-app surveys [9]
Fast comparison Interleaving of rankers [5]
Reported wins LinkedIn Feed-SR +2.10% time spent; LiRank +0.5% member sessions [22]

Serving & latency budget (200 ms p99 target [9])

Step Budget Notes
API, auth, A/B, seen cache 10 ms
Candidate generation (parallel sources) 30 ms ANN + index lookups fan out
Filtering + integrity lookups 10 ms precomputed classifier scores
Feature hydration 30 ms batched KV reads, ~6k features [18]
Light ranker (~1k) 15 ms CPU
Heavy ranker (~500) 50 ms GPU batch inference
Value model + re-rank + ads mix 15 ms
Network / slack 40 ms
Precompute option - Batch-precompute scores for inactive users; online for active ones (batch vs. online prediction tradeoff [8])
Fallback - Reverse-chron in-network feed if the scored pipeline fails (X Conversation Service fallback [18])

Monitoring

What Signal Action
Feature drift PSI/KL on top features, null rates Alert, fallback defaults
Prediction drift Mean predicted vs. observed per head Recalibrate / retrain
Online KPIs CTR, time spent, hide rate by slice Auto-rollback
Freshness Streaming counter lag Page on-call
Integrity Prevalence of violating content in feed Tighten filters
Latency / errors p50/p99 per stage, timeouts Degrade to light ranker

Failure modes

Failure Symptom Mitigation
Clickbait / engagement bait High CTR, low dwell, more hides Multi-task + negative-weight heads [19]
Popular / prolific posters dominate Close friends crowded out Affinity features, author diversity [15][18]
Celebrity / viral posts Fan-out hot spots, repeats Cache, dedup, fatigue rules [9][18]
Cold start (user or post) Generic feed; new posts never shown Onboarding topics, exploration slots [9]
Position bias Top slots over-labelled positive Position feature, set to a fixed value at serving (typical; [9] lists positional bias as a topic only)
Feedback loop / filter bubble Narrowing topics Exploration traffic, out-of-network quota
Data leakage Offline AUC up, online flat Point-in-time feature joins [9]
Catastrophic forgetting Drift after incremental training Replay buffer, periodic full retrain [9]
Integrity misses Harmful content ranks high Filter + demotion before and after ranking; X visibility-filters use hard filters, visible treatments and coarse down-ranking [17]
Ranker timeout / outage Empty or stale feed Serve reverse-chron in-network fallback; degrade to light ranker [18]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why multi-task instead of N separate models? How do you set the value-model weights? [9][19]
  • How would you handle passive users who never like or comment? [9]
  • Pointwise vs. pairwise vs. listwise ranking: which and why? [13][8]
  • How do you keep close friends' posts from being drowned by pages and frequent posters? [15]
  • How do you rank a celebrity post with millions of followers (fan-out, caching)? [9]
  • How do you correct for position bias in training labels?
  • How do you calibrate probabilities after negative downsampling?
  • Design the comment ranking under a post (spam, toxicity, freshness). [14]
  • How do you add out-of-network / recommended content to a follow-based feed? [17][22]
  • What guardrail metrics stop you from shipping an engagement-bait winner? [5]
  • How fresh must features be, and what goes in batch vs. streaming? [9]
  • How do you fit ~500 candidates through a heavy ranker inside 200 ms? [9][18]
  • Cold start for new users and new posts? [9]
  • How would you measure long-term satisfaction rather than short-term clicks? [23]
  • Where do integrity classifiers run, and how do they interact with ranking? [17]
  • What does the feed show if the heavy ranker times out? [18]
  • Why would a reply the author engages with be weighted 150x a like? [19]

Portal comparison

Portal Objective Candidate gen Ranker Distinctive emphasis
ByteByteGo [1] Engagement (ads interleaved) Retrieval of unseen posts Multi-task DNN over reactions Clarifying-questions dialogue; hide/block as negatives
AIMLInterviews [9] Weighted sum of reactions Rule-based unseen posts Multi-task NN + dwell + skip heads Passive users; BERT/CLIP features; 2B DAU / 200 ms
Educative Grokking ML Interview [3] P(engage) on Twitter feed Tweet selection stage Ranking + diversity Training data generation, online experimentation
Educative Grokking MLSD [4][5] Social feed ranking Funnel Multi-stage Guardrails, interleaving, creator equity

05. Design People You May Know (PYMK) / Friend Recommendation (Graph-Based)

Prompt as usually given: "Design the People You May Know feature. Given a user, return a ranked list of other users they are likely to connect with." Variants: Facebook PYMK, LinkedIn PYMK (connection invites), Twitter/X "Who to Follow" (asymmetric follow), Snapchat "Quick Add", Instagram "Suggested for you".

Company tags

Company (reported) Where it was reported Notes
Meta / Facebook alirezadir AIMLInterviews question list: "Friends / follower recommendation: Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn" [2] Symmetric friendship; maximize connections formed [1]
LinkedIn Same list [2]; Kao's write-up frames it "similar to LinkedIn" [6] Production PYMK uses LiGNN embeddings [10]; equity-aware PYMK [13]
Twitter / X Same list [2] Asymmetric "Who to Follow"; open-sourced FRS [7][8], WTF paper [9]
Snap (production, not a reported ask) Snap Research papers on friend-recommendation EBR [11][12] Useful "real system" to cite in the interview

Note: company tags for this problem come mainly from the AIMLInterviews list [2]. Blind, LeetCode and Prepfully pages could not be reached in this run.

Portals that cover it

Portal Treatment Link
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu, MLSDI ch. 11 "People You May Know") Full chapter. Graph edge prediction with a GNN, FoF candidates, batch vs. online prediction [3]
alirezadir AIMLInterviews (GitHub, free) Outline: 1B users, pointwise vs. edge-prediction framing, GNN, FoF, batch precompute [1][2]
shafaypro CrackingMachineLearningInterview (GitHub, free) Deepest free write-up: 5-stage funnel, P(send) x P(accept), leakage, interference, safety [4]
jsheng0901 MLSD notes (GitHub, free) GCN -> GraphSAGE -> GAT progression, negative resampling, weekly batch refresh [5]
M. C. J. Kao "MLSD Interview Extension: PYMK" (Medium, mirrored on GitHub) Serving flowchart, Airflow offline pipeline, ego-cluster A/B testing [6][16]
Khang Pham (Educative / repo), Chip Huyen booklet Checked: no PYMK chapter (LinkedIn feed and generic recsys only) [17][18]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Input / output user_id (+ surface context) -> ranked list of candidate users [1][6]
Business goal Maximize connections formed (accepted, not just sent) [1][4]
Edge type Symmetric friendship (FB/LinkedIn) vs. asymmetric follow (X) [1][4]
Users ~1B total users [1][4]
Degree ~10K connections/user (alirezadir) vs. "few hundred median, long tail of hubs" (shafaypro) [1][4]
DAU 300M DAU (exercise assumption) [4]
Candidate space 1B -> ~1M FoF (1K x 1K) -> ~1-5K after scoring/quotas [1][4]
Serving latency ~50 ms p99 (exercise assumption); rules out request-time graph traversal [4]
Peak QPS 300M DAU x ~3 PYMK views/day / 86,400 ~ 10K avg, ~30K peak typical assumption
Freshness Minutes for new users / big graph events; daily for everyone else [4]
Batch refresh Precompute for active users (last 30 days); refresh daily to weekly [5][6]
Non-functional Privacy (contacts, minors), blocks applied instantly, fallback = hide module [1][4]

  • Graph events (accept, signup, contact upload, block) trigger incremental refresh of the affected users' lists via a stream processor [4].
  • If the store is unavailable, hide the module; never show unfiltered candidates [4].

                    ^                                          |

                    +------------------------------------- user actions
  • Retrain on a schedule (weekly/monthly) or on graph-drift alarms [5].
  • Accepts arrive days late: use a fixed collection window or treat recent rows as censored [4][5].

Figure 5.3 - GNN node encoder + pair scorer with multi-task heads

   viewer u                                         candidate v

 | mean/attn aggr.  |                            | mean/attn aggr.  |
 +--------+---------+                            +---------+--------+

          +----------------------+-------------------------+
                                 |

                                 v

 | Pair feature vector = [h_u, h_v, h_u*h_v,  CN, Adamic-Adar, Jaccard,  |

                                    v
                    +-------------------------------+
                    | Shared MLP tower (ReLU, BN,   |
                    | dropout)                      |

                        |           |           |
                        v           v           v
                 +-----------+ +-----------+ +-----------+
                 | P(send)   | | P(accept  | | P(report /|

                       +------+------+-------------+

        score = P(send) x P(accept|send) x value(edge) - w x P(report)
  • (A) alone is the ByteByteGo / AIMLInterviews answer (GNN edge prediction) [1][3].
  • (B) adds the reciprocity objective (ESMM-style, like CTR x CVR in ads) [4].

  • Snap: EBR improved friendships made in both sparse and dense markets [11]; ANN query expansion gave ~11% relative gain in reciprocated communication, 800M+ MAU [12].

Data & labels

Item Choice Notes / source
Positive (edge model) Edge formed in (t, t+1] that was absent at snapshot t [1][5][6]
Positive (ranker) send on impression; accept given send; edge used within 28 days [4]
Negatives Seen-but-not-sent impressions; hard negatives (FoF not connected) Random pairs teach "rank by degree" [4][5]
Explicit negatives Dismiss, "I don't know this person", ignored/declined, report Separate heavily-weighted head [4]
Resampling Re-sample negatives each epoch, keep class balance [5]
Label window Fixed 14-day accept window, or censor recent sends [4][5]
Split Temporal: train before cutoff, evaluate after Random edge splits overstate quality [4]

Features

Group Examples Source
Neighbourhood overlap Common neighbours (time-discounted), Adamic-Adar, Jaccard, resource allocation [1][4]
Paths / walks Shortest path (cap 3-4), 2/3-hop path counts, PPR both directions [4][9][14]
Degree Degrees, degree ratio, incoming request volume, clustering coefficient [4][5]
Shared context Same school + years overlap, employer, industry, city, groups, contact match [1][5]
Interaction (no edge) Profile views, co-tags, comments on same posts (feature only, never shown) [4]
Embeddings GNN / node2vec cosine, pair score [4][10]
User Account age, activity, accept rate of received requests, device, time [1][5]
Source Which generator produced the candidate + rank within it [4]

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Option Pros Cons
Heuristic Rank FoF by mutual-friend count / Adamic-Adar Cheap, explainable ("12 mutual") Hubs dominate; no cold start
Walk baseline Personalized PageRank / SALSA random walk with restart Reaches 3+ hops, down-weights hubs Hard to add side features [9]
Learned walk Supervised random walks (edge weights learned from features) Combines structure + attributes Older, costly per-user [14]
Pointwise GBDT / LR on pair features Strong light ranker, fast batch Ignores graph beyond hand features [1]
GNN GCN -> GraphSAGE (inductive, sampled) -> GAT (attention edge weights) Uses structure + features; new users Training scale, leakage risk [5][15][19]
MTL ranker Shared tower, send / accept / report heads Models reciprocity, safety More labels, calibration needed [4]
EBR GNN embeddings in ANN as extra source Beyond-2-hop recall, cold start "Similar stranger" risk [4][11]

Loss

Component Loss Notes
GNN edge prediction BCE on sigmoid(h_u . h_v) with sampled negatives [1][5]
EBR retrieval Sampled softmax over in-batch / sampled users Snap friend EBR pattern [11]
MTL ranker sum_k w_k BCE_k (send, accept send, report)
Regularization Dropout, BN, residuals, early stopping [5]

Offline metrics

Metric Measures Source
Recall@k on future edges Candidate source coverage [4]
ROC-AUC, log loss per head Edge / head discrimination [1][4][5]
mAP, NDCG@k, precision@k Ranked list quality [1][4]
Calibration per head Heads are multiplied, so must be calibrated [4]
Sliced metrics New users, low-degree, minors, with/without contacts [4]

Online metrics / A-B

Type Metric Source
Primary Accepted connections per viewer; requests sent and accepted per window [1][4][5]
Long term Connections with interaction within 28 days; new-user retention; WAU [4][10]
Funnel Impressions -> send rate -> acceptance rate [4]
Guardrails "Don't know"/remove rate, reports, pending backlog, requests to minors [4]
Design Interference (treated users invite control users): ego-cluster or graph-cluster randomization; long-term holdouts [4][6][16]

Serving & latency budget (~50 ms p99 assumption [4])

Step Budget Notes
Fetch precomputed list (KV) ~5 ms 100-500 candidates per user [4]
Read-time hard filters ~5 ms KV sets for blocks, pending, friends
Online feature fetch ~10 ms Mutual counts, recent activity
Light re-score (optional) ~15 ms GBDT or small MLP on ~500
Re-rank + social proof ~5 ms Diversity, caps, explanations
Network / slack ~10 ms Typical assumption
Cache miss / new user Async Online FoF + EBR with lightweight ranker, then write back [5][6]

Monitoring

Signal What to watch
Data Feature distribution drift, degree-distribution change, graph-structure alarms [5]
Model AUC/calibration per head on fresh data, score distributions
System p99 latency, KV hit rate, batch job freshness/SLA, training cost [5]
Ecosystem Incoming-request concentration (rich-get-richer), cross-cluster edge share [4][13]
Safety Reports, "don't know", adult-to-minor suggestion rate (should be 0) [4]

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Hub explosion in FoF (one friend with 100K edges) Sample/cap hubs, Adamic-Adar 1/log(deg) weighting [4]
Target / future-edge leakage Point-in-time joins, drop target edge, temporal split [4][6]
Optimizing sends only -> spam to popular users P(accept
Rich-get-richer, homophily Exposure caps, degree discounts, exploration, equity-aware objective [4][13]
Cold start (no edges) Contacts (consented), onboarding profile via inductive GNN, inviter's friends [4][11]
Creepy / privacy-leaking suggestions No sensitive sources, explanations only from visible signals [4]
Self-confirming evaluation Exploration traffic, long-term holdouts [4]
A/B contamination via network Ego-cluster / graph-cluster randomization [6][16]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Symmetric friendship or asymmetric follow? How does the objective change? [1][4]
  • How do you generate candidates on a 1B-user graph without request-time traversal? [1][4]
  • Why is Adamic-Adar often better than common-neighbour counts? [4]
  • Train on send, accept, or edge usage? How do you handle accept selection bias? [4]
  • How can link-prediction features leak, and how do you split train/test? [4][6]
  • Pointwise classifier vs. GNN edge prediction: what does each miss? [1][5]
  • GCN vs. GraphSAGE vs. GAT; how do you train a GNN on billions of nodes? [5][15]
  • Batch precompute vs. online prediction; how fresh must new users' lists be? [3][4][5]
  • Brand-new user with zero friends: what do you show? [4][11]
  • A/B test shows +5% connections; what could be wrong (network interference)? [4][6]
  • How do you avoid rich-get-richer and suggesting the same celebrities? [4][13]
  • What makes a suggestion "creepy", and how do you stop it? Minors? [4]
  • How do accepts arriving days later affect labels and metrics? [1][5]
  • How would you add embedding-based retrieval beside FoF? [10][11]
  • Which filters run before ranking and which after? (cheap pre-rank, heavy post-rank) [7]
  • Should onboarding (NUX) and the home module share one flow? (per-surface flows) [7]
  • How do you rank users who are not active enough to have a precomputed list? [5][6]

06. Design an Ad Click-Through-Rate Prediction and Ad Ranking System (with Auction and Calibration)

Prompt variants: "Ad click prediction on social platforms" (ByteByteGo), "Ad prediction system" (Educative), "Ads click prediction / ads ranking" (alirezadir), "Ad Click Prediction" (Khang Pham), "Design the ads ranking system for a feed" (Meta-style phrasing).

Company tags

Company Evidence Source

Google Search ads CTR at scale (FTRL-Proximal LR, isotonic calibration layer, Ad Rank); DCN-V2 paper reports production use in Google rankers [9] [23] [27]
Snap Engineering write-up on Snapchat ad ranking (listed in [24]) [12] [24]
LinkedIn Deep-learning ads CTR model; ads allocation in feed via constrained optimisation [13] [24] [25]
Twitter / X Ads engagement with delayed feedback, and prediction of ad-request value [4] [11] [14] [24]
Pinterest, Etsy, Wayfair Lookalike ad targeting, real-time ads personalisation, ads bidding (all listed in [24]) [15] [16] [17] [24]

Portals that cover it

  • ByteByteGo / Aminian & Xu, ML System Design Interview, chapter "Ad Click Prediction on Social Platforms" [1]
  • Educative, Grokking the Machine Learning Interview, "Ad Prediction System" module [2]
  • Educative / Khang Pham, Machine Learning System Design, plus the khangich GitHub "Ad Click Prediction" case and Adtech reading list [3] [4]
  • alirezadir/Machine-Learning-Interviews (AIMLInterviews), mlsd-ads-ranking.md "Ads click prediction" [5] [6]
  • Hello Interview (recsys pattern), Exponent / Aced, IGotAnOffer, Prepfully: generic ranking frameworks used for this prompt [18] [19] [20] [21]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source / status
Business goal Maximise long-term revenue = advertiser value + user experience (not raw CTR) [1] [5] [22]
Functional For each ad slot in a feed or search page, pick and price ads; predict P(click), optionally P(conv) [5]
ML task Pointwise LTR: binary classification on (user, ad, context) [5]
Label Click within t seconds of impression = 1, else 0; "hide/report ad" = negative signal [5]
Users / ads 1B+ DAU; 10M+ active ads, millions of advertisers typical assumption
QPS 100k-1M ad requests/s at peak (Khang Pham's worked case assumes 4k/s); ranker scores 100s-1000s ads per request typical assumption; [4]
Latency Ads pipeline p99 ~100-150 ms total, ranker ~10-30 ms typical assumption; 150 ms in [4]
Base rate CTR is low (often ~1-2% or less), so classes are very imbalanced [4] [7]
Freshness New ads and campaigns arrive constantly; stale models lose accuracy daily [7] [9]
Hard constraints Calibrated probabilities (they feed the auction and billing); budget pacing; privacy; ad policy [7] [9] [22]

Funnel numbers (typical assumption)

Stage In -> out Model Budget
Targeting + retrieval 10M -> 10k Inverted index + ANN embeddings 10-20 ms
Filtering 10k -> 2k Rules (budget, frequency cap, policy) 2-5 ms
Light ranking 2k -> 200 Two-tower / small GBDT/DNN 5-10 ms
Heavy ranking + calibration 200 -> 200 scored DCN-V2 / DeepFM / MTL DNN 10-30 ms
Auction + re-rank 200 -> 1-5 slots eCPM, GSP/VCG, business rules 1-5 ms
