DIAGRAM 4: the real system (Facebook, He et al. 2014)

Diagram 4. Facebook's hybrid GBDT + logistic regression CTR model with online joiner and online learning [7] [8]

 +--------------------+     raw features x (continuous + categorical)
 | Ad impression +    |--------------------------------------------+
 | user/ad/context    |                                            |
 +--------------------+                                            v
                         +-----------------------------------------------+
                         | Boosted trees (batch, daily / every few days) |
                         |  tree 1    tree 2    ...    tree T            |
                         |   leaf k1   leaf k2          leaf kT          |
                         +----------------------+------------------------+
                                                | one-hot leaf indices
                                                v   (learned feature transform)
                         +-----------------------------------------------+
                         | LR, near-real-time SGD, per-coordinate LR     |
                         | p = sigmoid(w . leaf_onehot + b)              |
                         +-----------+------------------------+----------+
                                     ^                        |
                                     | updated LR weights     | p -> recalibrate
                                     |                        v   (if downsampled)
 +--------------------+  labels  +---+----------------+  +-----------------+
 | ONLINE JOINER      |--------->| Online trainer     |  | Auction (eCPM)  |
 | impressions+clicks |          | (Scribe stream)    |  +-----------------+
 | waiting window t   |          +--------------------+
 +--------------------+
 Findings: hybrid beat either alone (trees cut NE >3.4%); weekly -> daily
 training cuts NE ~1%; best negative-downsampling rate 0.025 (then recalibrate);
 NE + calibration are the offline metrics; historical features dominate top 10.

Data & labels

Item Choice Notes / source
Positive Click within t s of impression [5] [7]
Negative Impression with no click by end of window; hide/report as strong negative [5]
Conversion label Purchase/install after click, arrives hours-days later delayed feedback [11]
Window t Trade-off: short = fresher but more false negatives; long = accurate but stale [7] [11]
Imbalance Downsample negatives at rate w; recalibrate q = p / (p + (1-p)/w) [7]
Position bias Log position; use as training feature and fix it at serve time, or use a shallow position tower typical practice
Leakage Point-in-time feature joins; split train/test by time, not randomly [5]

Features

Group Examples Encoding
Ad ad id, advertiser id, campaign, category, creative image/text/video Embeddings; pretrained encoders (e.g. SimCLR-style) [5]
Ad engagement impressions, clicks, CTR at ad/advertiser/campaign level, 1h/1d/7d Dense, log-scaled, smoothed for new ads
User demographics, location, device, language Embeddings / one-hot
User history historical CTR, last N clicked ads/categories Sequence + attention
User-ad cross user x ad-category CTR, previous impressions of this ad (fatigue) Crosses or learned by DCN/FM
Context slot/position, time of day, surface (feed/stories/search), query One-hot / embeddings
Bid / objective bid type and objective (not usually a CTR feature; used in auction) Kept out of pCTR to avoid bias

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Model Strengths Weaknesses Source
Logistic regression (+ hashing) Fast, calibrated-ish, easy online learning (FTRL) No interactions without manual crosses [5] [9]
LR + manual feature crosses Captures key pairwise interactions Manual, combinatorial, sparse [1] [5]
GBDT Strong on dense features, interpretable Poor with huge sparse IDs; no continual training [5]
GBDT + LR Trees as feature transform; LR learns online Two systems to maintain [7]
Factorization Machine (FM/FFM) Learned pairwise interactions via embeddings Only 2nd-order [1] [5]
Wide & Deep / DeepFM Memorisation + generalisation, no manual crosses Bigger, harder to calibrate [26] [28]
DCN / DCN-V2 Explicit bounded-degree crosses + deep tower; production use at Google Tuning cross depth [27]
DLRM / DIN / MMoE multi-task Huge embedding tables, user-sequence attention, joint pCTR/pCVR Infra cost, GPU serving [29] [30]

Loss

Loss Use
Binary cross-entropy (log loss) Default for pCTR; directly optimises calibrated probability [1] [5]
Weighted BCE / importance weights Correct for negative downsampling [7]
Multi-task sum: L = BCE(click, pCTR) + BCE(click & conv, pCTR x pCVR) over all impressions ESMM: pCVR learned implicitly, avoiding sample-selection bias and click sparsity [30]
Pairwise / listwise (optional) Improves ordering but breaks calibration; usually avoided as the only loss because the auction needs absolute probabilities
L1/L2 + FTRL regularisation Sparsity for huge hashed feature spaces [9]

Calibration

Topic Detail Source
Why eCPM = bid x pCTR: a 10% overestimate means overcharging/mis-ranking advertisers [7] [9] [22]
Calibration ratio sum(predicted pCTR) / sum(actual clicks); target 1.0 overall and per slice [7]
Downsampling fix q = p / (p + (1-p)/w), w = negative sampling rate [7]
Post-hoc methods Google: fit tau(p) = gamma x p^kappa by Poisson regression, or piecewise-linear isotonic map per data slice; Platt / temperature scaling for DNNs [9] [31]
Monitoring Calibration plots by bucket, per advertiser; alert when ratio drifts beyond about +-5% typical assumption
Training-time subsampling Google keeps all clicked queries and a fraction r of others, weighting kept negatives by 1/r so the loss stays unbiased [9]

Auction and ranking score

Concept Formula / rule Source
Expected value (CPC bid) eCPM = 1000 x bid_CPC x pCTR standard practice
Optimised CPM / CPA value = bid_CPA x pCTR x pCVR [12]
Meta "total value" advertiser bid x estimated action rate + ad quality [22]
Google "Ad Rank" bid, ad quality (expected CTR, relevance, landing page), thresholds, context [23]
Pricing GSP: pay the minimum needed to keep the slot; VCG: pay the externality imposed; plus reserve prices standard practice
Re-rank / policy Ad load limits, advertiser diversity, frequency caps, pacing multiplier on bid [1] [5]
Ads allocation in feed Choose ad slots in an organic feed by maximising revenue subject to user-engagement constraints (LinkedIn) [25]
Autobidding / pacing Platform adjusts bids per auction to hit advertiser budget and CPA/ROAS goals [17]

Offline metrics

Metric Why Source
Normalised entropy (NE) / normalised cross-entropy Log loss divided by the entropy of the background CTR; lower is better [1] [7]
Log loss Measures probability quality (needed by the auction) [5]
ROC-AUC / PR-AUC Ranking quality; insensitive to calibration, so do not use alone [7]
Calibration ratio, reliability diagram Absolute probability correctness [7]
Sliced metrics New ads, new users, country, surface, advertiser size typical practice

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Type
Revenue per mille (RPM) / revenue lift Primary business metric [5]
CTR, conversion rate Engagement [5]
Advertiser ROI / cost per action, advertiser retention Advertiser health
Hide/report rate, organic engagement, session time User-experience guardrails [5]
Calibration in production, auction-price changes Safety
A/B design Randomise users; watch budget-split interference between arms (advertiser budgets are shared), so use budget-split or advertiser-side experiments

Serving & latency budget

Component Budget (p99) Technique
Feature fetch 5-10 ms In-memory KV store, batched multi-get, cached ad features
Retrieval 10-20 ms Inverted targeting index + ANN
Light ranker 5-10 ms Two-tower dot product, ad embeddings precomputed
Heavy ranker 10-30 ms GPU/CPU batch inference, quantised embeddings, model distillation
Auction + logging <5 ms In-process; async log write
Total ~100 ms Timeouts with fallback to a cached or simpler model

Monitoring

What Signal
Prediction drift Mean pCTR vs observed CTR per hour/slice (calibration ratio)
Feature drift / missing Null rate, distribution shift (PSI) per feature; online/offline skew check
Data pipeline Joiner lag, label delay, event loss
Business Revenue, spend pacing, advertiser complaints, auction clearing price
Model freshness Hours since last successful update; NE on latest hour

What the production papers add (often missed in portal answers)

Item Detail Source
Online joiner click coverage Too short a wait window loses clicks and biases empirical CTR low; too long delays data and costs memory [7]
Probabilistic feature inclusion Add a new sparse feature only after it is seen n times (counting Bloom filter) or with probability p (Poisson) to save RAM [9]
Progressive validation Score each example before training on it in online learning; no separate holdout needed [9]
Confidence estimates Per-prediction uncertainty to drive exploration and guard bids on rare ads [9]
Automated feature management Feature metadata, owners and automatic alerts on signal changes across many models [9]
Model size vs trees Fewer boosted trees keep latency and memory down at small NE cost [7]

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Mis-calibration after downsampling or a model swap Recalibration step; calibration gate in deployment [7]
Cold-start ads (no history) Content embeddings, advertiser priors, exploration budget (bandits / boosted bids)
Delayed conversions labelled as negative Delayed-feedback model, longer windows, label correction [11]
Training-serving skew Log features at serve time; reuse those logs for training [7]
Feedback loop / selection bias (only shown ads get labels) Exploration traffic, inverse propensity weighting
Ad fatigue Frequency caps; impression-count features [5]
Click fraud / bots Invalid-traffic filters before labelling
Catastrophic forgetting with continual training Replay buffer, periodic full retrain [5]
Privacy changes (lost cross-app signals) On-platform signals, aggregated conversion APIs, modelled conversions

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why must pCTR be calibrated, and how would you measure and fix miscalibration? [7]
  • You downsampled negatives to 1%. How do you correct the predicted probabilities? [7]
  • Why is AUC not enough as an offline metric for ads? What is normalised entropy? [7]
  • How do you pick the click attribution window t, and how do you handle delayed conversions? [11]
  • How does the auction combine bid, pCTR, pCVR and quality? GSP vs VCG? [22] [23]
  • How do you rank ads for a CPA (conversion) advertiser vs a CPC advertiser?
  • Walk through LR -> FM -> DeepFM -> DCN. Why do plain MLPs struggle with sparse crosses? [1] [5]
  • How fresh must the model be? Online learning vs daily retrain trade-offs? [7] [9]
  • How do you handle a new ad or new advertiser with no history (cold start)?
  • How do you deal with position bias in click logs?
  • How do you A/B test when the treatment and control arms share advertiser budgets?
  • How would you keep the heavy ranker within 30 ms for 1,000 candidates?
  • How do you trade off ad revenue against user experience (ad load, hides)?
  • What happens to the system when third-party tracking signals disappear?
  • How do you prevent the model from learning from fraudulent clicks?
  • How long should the online joiner wait before labelling a no-click, and what does that do to click coverage? [7]
  • How would you add millions of new sparse features without blowing up model RAM? [9]
  • Where should ads go in an organic feed, and how many? [25]

[4] [5] [6] [10] [24] were re-read from GitHub; the texts of [7] and [9] were checked from PDF mirrors, confirming NE, calibration ratio, online joiner, downsampling recalibration, Poisson/isotonic calibration and subsampling weights. URLs for [7]-[9], [11]-[17] and [31] are confirmed as links in [4] [10] [24]; their pages were not loaded. [1]-[3], [18]-[23] and [26]-[30] are cited from prior knowledge. An unsupported TikTok/Amazon/Reddit/Uber tag row was removed. Scale numbers marked "typical assumption" are not sourced.

07. Design Product Search Ranking for an E-commerce Site (Amazon Search), Including Query Understanding

Prompt as usually given: "A user types a query into the Amazon (or Walmart, Etsy, Flipkart) search box. Design the ML system that returns the most relevant products, ranked to maximise purchases." Variants: "design a search ranking system", "improve product search recall", "design Airbnb search ranking", "design typeahead / query autocomplete" (a sub-problem).

Company tags

Company (reported) Where it was reported Notes
Amazon Community-compiled Amazon MLE interview process [22] Sample ML system design prompt: "Design a search retrieval and ranking pipeline, including online experiments and position-bias correction" [22]; Stores "search and personalization" team owns product search ranking [22]
Airbnb Khang Pham case list [5]; Chip Huyen exercise 9 [7] "Display top 10 results when a user searches for rental listings in a certain location" [7]
Google (adjacent, not confirmed) Chip Huyen exercises 5-6 use Google-style "related searches" and Google Images text-to-image search [7] Web/image-search framing of the same retrieve-then-rank funnel
Walmart, Etsy, eBay Not confirmed as interview prompts; they publish the production systems this question mirrors [14] [15] [19] Use their papers as "real system" talking points

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Text query in, ranked list of products out (SERP); filters/facets; ad auction out of scope (sponsored slots only blended in) [1]
Business goal Higher CTR and conversion (purchases per search) [1]
Personalization Optional in v1 ("not required" in [1]); add in v2 via user features / personalized EBR [14] [1] [14]
Users 50M DAU (alirezadir assumption); Amazon-scale 300M+ users (typical assumption) [1]
Catalog [1] writes "from 100 B to 100k" (likely a typo); 100M-1B products is a typical assumption [1]
Query volume 5M queries/day in [1]; Amazon-scale ~10k-50k QPS peak (typical assumption) [1]
Latency End-to-end p99 < 200 ms; ranker < 50 ms; feature fetch < 10 ms [4] [4] + assumption
Funnel sizes Catalog -> ~100k (retrieval) -> stage-1 -> ~500 (stage-2 output) [1]; [4] uses 500 as the stage-1 window; top 10-50 shown [1] [4]
Freshness New products searchable in minutes (index); price/stock real time; models retrained daily-weekly Typical assumption
Languages / locales Multi-locale (ESCI covers US, ES, JP) [10]

Stage In -> out Model p99 budget

DIAGRAM 3: model architecture

Diagram 3a. Retrieval: Amazon "Semantic Product Search" style two-tower model [8] (shared token embeddings over word unigrams, bigrams and character trigrams; average pooling; trained on purchase / impression / random negatives with a 3-part hinge loss)

        QUERY TOWER                                   PRODUCT TOWER
 "nike running shoes men"                 title + brand + attributes + category
            |                                              |
            v                                              v
 +-----------------------+                     +-----------------------+
 | tokenize: unigrams,   |                     | tokenize: unigrams,   |
 | bigrams, char-3grams; |                     | bigrams, char-3grams; |
 | OOV -> hashed bins    |                     | OOV -> hashed bins    |
 +-----------+-----------+                     +-----------+-----------+
             v                                             v
 +-----------------------+    shared weights   +-----------------------+
 | token embedding table |<------------------->| token embedding table |
 +-----------+-----------+                     +-----------+-----------+
             v  average pool                               v  average pool
 +-----------------------+                     +-----------------------+
 | dense layer(s) + norm |                     | dense layer(s) + norm |
 +-----------+-----------+                     +-----------+-----------+
             | q (d=256)                                   | p (d=256)
             +-------------------+   +---------------------+
                                 v   v
                          +-----------------+
                          | cosine(q, p)    |
                          +--------+--------+
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------------+
       | 3-part hinge loss [8]:                                      |
       |  purchased      -> push score above high threshold          |
       |  impressed, not purchased -> push into middle band          |
       |  random negative -> push below low threshold                |
       +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  Serving: p precomputed for all products -> ANN index; q computed per query
  (cached for head queries). Upgrade path: BERT-style towers, hard negatives,
  personalized user tower (Etsy [14], Facebook EBR [13]).

Diagram 3b. Ranking: multi-task learning-to-rank DNN with LambdaRank-style listwise objective (synthesised from [1] [11] [17]; Airbnb's GBDT -> NN -> deep NN path [11])

 +-------------+ +--------------+ +----------------+ +-------------+ +----------+
 | Query feats | | Product feats| | Query-product  | | User / ctx  | | Retrieval|
 | category,   | | price, rating| | BM25, attr     | | history emb,| | scores:  |
 | intent, len,| | #reviews,    | | match, q-cat   | | device,     | | cosine,  |
 | head/tail,  | | sales rank,  | | CTR, CTR/CVR of| | locale,     | | BM25     |
 | q-embedding | | stock, ship  | | (q,p) pair     | | time        | |          |
 +------+------+ +------+-------+ +-------+--------+ +------+------+ +----+-----+
        |               |                 |                 |             |
        +---------------+---------+-------+-----------------+-------------+
                                  v
           +----------------------------------------------+
           | Shared bottom: concat -> cross layers (DCN)  |
           | -> MLP 512-256-128                           |
           | inputs: sparse ids -> embeddings; dense ->   |
           | log/normalize (NN needs it [11])             |
           +-------+-----------------+---------------+----+
                   |                 |               |
              +----v----------+  +---v----------+  +-v-------------+
              | head: P(click)|  | head: P(ATC) |  | head: P(buy)  |
              +-------+-------+  +------+-------+  +-------+-------+
                      +-----------------+------------------+
                                        v
               score = w1*P(click) + w2*P(ATC) + w3*P(buy)   (or P(buy) only)
                                        v
          +----------------------------------------------------------------+
          | Loss per query group: LambdaRank (NDCG-weighted pairwise) on   |
          | graded labels 0-4 [1] [17] + BCE per head; position fed as a   |
          | feature at train time, fixed to slot 1 at serving (bias fix)   |

Data & labels

Source Label / use Caveats
Search logs (implicit) Graded: impression 0, click 1, dwell > T 2, add-to-cart 3, purchase 4 [1] Position bias, presentation bias, only shown items labelled
Purchases Strongest positive; Amazon trains on purchases [8] [9] Sparse, delayed; some purchases look irrelevant to the query [28]
Impressed-not-purchased Hard-ish negatives / middle band [8] Not truly irrelevant
Random products Easy negatives (or page 10+ results) [1] [8] Too easy alone; add hard negatives [13]
Human judgements ESCI 4-class (Exact, Substitute, Complement, Irrelevant): 130k queries, 2.6M judgements, 3 locales [10] Costly; [1] estimates 100k queries x 10 results x 10 raters = 10M and rejects it as not scalable
Catalog Product tower inputs, attribute tags for QU Noisy seller-entered text
Window >= 1 week to cover weekly cycle; temporal split [1] Holiday seasonality

Features

Group Examples Freshness
Query Length, category distribution, head/torso/tail bucket, intent, historical CTR, embedding [1] [4] Daily (head cached)
Product Price, rating, #reviews, sales rank, stock, delivery speed, title/image embeddings, age Price/stock real time; rest daily
Query-product BM25 / TF-IDF unigram+bigram, attribute match (brand, color, size), query-category match, historical (q,p) CTR/CVR, embedding cosine [1] [4] Hourly-daily
User Past purchases/views in category, brand affinity, price sensitivity, Prime Near real time
Context Device, locale, time, previous queries in session [1] Request time
Position (train only) Displayed rank Fixed at serving

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
QU Rules + dictionaries + edit-distance spell Neural query rewriting from reformulation logs (Amazon QUEEN [23]), BERT NER, LLM rewrites (offline for head queries) Quality vs latency; cache head
Retrieval Inverted index + TF-IDF/BM25, weighted linear relevance (term match 0.5, popularity 0.125, intent 0.0625) [1]; same signals unweighted in [4] Two-tower EBR [8], personalized EBR [13] [14], hybrid with lexical [15] Recall on tail vs precision on exact attrs
Stage-1 LR / small GBDT pointwise, AUC [1] [4] Distilled small NN Microseconds per item [1]
Stage-2 LambdaMART (GBDT) [1] [17] [31] Multi-task DNN with LambdaRank loss [11] [25]; Etsy moved search ranking from GBDT to DNN [19]; cross-encoder (BERT) on top-50 DNN needs feature normalization and more data [11]
Re-rank Business rules, dedupe Diversity model [12], explore/exploit Relevance vs diversity
Seasonality Recency-weighted retrain Seasonal-relevance model as ranking feature (Amazon [24]) Extra model to maintain

Loss

Model Loss Why
Two-tower In-batch softmax / contrastive; 3-part hinge with purchase/impression/random [8] Learn semantic match at scale
Stage-1 Binary cross-entropy (pointwise) [1] Cheap, calibrated
Stage-2 LambdaRank / LambdaMART: pairwise with delta-NDCG weights [17] Optimises ranking metric directly
Multi-task heads Sum of BCE per head (click, ATC, buy) Dense click signal helps sparse purchase
Debiasing Inverse propensity weighting; unbiased LambdaMART [33] (XGBoost lambdarank_unbiased [31]) Remove position bias

Offline metrics

Metric Stage Note
Recall@k (k=100, 1000) Retrieval Did the purchased item enter the funnel?
NDCG@10 Ranking Graded labels 0-4; chosen because relevance is non-binary [1] [4]
MRR Ranking Position of first purchased item [1]
AUC / log loss Stage-1, heads Pointwise quality [1] [4]
ESCI-judged NDCG / precision Whole SERP Human relevance, catches "buyable but irrelevant" [10]
Slices All Head vs tail queries, locale, new products, category

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Type Note
Conversion rate (purchases / search) Primary Business goal [1]
Revenue / GMV per search Primary Watch price-mix shift
CTR Secondary Prone to clickbait [1]
Successful session rate (dwell > T or ATC) Secondary [1] [4]
Zero-result rate, reformulation rate, time-to-first-click Guardrail QU quality signals
Latency p99, error rate Guardrail SLA
Interleaving Fast pre-test Higher sensitivity for ranking comparisons

Serving & latency budget

Component Choice Budget
QU Cached results for head queries (~top 1M queries); online models for tail 10-15 ms
ANN HNSW / PQ-quantized index, sharded by product id [14] 10-20 ms
Inverted index Sharded Lucene/Elasticsearch-style 10-20 ms (parallel with ANN)
Feature fetch Online KV (Redis/DynamoDB) [4] < 10 ms [4]
Stage-1 / Stage-2 CPU GBDT; GPU or CPU-optimised DNN, batch per request 10 ms / 30-40 ms
Total p99 < 200 ms (assumption)

Monitoring

What Signal Action
Input drift Query distribution, new tokens, category mix (holidays) Refresh QU dictionaries, retrain
Feature health Null rates, staleness of price/stock Alert, fallback defaults
Quality Zero-result rate, NDCG on daily human-judged sample [10] Rollback
Train-serve skew Logged serving features vs offline recomputed Log features at serve time
Index ANN recall vs brute force on sample, index age Rebuild
Business Conversion per search by slice Alert on drops

Failure modes

Failure Cause Mitigation
Accessories outrank main product ("iphone" -> cases) Click/purchase popularity beats relevance ESCI relevance model as feature/gate [10]; product-type match
Inappropriate items on SERP Offensive/adult products match query P(inappropriate) filter model (LR/MART/DNN) before the blender [1]
Zero results on tail queries Lexical mismatch, typos Spell correct, query relaxation, semantic retrieval [8] [15]
Attribute violations ("red dress" shows blue) Semantic retrieval ignores exact attrs Hybrid lexical + attribute filters [15] [16]
Rich-get-richer Feedback loop, position bias IPW, exploration slots, position feature [33]
Cold-start products No engagement stats Content features, embedding retrieval, boost new items
Seasonality Holiday query shift ("costume" in October) Short retrain cycle, seasonal-relevance feature [24]
Spam / keyword stuffing Sellers gaming titles Spam classifier, quality features
Latency blow-up on broad queries Huge candidate sets Cap per-source candidates, early termination

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you build relevance labels? Clicks vs purchases vs human ESCI judgements, and how do you combine them? [1] [10]
  • How do you correct position bias in click logs (IPW, position-as-feature, randomized swaps)? [22] [33]
  • Walk through query understanding for "apple watch band 41mm black": which models, in what order?
  • Why two-stage ranking instead of one heavy model? Where does the cutoff (500) come from? [1] [4]
  • Lexical vs semantic retrieval: when does each fail, and how do you merge them? [8] [15]
  • How do you handle tail queries and zero-result searches?
  • Pointwise vs pairwise vs listwise loss: why LambdaMART for stage 2? [17]
  • Why can NDCG go up offline while conversion goes down online?
  • How do you rank a brand-new product with no history?
  • How would you add personalization without hurting relevance? [13] [14]
  • How do you blend sponsored products with organic results?
  • How do you design the A/B test; why might interleaving be used first?
  • Real-time features for product search (price, stock): architecture and skew?
  • How would you learn query rewrites from reformulation sessions? [23]
  • How do you handle seasonal queries whose intent shifts over the year? [24]
  • How would you blend text-search results with visual search in one SERP? [1]
  • How would you use an LLM here (query rewriting, relevance labelling, cross-encoder distillation) within latency?
  • How do you keep the ANN index fresh as millions of products change daily?

08. Design Product Recommendations for Amazon ("Customers Also Bought" + Homepage Recs)

Prompt as usually given: "Design the recommendation system behind Amazon's product detail page ('customers who bought this also bought') and the personalized homepage." Variants: "similar items" carousel, "frequently bought together", replacement items for out-of-stock products (Instacart, Chip Huyen ex. 3), cart add-on recs, recs in email.

Sourcing note: at review time the web-search budget was exhausted and several hosts (amazon.science, arxiv.org, bytebytego.com, igotanoffer.com, hellointerview.com) did not resolve. (fetched) = read during review; (ch-ref) = verified in an earlier chapter of this atlas; (known) = canonical paper cited by DOI/arXiv ID. Company tags for this exact prompt are thinner than for feed/video prompts; treat them as indicative.

Company tags

Company What is reported Source
Amazon MLE loop includes ML design. Product recs is the house problem: item-to-item CF was invented there [1][2][3] [11]
Instacart "Replacement product recommendation" is in the AIMLInterviews MLSD question list [8]
Generic e-commerce "Suggest replacement items for out-of-stock products" (Chip Huyen exercise 3) [10]
Meta (Marketplace) Marketplace recs named as a Meta MLSD prompt [12]

Portals that cover it

Portal Treatment Link
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu, MLSDI) No Amazon chapter. The closest is "Similar Listings on Vacation Rental Platforms" (session-based item embeddings), plus "Video Recommendation" for the homepage half [13][14]
Educative "Grokking the ML Interview" Recommendation-system module (Netflix-style). Candidate gen with CF and embeddings, then a ranker [15]
Educative / Khang Pham "ML System Design" Case studies plus Wide & Deep and YouTube DNN reading [9][16]
alirezadir AIMLInterviews Recsys template (CF, two-tower, LTR, metrics) and the Instacart prompt [8]
Hello Interview Recommendation-systems pattern page (retrieval, ranking, re-ranking) [17]
Exponent / Aced MLSD course and guide; the recsys framework applies directly [18][19]
Chip Huyen Exercises 3 and 21 (replacement items, faster checkout) [10][20]
IGotAnOffer, Patrick Halina, DesignGurus Amazon MLE guide, generic MLSD guides [11][21][22]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Surfaces (a) Detail page "also bought/viewed" and "frequently bought together" (complements), item-anchored. (b) Homepage, user-anchored. (c) Cart and email [1][2][26]
Business goal Incremental revenue/GMV and conversion, not just CTR [2][3]
Functional Top-K (about 10-50) items per widget, in stock, eligible, deduped, diversified assumption
Catalog Hundreds of millions of SKUs (long tail). Plan for 10^8-10^9 items assumption
Users About 300M active customers. Most are sparse, many are logged out assumption
QPS 10^5+ widget requests/s at peak (several widgets per page view, Prime Day spikes) assumption
Latency Under 100 ms p99 per widget. Model scoring about 20-40 ms assumption
Freshness Session signals within seconds. Item-item tables daily to hourly. New SKUs within hours assumption
Key constraint Item-to-item similarity is computed offline; the online step is a lookup, so it scales independently of user count [1] [1]

Diagram 3: Model architecture

Figure 8.3: Two-stage model. A two-tower retriever and item-item CF feed a multi-task ranker. Its heads are combined into one expected-value score.

     RETRIEVAL: TWO-TOWER (sampled softmax, logQ correction)
 +---------------------------+           +-----------------------------+
 | User/query tower          |           | Item tower                  |
 | user_id emb, last-N views |           | ASIN id emb (hashed), brand,|
 | & buys (avg/attn pool),   |           | category path, price bucket,|
 | search terms, anchor ASIN |           | title text emb, image emb   |
 | (detail page), ctx (dev,  |           |                             |
 | locale, time)             |           |                             |
 +-------------+-------------+           +--------------+--------------+
               | MLP -> u (d=128)                       | MLP -> v (d=128)
               +------------------+  dot(u,v)  +--------+
                                  v            v
                          +--------------------------+
                          | score = u . v; ANN top-N |
                          +--------------------------+

     RANKING: MULTI-TASK DNN (DLRM / Wide&Deep / DIN-style)
 +----------+  +-------------+  +------------------+  +-------------------+
 | Sparse   |  | Dense       |  | User behaviour   |  | Cross features    |
 | ids:user,|  | price, avg  |  | seq (last 50     |  | i2i sim(anchor,   |
 | item,    |  | rating, CTR,|  | items) -> target-|  | cand), bought-same|
 | brand,cat|  | conv, stock |  | attention (DIN)  |  | -category-30d     |
 +----+-----+  +------+------+  +--------+---------+  +---------+---------+
      | emb tables    |                  |                      |
      +-------+-------+--------+---------+----------+-----------+
              v                v                    v
         +--------------------------------------------------+
         | Feature interaction (dot / DCN cross layers)     |
         +-------------------------+------------------------+
                                   v
                 +-----------------------------------+
                 | Shared bottom / MMoE experts      |
                 +----+------------+-------------+---+
                      v            v             v
                 +--------+   +---------+   +----------+
                 | pClick |   | pATC    |   | pBuy|clk |  (+ pReturn head)
                 +---+----+   +----+----+   +----+-----+
                     +-------------+-------------+
                                   v
          final = pClick * pBuy|clk * margin_or_price^a  + b * pATC
                  (weights tuned online; a, b are business knobs)

Diagram 4: Real system (Amazon item-to-item collaborative filtering)

Figure 8.4: Amazon's item-to-item CF, as described in Linden, Smith & York (2003) and Smith & Linden (2017). The expensive similar-items table is built offline. Online work only looks up and merges the neighbours of the items the user has interacted with [1][2][3].

 OFFLINE (batch, daily)                         ONLINE (per request)
 +-------------------------------+              +-------------------------------+
 | Purchase / view histories     |              | User's recent items (bought,  |
 | for every customer            |              | viewed, in cart) or anchor    |
 +---------------+---------------+              +---------------+---------------+
                 | for each item i, each customer c             | for each item j
                 | who bought i, each item k bought by c:       v
                 | count co(i,k)                +-------------------------------+
                 v                              | lookup SimTable[j] -> top-N   |
 +-------------------------------+      +------>| neighbours                    |
 | Similarity(i,k): cosine on    |      |       +---------------+---------------+
 | customer vectors (2003), or   |      |                       | merge, weight by
 | observed vs EXPECTED co-buys  |      |                       | recency, drop owned
 | under a random-buyer baseline |  +---+---+                   v
 | (2017; corrects popularity),  |->| Sim   |   +-----------------------------------+
 | time order, relation type     |  | Table |   | top-K "Customers who bought this  |
 +-------------------------------+  | (KV)  |   | also bought" / "Recommended for   |
  cost ~ O(items x avg basket^2);   +-------+   | you"                              |
  most items have few customers                 +-----------------------------------+
                                                latency independent of #users

Data & labels

Signal Use as label? Notes
Purchase (net of returns) Primary positive Sparse, delayed up to days. Use an attribution window [2]
Add-to-cart Auxiliary positive Denser than purchases, strong intent
Click on rec Auxiliary positive Densest. Rewards clickbait if used alone
Impression without click Negative (ranker) Only items that were actually shown. Watch position bias
Detail view / dwell Feature + weak positive Drives the "also viewed" widget
Rating / review Feature Too sparse and biased to use as a label
Co-purchase in the same basket or session Item-item pair positive Basis for "also bought" / "frequently bought together" [1]
Random catalog items Negatives (retrieval) In-batch and sampled negatives, with logQ correction [5]

Features

Group Examples
User Hashed user id, purchase categories (30/90/365 d), price sensitivity, Prime flag, locale
Session / context Anchor ASIN, last-N viewed and searched, device, time, page type, cart contents
Item ASIN id, brand, category path, price, rating, review count, stock, delivery speed
Item content Title and description text embedding, image embedding (for cold start)
Item stats Rec CTR, conversion rate, return rate (smoothed, by age bucket)
User x item Category affinity, brand affinity, already-owned flag, i2i score to recent items
Anchor x candidate Co-purchase lift, complement vs substitute type, price ratio

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
"Also bought" Co-occurrence counts Item-to-item CF with an expected-vs-observed correction [1][2] Cheap and explainable. Weak on new items
"Frequently bought together" Co-purchase pairs minus co-view pairs (removes substitutes) Complement model with type-aware, diversified outputs (Amazon P-Companion) [26] Separates complements from substitutes; handles cold-start anchors via content
Item similarity Content (text/category) kNN Item2vec / session embeddings (ByteByteGo similar-listings style) [13] Covers cold start. Needs ANN
Homepage retrieval Popular by category Matrix factorization, then two-tower [4][5] Two-tower personalizes and scales via ANN, but is costly to train
Sequential Last-viewed neighbours Transformer next-item model (e.g. SASRec) [24] Captures intent shifts. Higher latency
Ranker Logistic regression or GBDT on hand-made features Wide & Deep / DLRM / DIN with multi-task heads [6][7][23][25] Better calibration and accuracy. Needs a GPU/CPU serving budget
Re-rank Business rules MMR diversity plus a constrained optimizer (sponsored slots, margins) Trades a little relevance for diversity and revenue

Loss functions

Model Loss
Two-tower Sampled softmax / in-batch softmax with logQ correction [5]. Optionally a hard-negative margin loss
Item embeddings Skip-gram with negative sampling over sessions or baskets
Ranker heads Per-task binary cross-entropy, summed with task weights (or uncertainty weighting). pBuy trained on clicked items, or as an ESMM-style pClick x pBuy chain to avoid selection bias [27]
Re-rank (optional) Listwise (LambdaRank / softmax over the slate)

Offline metrics

Stage Metric
Retrieval Recall@K / hit-rate@K on next purchase, catalog coverage
Ranking AUC and log loss per head, NDCG@K, calibration (predicted vs. observed)
Slate Intra-list diversity, novelty, share of long-tail items
Evaluation Time-based split (train on days 1..T, test on T+1). Counterfactual / IPS replay on exploration logs
Slices New users, new items, categories, logged-out, mobile vs desktop

Online metrics / A-B

Type Metric
Primary Revenue or GMV per visit attributed to the widget, conversion rate
Secondary Widget CTR, add-to-cart rate, units per order
Guardrails Return rate, page latency p99, sponsored revenue, complaints, sitewide sales (cannibalization)
Design User-level randomization. 1-2 weeks to cover the purchase delay. Holdout for long-term effect. Interleaving for fast ranker comparisons

Serving & latency budget (assumption, per widget, p99)

Step Budget How
Request parse + user/session fetch 5 ms Online feature store
Candidate gen (parallel) 15-25 ms KV lookup of the item-item table (about 1 ms); ANN HNSW top-500
Filters 5 ms Bloom filter of owned items, inventory cache
Feature assembly 10 ms Batched multi-get
Ranking ~500 items 20-30 ms CPU/GPU batched inference, quantized embeddings
Re-rank + policy 5 ms In-process
Total under 80-100 ms Fallback: cached precomputed recs per user, or bestsellers

Monitoring

What Signal
Data Feature null rates and drift (PSI), label delay, event volume per surface
Model Calibration per head, score distribution, online AUC from delayed labels
Business Widget CTR and GMV per visit by surface, anomaly alerts during events (Prime Day)
System p99 latency, fallback rate, ANN recall vs exact search, KV staleness
Ecosystem Concentration (Gini of impressions), share of new and long-tail items

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Popular items dominate "also bought" (e.g. batteries everywhere) Expected-vs-observed similarity, IDF-style damping [2]
Recommending items the user just bought (non-consumables) Owned-item filter. Allow consumables (replenishment)
Substitutes on the post-purchase page Separate complement and substitute models by page context [2][26]
New SKU or new user cold start Content-tower embeddings, category bestsellers, exploration slots
Out-of-stock or undeliverable recs Real-time inventory filter; substitute recs (Instacart / Huyen prompt) [8][10]
Feedback loop / position bias Exploration traffic, position feature at train time (set to a constant at serve time), IPS
Seasonal shift (holidays, Prime Day) Faster retrains, recency-weighted features, short-window trending source
Training-serving skew Point-in-time feature snapshots, logging the features used at serving

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How would you compute item-item similarity for 10^8 items without O(N^2) work?
  • "Also bought" vs "also viewed" vs "frequently bought together": should these be one model or three? How do you tell complements from substitutes?
  • Why might cosine similarity on co-purchase counts over-recommend bestsellers? How do you fix it?
  • Purchases arrive days late. How do you build labels and train daily?
  • Click, add-to-cart or purchase: which do you optimize? How do you combine multi-task heads into one score?
  • How do you handle a brand-new product with no interactions, or a logged-out user?
  • How do you build "frequently bought together" so it shows a phone case for a phone, not another phone? What data separates complements from substitutes?
  • How do you avoid recommending a second TV to someone who just bought one, while still recommending detergent?
  • How do you rebuild the ANN index and item-item table without downtime? How stale is acceptable?
  • How do you blend sponsored products with organic recs without hurting trust?
  • How do you measure incrementality (would the user have bought it anyway)?
  • Diversity: how would you stop the carousel showing 10 phone cases of the same type?
  • How do you serve recs under 100 ms during Prime Day traffic spikes? What is the fallback?
  • How do you evaluate offline when the logging policy biased what users saw?
  • How would you add an LLM (for example, generating "why recommended" text or a semantic retrieval source)?

Portal comparison

Portal Framing Candidate gen Ranker Distinctive emphasis
Amazon papers [1][2][3] Item-anchored, scale-first Item-to-item CF table Light heuristics (in 2003) Offline table, online lookup; expected co-buy correction
ByteByteGo [13][14] Similar listings (session-based) + video home feed Session item embeddings + ANN; multi-source Two-tower / DNN Embeddings from co-occurrence in sessions; hybrid filtering
Educative Grokking [15] Netflix-style personalized recs CF/MF + content + embeddings Pointwise DNN Data-generation and staged funnel
alirezadir AIMLInterviews [8] Generic recsys template; Instacart replacement prompt User/item CF, MF, two-tower, content Pointwise / pairwise / listwise LTR 9-step formula, metrics catalogue
Hello Interview [17] Recsys pattern Multi-source retrieval Multi-stage ranking + re-ranking Interview delivery and tradeoff talk
Chip Huyen [10][20] Out-of-stock replacements, checkout speed Open-ended Open-ended Business framing, data and deployment issues

09. Design Similar Listings and Search Ranking for Airbnb (Listing Embeddings, Two-Sided Marketplace)

Prompt as usually given: "Design the 'similar listings' carousel on an Airbnb listing page", or "Design the system that returns the top 10 listings when a user searches for rentals in a location on Airbnb" (Chip Huyen, exercise 9 [5]). Variants: hotel or vacation-rental search ranking (Booking.com, Expedia, Vrbo style), "rental recommendation", Airbnb Experiences ranking [18], real-time in-session personalization.

Sourcing note (review pass, Oct 2026): medium.com, arxiv.org, doi.org and bytebytego.com did not resolve from the build sandbox and the web-search budget was spent. (fetched) = read for this chapter. (listed) = title, year and URL confirmed in a curated GitHub list (eugeneyan/applied-ml, alirezadir, ByteByteGoHq, wzhe06/Reco-papers); text not re-read. (ch-ref) = verified in an earlier chapter. Check paper numbers against the PDF before quoting.

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Surfaces (a) "Similar listings" carousel on the listing detail page. (b) Search results for location + dates + guests. (c) Real-time re-ranking within a session [1][2]
Business goal Bookings (conversion), not clicks. The marketplace has two sides, so the host must also accept the booking (host rejection counts as a negative) [1][3][16]
Functional Return the top K (about 10-20 per page, roughly 18 per search page) listings that are available for the dates, match the filters and are bookable assumption
Catalog About 4.5M active listings when the paper was written (2018), now more than 7M. Inventory is spread across about 100k+ cities or markets [1] / assumption
Training data About 800M search click sessions for listing embeddings [1]
Users Hundreds of millions of guests. Most book once or twice a year, so per-user history is sparse [1] / assumption
QPS About 10^4-10^5 search and carousel requests per second at peak assumption
Latency Under 200 ms p99 end to end for search. The ranking model has about 30-50 ms for roughly 1-2k candidates assumption
Freshness Clicks and skips within the session take effect within seconds. Embeddings retrain daily. Availability and price must be real-time [1]
Key constraints Listings are unique items with limited availability; a listing booked for one guest's dates is gone. Queries are geo-bound. Cold start: new listings appear every day [1][2]

Data & labels

Data Use Label / note
Click sessions (more than 30 s dwell, split on a 30-min gap) Listing embeddings Co-occurrence within window m=5 [1]
Booked sessions Global context for embeddings Booked listing = positive for every window [1]
Booking sessions (users x listing types) User-type / listing-type embeddings Long-term preference. Host rejections are explicit negatives [1]
Search impressions Ranker book=1, host contact=0.25, click=0.01, impression=0, host reject=-0.4 [1]
Skipped listings (shown above a click but not clicked) EmbSkipSim feature, negatives Implicit negative [1]
Reviews, ratings, calendar, host response Features Quality and trust signals

Features

Group Examples Freshness
Listing Price per night, type, capacity, amenities, review count/score, booking rate, photo quality Daily / hourly
Query Location, distance to the query center, check-in date, length of stay, guests, lead time Per request
Query x listing Distance to the map center, price relative to market median, fit to the date range Per request
User / guest Past booked price, trip type, user_type embedding Daily
Real-time session EmbClickSim, EmbSkipSim, EmbLongClickSim, EmbWishlistSim, EmbInqSim, EmbLastLongClickSim [1] Seconds
Host / marketplace Host acceptance rate, instant-book flag, response time, superhost, cancellation history Daily
Context Device, locale, seasonality, holidays Per request

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Option Pros Cons
Similar listings Rule: same city + price band + type Simple, no training Ignores taste and style
Similar listings Item CF (co-click/co-book matrix) Uses behaviour Sparse, poor cold start
Similar listings Skip-gram embeddings + booked global context + market negatives [1] Captures style and price within a market; cheap ANN Clicks are not bookings; needs cold-start fill
Similar listings GNN or two-tower with content (photos, text) Better for new and rare listings Heavier to train and serve
Ranking Hand-tuned scoring function Transparent Plateaus quickly
Ranking GBDT LambdaRank [1] Strong on tabular data Manual feature crosses
Ranking DNN, then two-tower DNN [2][3] Scales with data, learns crosses Hard to debug; many failed attempts reported [2]
Ranking Multi-task journey ranker [16] Optimizes the full booking funnel and penalizes bad outcomes Weighting the tasks is hard
Re-rank Greedy MMR / diversity network [4] Variety of location and price Can lower per-item relevance
Re-rank Learned diverse ranking: score each slot given the listings already placed above it [19] Diversity learned from bookings, not hand-tuned Sequential scoring costs latency

Loss functions

Model Loss Note
Listing embedding Skip-gram negative-sampling log loss, plus booked-global and market-negative terms [1]
User/listing type embedding Same, with host-rejection negatives Two-sided signal [1]
Ranker Pairwise LambdaRank (booked > not-booked within a search) Optimizes NDCG directly [1][2]
Multi-task Sum of per-milestone BCE terms (weighted), plus a negative-outcome head [16]

Offline metrics

Metric Model Note
Average rank of the eventually-booked listing Embeddings Rank the candidates by similarity to the last clicked listing [1]
NDCG@K / NDCU on booking Ranker Main gate for promotion [1][2]
Recall@K of ANN vs exact k-NN Retrieval Index quality
Coverage / new-listing share Retrieval and re-rank Cold start health
Calibration per market Ranker Required for multi-task combination

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Type Note
Bookings per search user, booking conversion Primary North star
Similar-carousel CTR and bookings from the carousel Surface 2018 paper: about +21% carousel CTR and about +4.9% more guests finding their booked listing in the carousel [1]
Host acceptance rate, cancellations Guardrail Two-sided health [16]
GMV / nights booked, price mix Business Watch for a drift toward cheaper or pricier listings
Search latency, zero-result rate Guardrail
Interleaving (team-draft) wins Fast pre-screen Airbnb uses interleaving before A/B [15]

Serving & latency budget (assumption, search, p99)

Step Budget Note
Parse query + geo lookup 10 ms Geocode, map bounds
Retrieval (geo index + ANN) 30 ms 2-5k candidates
Availability/price filter 30 ms Calendar service, the largest cost
Feature fetch (batch) 30 ms Online store + session store
Ranker inference 40 ms 1-2k listings, CPU/GPU batch
Re-rank + policy 10 ms Diversity, dedupe, boosts
Network/serialization slack 40 ms Total under 200 ms
Carousel (similar listings) under 50 ms Precomputed k-NN lists per listing, then filter by dates

Monitoring

Signal Why
Embedding drift (neighbour overlap from day to day) Daily retrain can reshuffle the similar lists
Feature freshness (session store lag) Real-time features silently going stale
Score distribution per market Calibration breaks in new or seasonal markets
New-listing impression share Cold-start starvation
Host rejection / cancellation of ranked bookings Marketplace quality
Latency and calendar service error rate Availability errors lead to empty or wrong results

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Click-optimized embeddings surface listings people click but do not book Booked listing as global context; rank on the booking label [1]
Similar listings from another city (cross-market leakage) Market negatives in training [1]; geo filter at serving
New listings never shown Cold-start embedding averaging [1]; exploration slots; new-listing boost
Position bias in logged labels Position as a training feature with dropout; set to 0 at serving [3]
Many near-duplicate results (same building or host) Diversity re-rank [4][19], host dedupe
Popular listings get booked out, so rankings go stale Real-time availability filter; demand-aware features
Hosts reject the guest P(host accept) head; host preference features [1][16]
Seasonality shift (holidays) Time-based splits, daily retrain, seasonal features [10]
Cold-start listing with no clicks yet Random walk with restart on the listing co-click graph, or content embedding, to seed neighbours [10]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why train embeddings on click sessions rather than booking sessions? What do the booked global context and the market negatives each fix?
  • How do you get an embedding for a listing created today (cold start)?
  • How do you evaluate embeddings offline before an A/B test?
  • How do you combine long-term preference (user_type) with in-session intent (EmbClickSim)?
  • What is the label for ranking, and why use graded labels (book, contact, click, host reject) instead of a single click label?
  • How do you handle the host side: rejections, acceptance rate, fairness to new hosts?
  • How do you correct position bias in the training data?
  • How do you enforce date availability and price filters without blowing the latency budget?
  • How would you add diversity (location, price) without losing bookings?
  • Pointwise vs pairwise vs listwise ranking: which one, and why?
  • How do you trade off guest conversion against host revenue and platform GMV?
  • How do you speed up ranking experiments? (interleaving, then A/B)
  • What changes for map search, flexible dates, or "I'm flexible" queries with no location?
  • How do you serve the similar-listings carousel: precomputed k-NN or online ANN?
  • How do you detect that a daily embedding retrain broke similarity?
  • How would you learn diversity from data instead of a hand-tuned MMR penalty? [19]
  • How would ranking change for Airbnb Experiences, which have far less traffic? [18]

10. Design a Visual Search / Image Similarity System (Pinterest Lens, Google Lens)

Prompt as usually given: "A user uploads a photo, or crops a region of a Pin. Return the most visually similar images, ranked." Variants: "shop the look" (photo to buyable products), camera search (Lens), near-duplicate detection, "more like this", and text-to-image search (CLIP-style).

Sourcing note: during review, only github.com was reachable from the build sandbox (arxiv.org, medium.com, bytebytego.com, igotanoffer.com and research.google failed DNS) and the web-search budget was spent. Tags: (fetched) = opened and checked in review; (ch-ref) = verified in another chapter of this atlas; (known) = canonical paper cited by arXiv ID, not re-fetched; (book) = structure from the published book. Company tags separate "built it" (engineering paper or post) from "asked it" (interview report).

Company Evidence Notes Source

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Input: image (photo or crop/bounding box). Output: top-K similar images, ranked [1]
Functional (opt.) Detect objects in the photo and let the user pick one; text + image query; shopping filter [17][21]
Out of scope (book version) Video; personalization (often added as a follow-up) [1]
Non-functional Low latency, high recall, safe results (no NSFW, no private Pins) [1]
Catalog size Billions of images (book uses about 100-200 billion for the Pinterest-style prompt) [1] (typical)
Users / QPS ~100M+ DAU; ~1K-10K visual QPS at peak typical assumption
Latency p99 under ~200-300 ms end to end; embedding ~20-50 ms on GPU; ANN ~10-30 ms typical assumption
Freshness New images searchable within minutes to hours (incremental index) [29]
Embedding size 64-512 dims float, or binarized / PQ-compressed for storage [18][26]

Diagram 3: model architecture

Diagram 3. Shared-weight (Siamese) image encoder trained with contrastive loss

  query image q          positive p            negatives n1 .. nk
       |                     |                        |
       v                     v                        v
 +-----------+         +-----------+           +-----------+
 | CNN / ViT |=========| CNN / ViT |===========| CNN / ViT |   shared weights
 | backbone  |         | backbone  |           | backbone  |   (ResNet, ViT,
 +-----+-----+         +-----+-----+           +-----+-----+    CLIP, DINOv2)
       | pooled              |                       |
       v                     v                       v
 +-----------+         +-----------+           +-----------+
 | proj head |         | proj head |           | proj head |   MLP -> d dims
 | + L2 norm |         | + L2 norm |           | + L2 norm |
 +-----+-----+         +-----+-----+           +-----+-----+
       | e_q                 | e_p                   | e_n1..e_nk
       +----------+----------+-----------+-----------+
                  v                      v
        +---------------------------------------------+
        | sim_i = cos(e_q, e_i) / temperature         |
        | softmax over {p, n1..nk}                    |
        | loss = cross-entropy(label = p)  (InfoNCE)  |
        +---------------------------------------------+

  Serving: only one tower is used. Index stores e_i for every catalog image;
  query computes e_q once, then ANN finds argmax cos(e_q, e_i).

ANN index sizing (FAISS guidance)

Scale Suggested index Note Source
100M-1B vectors IVF1048576_HNSW32 (2^20 lists, HNSW coarse quantizer) Training slow; plan 30-256 training vectors per centroid [33]
10M-100M IVF262144_HNSW32 Train on GPU, rest on CPU, or two-level clustering [33]
RAM-bound OPQ + PQ (4-bit FastScan) or RaBitQ (~1 bit/dim) All FAISS indexes live in RAM; HNSW costs ~(4d + 8M) bytes/vector [33]
GPU Plain IVF (IVF+HNSW not on GPU) Use for batch backfill / re-index [33]

Data & labels

Source Positive Negative Pros Cons Source
User interactions (query, clicked/saved result) Shown-not-clicked, random Matches product goal Position bias, noisy, cold start [1]
Self-supervision (image, augmented view) Other images in batch Free, unlimited labels Learns invariance, not "style" [1][23]
Image-text pairs (image, caption / Pin text) Other pairs in batch Enables text-to-image search Needs clean text [22]
Human annotation Same product / same object Different product High precision Costly, slow [1][21]
Product catalog Scene crop <-> catalog image of same SKU Other SKUs, same category Shopping relevance Needs detection + matching [18][21]

Features

Group Examples Used in
Raw pixels Resized 224x224 RGB, crop from detector box Encoder
Visual embedding d-dim vector (float / binary / PQ code) Retrieval, ranking
Image metadata Category, detected objects, OCR text, quality, resolution, NSFW score Filter, rank
Engagement Saves, clicks, CTR of result image Rank
Text Pin title, board name, alt text (text tower or CLIP) Rank, hybrid query
User (optional) Recent interests, locale Personalized re-rank

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Option Tradeoff Source
Baseline Hand-crafted features (SIFT, color histograms) + LSH Cheap, poor semantic similarity [16]
v1 ImageNet-pretrained CNN, take penultimate layer Easy, strong start; not tuned to task [16][20]
v2 Fine-tuned encoder with contrastive / triplet loss Task-aligned; needs labels and hard negatives [1][24]
v3 Multi-task / proxy-based metric learning, one embedding for many products One model to maintain; task balancing needed [18]
v4 Foundation encoders (CLIP, DINOv2) + fine-tuning Zero-shot text<->image; larger serving cost [22][31]
Detector front end Faster R-CNN / SSD style detector for crops Better object-level matches; extra latency [17][21]
ANN Tree / LSH / clustering (IVF) / graph (HNSW) / ScaNN (anisotropic VQ, SOAR) Recall vs memory vs latency [1][26][27][28][35]

Loss

Loss Form Note Source
Contrastive (softmax / InfoNCE) CE over sim(q, p) vs sim(q, n_i), with temperature Book's main choice; scales with in-batch negatives [1][25]
Triplet max(0, d(q,p) - d(q,n) + margin) Sensitive to negative mining [24]
Proxy-based softmax Classify embedding against learned class proxies Stable at scale; used by Pinterest [18]
SimCLR NT-Xent Two augmented views as positives Self-supervised pretraining [23]
CLIP symmetric CE Image<->text matching matrix Multimodal search [22]

Offline metrics

Metric What it measures Note
Recall@K Share of relevant items in top K Main retrieval metric; also measure ANN recall vs exact kNN
Precision@K Share of top K that is relevant Ignores order
MRR 1 / rank of first relevant result Good when one right answer (same product)
mAP Mean of average precision over queries Needs binary relevance; book's choice for binary labels [1]
nDCG Graded relevance, position discounted Needs graded labels [1]
Human side-by-side Raters compare old vs new results Used at Pinterest and Bing [16][19]

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Notes
CTR on results Primary engagement signal [1]
Saves / repins per search, add-to-cart (shopping) Stronger intent than clicks
Time spent on suggested images (daily/weekly) Book's secondary metric [1]
Search abandonment, zero-click rate Guardrail
Latency p50/p99, error rate Guardrail
A-B design User-level split; re-index needed per arm when the embedding space changes (two indexes side by side)

Serving & latency budget (typical)

Step Budget Notes
Upload + preprocess 20-40 ms Client-side resize to cut bytes
Object detection (opt) 20-40 ms GPU; can run on device
Embedding 15-40 ms GPU batching, FP16/INT8, distilled model
ANN retrieval 10-30 ms HNSW or IVF-PQ in memory, sharded; fan-out + merge
Filter + feature fetch 10-20 ms Feature store / KV lookups
Rank + re-rank 10-30 ms Light GBDT or MLP over ~300 candidates
Total ~100-200 ms server side Cache embeddings of popular query images

Monitoring

What Signal
Embedding drift Mean/variance of query embeddings, nearest-neighbor distance distribution
Index health Index size, staleness (time since last build), ANN recall on a probe set
Model version mismatch Query encoder version must equal index encoder version
Quality CTR, zero-result rate, human rating samples per week
Safety NSFW leakage rate in results, takedown latency
System p99 latency per stage, GPU utilization, shard hot spots

Failure modes

Failure Cause Mitigation
Duplicate-heavy results Many reposts of the same image Near-dup clustering, dedupe at re-rank
Wrong object matched Cluttered photo, background dominates Detector + user-selected crop [17]
Space mismatch after retrain Query and index encoders differ Full backfill, atomic index swap, version pinning
Popularity / position bias in labels Clicks reflect slot, not relevance Position feature, randomized slots, IPS weighting
Unsafe or private results Missing filters Pre-filter at index time + post-filter at serve
ANN recall loss Over-compressed PQ, poor graph params Tune nprobe/efSearch; exact rerank on top 1000
Cold new images Not yet indexed Streaming incremental index [29][30]
Domain shift (camera vs Pin photos) Training on clean Pins only Train on camera-query logs (Lens task) [17][18]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you build training data without human labels? Clicks vs augmentation vs image-text pairs.
  • Why contrastive loss over classification? What is the role of temperature and batch size?
  • How do you mine hard negatives, and what goes wrong if negatives are too hard (false negatives)?
  • Exact kNN over 10 billion vectors is too slow: compare LSH, IVF-PQ, HNSW and ScaNN on recall, memory and update cost.
  • How do you handle retraining when every catalog embedding must be recomputed (backfill cost, dual index)?
  • The user's photo has five objects. How do you know which one they mean?
  • How do you remove near-duplicates and keep the results diverse?
  • How would you add text to the query ("this chair but in blue")?
  • How do you personalize visual search without losing visual relevance?
  • How do you keep NSFW, private or copyrighted images out of results?
  • How do you compress embeddings for billions of images (binarization, PQ, lower dims)?
  • How do you evaluate offline when relevance is subjective (style vs exact product)?
  • How do you detect that the model degraded after a deployment?
  • How do you serve new images within minutes of upload?
  • How do you handle positional bias in click labels?
  • Your index is 1B x 256-d floats (~1 TB). How do you fit it in RAM per shard (PQ, RaBitQ, binarization) and what recall do you lose? [33]
  • How do you blend visual results with text search results for the same query (blender stage)? [5][17]

11. Design Multimodal Video Search (YouTube Search over Text + Visual + Audio)

Prompt as usually given: "A user types a text query. Return the most relevant videos from a catalog of about 1B, ranked." The multimodal version asks you to search what is inside the video (frames, speech, on-screen text), not only the title and tags. Variants: in-video moment search ("find the scene where..."), podcast/audio search, query-by-image or query-by-clip, and personalised search.

Sourcing note: during compilation and review the shared web-search budget was used up and most portal hosts, company blogs and arxiv.org could not be reached from the build sandbox. GitHub pages were fetched and read (re-checked in review: [3][4][5][6][7][8][11]). Each reference carries a tag. (fetched) means the page was read for this chapter. (ch-ref) means the URL was verified in another chapter of this atlas. (known) means a canonical paper cited by its arXiv ID. (book) means the structure is taken from the published book. Company tags separate "built it" (a paper or engineering blog exists) from "asked it" (an interview report). The "asked it" evidence is thin, so treat it as indicative only.

Company Evidence Notes Source
Google / YouTube Built it: no public paper on YouTube search itself; adjacent public work is YouTube recs [18][37], YouTube-8M video understanding [38], VideoPrism video encoder [39], Google Search [23]. The book chapter is "YouTube Video Search". Asked it (indicative): Google MLE loops include ML design Canonical framing of the problem [1][2][14][18][23][37][38][39]
Meta (FB / IG video, Reels) Built it: photo search, Rosetta (text in images and video), embedding-based retrieval in FB search. Asked it (indicative): Meta MLE loops include ML design Multimodal content understanding at billions scale [6][15][19][20][21]
Netflix Built it: in-video search (2023), listed in [7] Mirrors the "moment search" variant [7][22]
Spotify Built it: natural-language podcast episode search (2022), listed in [7] Mirrors the audio/ASR branch (dense + lexical hybrid) [7][24]

TikTok, Amazon Prime Video and similar tags were removed in review: no interview report or public system write-up could be confirmed.

Portals that cover it

Portal Treatment Link
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu, MLSDI), ch. 4 "YouTube Video Search" The fullest treatment. Visual search (two-tower, contrastive) plus text search (inverted index), fusion, re-ranking [1][2]
alirezadir AIMLInterviews, "Multimodal video search" case Book-style summary: 1B videos, 50M DAU, 10M labelled pairs, BERT + ViT/ViViT, MRR, watch time. Its MLSD template lists "Image/Video search" and "Multimodal search" as sample questions [3][4]
alirezadir, "Image search" case Same contrastive / ANN template for the visual tower [5]
Chip Huyen, ML Systems Design exercises Ex. 6 "return images associated with a query like in Google Images"; Ex. 14 trigger-word audio detection (audio branch) [8]
Educative "Grokking the ML Interview" / Khang Pham MLSD Search ranking (staged funnel, LTR) in [9]; Khang Pham's repo lists Airbnb search ranking and YouTube recs cases, not video search [9][10][11]
Exponent, Hello Interview, IGotAnOffer, Patrick Halina Generic MLSD framework, timing, rubric. Use them for delivery, not for this problem's content [12][13][14][16][17]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Text query in, ranked list of videos out. Match title/desc/tags and visual content [1][3]
Extended functional Speech (ASR) and on-screen text (OCR) searchable; optional moment timestamps assumption, [19][22]
Personalisation Not required in the book version; add as a follow-up [3]
Users 50M DAU [3]
Catalog 1B videos with title, description, tags [3]
Training data 10M annotated (video, text query) pairs [3]
Uploads ~500 hours of video per minute (YouTube-scale), so indexing must be streaming assumption
QPS 50M DAU x ~5 searches/day = ~3k QPS avg, ~10k peak assumption
Latency p99 under 200-300 ms end to end; ANN under 20 ms per shard assumption
Freshness New upload searchable by text in minutes, by visual/ASR embedding within ~1 h assumption
Languages Open question in the source. Assume multilingual text encoder [3]
Business goal Higher CTR and total watch time from search [3]

Stage Input -> output Typical budget Notes
Query understanding raw text -> normalised q, lang, intent 10-20 ms Spell-fix, synonym, safe-search intent
Query encode q -> 256-768-d vector 5-15 ms (GPU/CPU distilled) Cache top-1M head queries
Lexical retrieval q -> ~1k docs 20-40 ms BM25 over title/desc/tags/ASR/OCR [1][3]
Dense ANN (x3 indexes) q_emb -> ~500-1k each 10-20 ms each, parallel HNSW / ScaNN / FAISS-IVFPQ [25][26][27]
Fusion + filter ~3k -> ~400 5-10 ms RRF or learned weights [1][28]
Ranker ~400 -> top 100 30-60 ms GBDT or small cross-encoder; position-debiased labels [36]
Re-rank / policy 100 -> 20 5 ms Rules [1][3]
Total ~150-250 ms p99 assumption

Data & labels

Source Label Pros Cons Source
Human-annotated (query, video) pairs Relevant / graded 0-4 Clean, measures relevance Expensive; 10M pairs in book setup [1][3]
Search logs Click + watch > X s = positive; skip / quick-back = negative Free, huge, fresh Position bias, clickbait, popularity bias [3]
Title/desc as weak caption (title, video) pair Billions of pairs Noisy, SEO spam [29][33]
ASR transcript windows (speech, clip) pair Self-supervised alignment Speech often not about visuals [33][34]
Query reformulation q1 -> q2 within session Negative for q1 results Ambiguous assumption
Debiased clicks Clicks reweighted by inverse examination propensity Removes position bias from log labels Needs propensity estimates (randomisation or click model) [36]

Features

Group Features Used at
Query Tokens, language, length, intent class, query embedding, query popularity Retrieval + rank
Video content Frame embedding, audio/ASR embedding, OCR text, title/desc/tags, duration, language Indexing + rank
Query-video BM25 per field, cosine per modality, historical CTR / watch for (q, v) Rank
Video quality Views, like ratio, upload age, channel authority, policy flags Rank + policy
User (optional) Language, region, watch history embedding, subscriptions Personalised rank
Context Device, time, safe-search setting Filter + rank

Model choices

Component Baseline Better Advanced Tradeoff Source
Text matching BoW / TF-IDF / BM25 word2vec avg BERT-family encoder Semantics vs cost [1][3]
Video encoder Frame-level ViT + mean pool Frame ViT + temporal transformer (CLIP4Clip) Video-level ViViT Temporal info vs train/serve cost [3][30][31]
Audio ASR text into lexical index ASR text embedding Audio encoder in joint space Coverage vs index size [32][35]
Retrieval Inverted index only + dense two-tower ANN Per-modality ANN + learned fusion Recall vs memory [1][25]
Fusion Weighted sum of scores RRF Learned LTR on all scores Simplicity vs quality [1][28]
Ranker Hand-tuned weights GBDT LambdaMART Cross-encoder on top-50 Latency vs precision assumption
Pretraining ImageNet ViT CLIP image-text Video-text (HowTo100M, MIL-NCE, VideoCLIP) Data domain match [29][33][34]

Loss functions

Model Loss Notes Source
Dual encoder InfoNCE / softmax contrastive, in-batch negatives, temperature tau Symmetric (q->v and v->q) as in CLIP [3][29]
Dual encoder (noisy ASR pairs) MIL-NCE Several nearby clips count as positives [34]
Hard-negative mining Same loss with mined near-misses Mine from ANN results of the previous model assumption
Dual encoder, in-batch negatives Sampled softmax with logQ correction Popular videos appear as negatives too often; subtract log sampling prob [37]
Ranker LambdaRank / listwise softmax on graded labels Optimises nDCG directly assumption
Multi-objective rank BCE(click) + regression(watch time) Combine with weights at serve time [14]

Offline metrics

Metric Why Source
MRR Book choice: eval set is (video, text) pairs with one known positive [1][3]
Recall@k (k=100-1000) Retrieval stage: did the right video survive? [3]
Precision@k, mAP Considered, less fit for single-positive sets [3]
nDCG@10 Graded human labels at rank stage [5]
Per-modality ablation Recall@k with visual / audio / text index off assumption
Public benchmarks MSR-VTT, HowTo100M-style text-video retrieval R@1/5/10 [30][33]

Online metrics & A/B

Metric Verdict in source Note
CTR Rejected as primary: rewards clickbait, not relevance [3]
Video completion rate Rejected: partial watch can still be relevant [3]
Total watch time from search Chosen primary [3]
Successful-session rate, zero-result rate, query reformulation rate Add as guardrails assumption
Latency p99, abandonment Guardrails assumption
Human side-by-side relevance ratings Pre-launch gate Rater guideline style as in [40]

Serving & latency

Concern Choice Source
Index size 1B x 256-d fp32 = ~1 TB per modality; PQ to 32-64 B/vec = 32-64 GB [25][26]
ANN algorithm IVF-PQ (FAISS), ScaNN, or HNSW; shard by video id, replicate for QPS [25][26][27]
Encoder serving Query tower online (distilled, cached); video towers offline batch only [3]
Encoder upgrade Re-embed full catalog, dual-index, atomic swap; query + video towers must match assumption
Cold start (new upload) Lexical index in minutes; embeddings within ~1 h; freshness boost in re-rank assumption
Cost control Embed only sampled frames / shots; skip re-embedding low-view long tail assumption

Monitoring

Signal Alert on Source
Zero-result and low-confidence query rate Spike after index or model swap assumption
Embedding drift Mean cosine of query vs top-1 falling; distribution shift per language assumption
Index health Index lag behind uploads, shard recall vs brute-force sample [26]
Online metrics Watch time from search, CTR, reformulation rate by query segment [3]
Policy Rate of removed / borderline videos in top-10 assumption

Failure modes

Failure Symptom Mitigation
Clickbait thumbnails/titles High CTR, short watch Optimise watch time; quality features [3]
Keyword stuffing / tag spam Lexical path returns irrelevant videos Field weights, spam classifier, dense path cross-check
Visual-text mismatch Video ranked for words only spoken, never shown (or vice versa) Per-modality scores into ranker
ASR errors / low-resource languages Missed matches Multilingual encoders, phonetic fuzzy match
Stale index after encoder change Recall collapse Version-locked towers, dual-write, shadow eval
Head-query bias Long-tail queries poor Hard negatives, query rewriting, human labels on tail
Harmful / policy content Unsafe results for benign queries Filter + demotion stage, safe-search

What production systems add beyond the portal answer

Addition Why it matters Source
Position-bias correction on click/watch labels Log labels otherwise teach the ranker its own past order [36]
logQ sampling-bias correction for in-batch negatives Corrects popularity skew in two-tower training at YouTube scale [37]
Pretrained video foundation encoder (YouTube-8M, VideoPrism) Video tower is pretrained on large YouTube-derived data, then tuned for retrieval [38][39]
Shot-level index for moments Netflix indexes moments, not whole titles [22]
Hybrid dense + lexical for spoken content Spotify added semantic episode search alongside term matching [24]
Text in frames (OCR) as a searchable field Rosetta extracts text from images and video frames [20]
Human rater guidelines and side-by-side evals Launch gate independent of engagement metrics [40]
Query autocomplete and spell correction Many sessions start from suggestions; cuts zero-result queries assumption

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why not just use Elasticsearch on titles? What does the visual tower add, and for which queries?
  • Frame-level vs video-level encoder: how do you pick, and what does each cost to serve 1B videos? [3]
  • How do you fuse lexical and dense scores? Why RRF vs a learned weight? [1][28]
  • Why MRR offline and watch time online? Why not CTR? [3]
  • How do you get 10M labelled pairs? What if you only have click logs (position bias)?
  • How do you index audio: ASR text, audio embeddings, or both?
  • The video encoder changes. How do you re-embed 1B videos without downtime?
  • How do you make a video uploaded 5 minutes ago searchable?
  • One embedding with fused modalities vs separate ANN indexes per modality: tradeoffs?
  • How do you add personalisation without hurting relevance for new users?
  • How would you return timestamps (moment search) instead of whole videos? [22]
  • How do you handle multilingual queries against videos in another language?
  • How do you measure and reduce index memory (PQ, dimension reduction)? [25]
  • How do you stop the system surfacing harmful content for innocent queries?
  • How would you use an LLM or VLM here (query rewriting, captioning frames into text)?
  • Click logs are position-biased. How do you build unbiased labels? [36]
  • In-batch negatives over-penalise popular videos. How do you correct it? [37]
  • Would you pretrain the video tower yourself or start from a video foundation model? [38][39]

Production (Netflix, Meta, Spotify) [19][21][22][24] Hybrid lexical + embedding CLIP-style, OCR, ASR Learned Internal Moment-level index; text-in-video; NL podcast search
