Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional (inline) Ghost-text completion of the rest of the line or a block at the cursor; accept with Tab, partial accept, cycle alternatives [4][8]
Functional (next edit) Predict the next edit anywhere nearby (rename propagation, cursor jump); Copilot "next edit suggestions" is the same product shape [7]
Functional (apply) Merge an LLM-written edit sketch into the full file quickly (fast apply) [31]
Functional (chat / agent) Explain, refactor, generate tests, multi-file edits, run tools (terminal, tests) [12] typical assumption
Context Prefix + suffix of current file, open tabs, imports, repo symbols, recent edits [4][8][16]
Users ~1-20M daily developers; ~1-3 completion requests per developer-minute while typing typical assumption
QPS 10M devs x ~200 requests/day -> ~2B/day, ~25k avg, ~75k peak QPS typical assumption
Requests (Cursor) Cursor reports 400M+ Tab requests per day [7] [7]
Latency Inline: p50 < 200-300 ms, p95 < 500 ms end to end (else user types past it); chat: first token < 1 s [6] typical assumption
Quality Acceptance rate (shown -> accepted) and retained characters after N seconds are north-star [3][6]
Safety No secrets / PII in suggestions; public-code match filter (Copilot checks ~150-char matches and can block or cite them) [34]; block insecure patterns; respect content exclusions [34] typical assumption
Privacy Enterprise: no training on customer code, zero retention, regional processing typical assumption
Cost GPU cost per request must be tiny: small model for inline, large model for chat typical assumption

Diagram 3 - Model architecture

Decoder-only transformer with fill-in-the-middle prompt; retrieval augments the prefix.

  INPUTS (packed into ~2k-8k token budget, priority order)
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | 1 file path + language   2 retrieved snippets (neighbor tabs / repo index)    |
  | 3 imports / symbol defs  4 recent edits diff    5 PREFIX   6 SUFFIX           |
  +---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
       PSM format:  <PRE> ctx + prefix <SUF> suffix <MID>  -->  generate middle
                                          |
                                          v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | tokenizer (code BPE, whitespace-aware)                                        |
  +---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+
                                          v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | decoder-only transformer  (inline: 1-15B, distilled; chat: frontier LLM)      |
  | causal self-attn x N layers, MQA/GQA for small KV cache, RoPE long context    |
  +---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+
                                          v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | decoding: greedy / low-temp sampling, n=1-3 candidates, max ~64-256 tokens,   |
  | stop on <EOT>, block end, or suffix overlap; speculative draft model          |
  +---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+
                                          v
  OUTPUTS: middle text + per-token logprobs --> show/no-show decision (threshold on
           mean logprob or a small "will-accept" classifier on context features)

  Training objective: next-token CE on [PRE..SUF..MID] (FIM rate ~50-90%) [2]
  Optional: reward model / policy gradient on accept vs reject (Cursor Tab) [7]

Data & labels

Source Use Label / signal Caveat
Public permissive code (GitHub) Pretraining Next token / FIM middle (self-supervised) License, dedup, test-set contamination [1][9]
Synthetic FIM splits Infill training Random span = target middle Split at realistic points (line, block, AST node)
First-party monorepo Fine-tune (Google, Meta) Next token on internal code Internal APIs; leakage across teams [6][15]
IDE telemetry (opt-in) Online metrics, RL Accepted & retained = positive; rejected / deleted = negative Position bias, users typing past; strong privacy limits
Accepted-then-edited SFT target Final code after N seconds Noisy; edit may be unrelated
Unit tests (HumanEval, MBPP) Offline eval pass@k Function-level only, contaminated [1][22]
Repo-level benchmarks Offline eval Exact match / edit sim with cross-file context [11]

Features / context signals

Signal Where Why
Prefix and suffix around cursor Client Core FIM input [2]
File path, language, imports Client Disambiguates APIs; cheap and high value [4][8]
Neighboring tabs snippets (sliding window, Jaccard sim) Client Copilot's "neighboring tabs" improved acceptance [4][8]
Repo retrieval (symbols, embeddings, BM25) Server / local index Cross-file APIs; RepoCoder iterative retrieval [10]
Recent edits diff Client Next-edit prediction [7]
Cursor position type (mid-line, after comment, empty line) Client Trigger / show decision (contextual filter) [8]
User history accept rate, typing speed Client Show threshold, debounce tuning [8]
Semantic engine results (types, members) Language server Google hybrid: filter/rank by compiler info [6]
Codebase embeddings index, synced by file-hash Merkle tree Server, refreshed from client Chat / agent retrieval without re-uploading the whole repo [32]

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Option Pros Cons
Baseline N-gram / language-server symbol completion Instant, exact Single tokens only
v1 Pretrained code LM, left-to-right only Simple Ignores suffix; poor mid-file
v2 FIM-trained decoder (Codex/StarCoder/Code Llama/DeepSeek-Coder/Qwen-Coder) [2][9][13][17][18] Uses suffix; standard today Needs realistic FIM splits
v3 + retrieval of repo context [4][10] Cross-file correctness Token budget, retrieval latency
v4 Distill / quantize large -> small for inline Meets <300 ms Some quality loss
v5 Fine-tune on accept/reject (DPO / online RL) [7] Optimizes what users value Feedback loop bias, reward hacking (show less)
Chat / agent Frontier LLM + tools + agent loop [12] Multi-file tasks Seconds-minutes latency, cost

Loss / objectives

Objective Formula (words) Notes
Causal LM Cross-entropy of next token Pretraining
FIM Same CE on permuted PRE/SUF/MID document; FIM rate up to ~90% without hurting left-to-right [2] Key for mid-file completion
SFT on prod prompts CE on middle only, prompt format equals production Closes train/serve skew
Show/no-show classifier Binary log loss on accepted vs not Controls noise and cost
Preference / RL DPO on (accepted, rejected) pairs, or policy gradient with reward = accept - penalty for rejected show [7] Must penalize showing bad suggestions
Distillation KL between teacher and student token distributions For small inline model

Offline metrics

Metric Measures Note
pass@k (HumanEval, MBPP) Functional correctness of k samples Unbiased estimator in [1]; contaminated
Exact match / edit similarity of middle Token-level fidelity on held-out repos Cheap; misses equivalent code
Cross-file EM (CrossCodeEval) [11] Retrieval usefulness Repo-level
Replay acceptance proxy Predict accept on logged contexts Off-policy, biased
Syntax / compile rate Parse and type-check success Uses language server
Latency, tokens/s, model size Serving fit Hard gate
SWE-bench resolve rate [12] Agent end-to-end For agent variant; use the human-validated Verified subset
Contamination-free eval (LiveCodeBench) [35] Problems released after model cutoff Fixes HumanEval leakage

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Definition Direction
Acceptance rate accepted / shown Up; strongest predictor of perceived productivity [3]
Retained characters Chars of accepted code still present after 30s-10m Up; guards against accept-then-delete [3][8]
Fraction of code written by AI AI chars / total chars committed Up [6]
Shown rate / suggestions per hour Volume Not blindly up (noise) [7]
Cancel / timeout rate Request cancelled by keystroke before response Down
p50/p95 latency Keystroke -> ghost text Down
Guardrails Secret leaks, public-code matches, vuln patterns ~0
Long-term Retention, DAU, survey (SPACE), PR throughput Up

Serving & latency budget (inline, p95 ~400 ms; typical assumption)

Step Budget Technique
Debounce + trigger 50-150 ms (not counted in model time) Skip mid-word, cancel stale requests
Client context + prompt build 10-20 ms Precomputed local index, Jaccard windows [8]
Network to region 30-60 ms Edge regions, HTTP/2 streaming, keep-alive
Gateway, auth, filters 10 ms In-memory policy cache
Repo retrieval (optional) 20-40 ms Precomputed index; can be client-side
Prefill (2-8k tokens) 30-80 ms Prefix/KV cache reuse across keystrokes, GQA
Decode (~20-60 tokens) 50-150 ms Small model, speculative decoding [14], int8/fp8, continuous batching (vLLM) [19]
Post-processing + filters 10-20 ms Truncation at block end, public-code filter
Apply edit (chat/agent only) ~1 s for a few hundred lines Speculative edits: the existing file is the draft, so most tokens are verified, not generated [31]

Monitoring

What Signal Action
Quality Accept rate, retained chars by language / IDE / tenant Alert on drop; roll back model
Latency p50/p95/p99, timeout and cancel rate Autoscale GPUs, shrink context
Cost GPU-sec per accepted char Route, cache, tune show threshold
Safety Secret detector hits, public-code match rate, insecure patterns Block, retrain filter
Drift New languages / frameworks, library version changes Refresh fine-tune data
Client health Extension crash rate, version skew of prompt format Force-upgrade, server-side compat

Failure modes

Failure Cause Mitigation
Suggestion arrives too late Long prompt, cold KV cache Cancel-on-keystroke, prefix cache, smaller model
Repeats suffix / overlaps existing code No FIM or bad truncation FIM training, suffix-overlap trimming [16]
Hallucinated APIs Missing cross-file context Repo retrieval, language-server validation [6][10]
Verbatim license-sensitive code Memorization Dedup training data, public-code match filter
Secret / PII leakage Secrets in training data or context Scrub data, redact prompts, output detector
Insecure code (SQLi, weak crypto) Learned from public code Security filter, static analysis on suggestion
Distracting noise Showing low-confidence suggestions Show/no-show model; RL penalizing rejects [7]
Accept-rate gaming Optimizing short trivial completions Track retained chars and AI-written fraction
Train/serve skew Prompt format in training differs from client SFT on logged production prompts
Prompt injection (agent) Malicious repo files / README Sandbox tools, confirm destructive actions

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you decide when to trigger a request and when to show a suggestion at all?
  • How do you build the prompt under a fixed token budget? What gets priority?
  • Why fill-in-the-middle, and how do you create FIM training examples? [2]
  • How do you bring in cross-file context with <50 ms extra latency? Client vs server index?
  • Acceptance rate vs retained characters vs pass@k: which is your north star and why? [3]
  • How would you hit p95 < 500 ms at ~75k QPS? Batching, KV cache reuse, speculative decoding?
  • One model or two (small inline + large chat)? How do you route?
  • How do you use accept/reject telemetry to improve the model without bias or reward hacking? [7]
  • How do you avoid regurgitating licensed code or leaking secrets?
  • How do you support enterprise customers who forbid training on their code?
  • How would you evaluate a new model offline when HumanEval is contaminated?
  • How do you handle a newly released library the model has never seen?
  • How would you extend this to next-edit prediction or an autonomous coding agent? [7][12]
  • How do you keep client prompt format and server model in sync across extension versions?
  • What do you log, and what is the privacy story?
  • How do you index a large repo for retrieval and keep it fresh as files change? [32]
  • How do you apply a model-written edit to a 1,000-line file in about a second? [31]
  • How do you detect and handle suggestions that match public code (block vs cite)? [34]

Portal comparison

Portal / source Framing Emphasis Gap
ByteByteGo GenAI book (Smart Compose chapter) [23] Prefix-only text completion Triggering, beam search, latency, perplexity/ExactMatch No suffix/FIM, no repo context
Copilot reverse-engineering (Thakkar) [8] Real system teardown Prompt wishlist, neighboring tabs, contextual filter, retained-text telemetry Client-side only; no training

Chip Huyen / generic GenAI frameworks [26][27][28] Generic LLM app Context construction, caching, guardrails, eval Not code-specific

27. Design a Voice Assistant / Speech Recognition Pipeline (Alexa, Siri)

Source note: pages re-fetched on 2026-10-14 are marked "(read)" in References. Apple, Google, arXiv, Meta and Netflix domains failed DNS lookup in this run, and the search budget was spent; those primary sources are marked "(not re-fetched)". Rows marked "(assumption)" are typical interview defaults.

Company tags

Company / context What links it to this problem Source
Amazon (Alexa, Echo) Product owner of the canonical "Design Alexa" system: wake word on device, cloud ASR -> NLU -> skills -> TTS (assumption; interview reports unverified)
Apple (Siri, "Hey Siri") Two-pass on-device DNN voice trigger plus speaker check, then server ASR [1] [2]
Google (Assistant, Gboard voice typing) All-neural on-device streaming RNN-T recognizer [3] [4]
Walmart (voice shopping) Unified multi-task model for several virtual assistants; voice reorder flow [12] [19] [20]
Meta (SeamlessM4T) Adjacent: multimodal speech translation model, not an assistant [12] [18]
OpenAI / NVIDIA Whisper and NeMo (Parakeet, Canary, Nemotron streaming ASR) are the usual open baselines [8] [10]

Portals that cover it

  • alirezadir's MLSD guide lists "Speech Recognition Systems" as a topic (MFCC features, acoustic modeling, HMMs, CTC) and "Chatbot system" / "Language identification system" as sample questions. No full speech case study [5].
  • khangich/machine-learning-interview has no speech case study [6].
  • Engineer1999's case-study list has the production references (Walmart virtual assistants and voice reorder, Netflix speech/music detection, Meta SeamlessM4T). No Alexa, Siri or wake-word entry [12].
  • ByteByteGo / Aminian, Exponent, Educative, Hello Interview: no dedicated speech chapter confirmed. Candidates apply the generic framework (see Chapter 1). (assumption)
  • Open-source production toolkits act as the "solution key": WeNet [9], NeMo [10], openWakeWord [11], Whisper [8].

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Wake word -> transcribe -> understand intent and slots -> execute skill -> spoken reply [1] (assumption)
Secondary Multi-language, far-field (3-5 m), barge-in, follow-up mode, speaker ID / personalization [2] (assumption)
Devices 100M-500M devices. About 1B utterances/day (assumption) (assumption)
QPS About 10k average and 30-50k peak ASR streams. Each stream is long-lived over 2-10 s (assumption)
Latency Wake detect under 200 ms. Partial transcripts every 80-200 ms. End-of-speech to first TTS audio under 1 s [10] (assumption)
Accuracy WER 5-8% on assistant traffic. Wake word: FRR under 5%, FA under 0.5/hour (openWakeWord targets) [11]
Power Always-on detector runs on a DSP or low-power core at a few mW [1]
Privacy Audio stays on device until the trigger fires. Opt-in audio retention for training [1] (assumption)
Vocabulary Open vocabulary plus 100k+ contact, song and skill entities that need contextual biasing [4] (assumption)

  • Whisper is an encoder-decoder Transformer that handles transcription, translation, language ID and VAD as token tasks. Model sizes run from 39M to 1.55B parameters [8].
  • A common hybrid: keep the on-device wake word and streaming ASR, and route long-tail queries that NLU rejects to an LLM. (assumption)

Data & labels

Model Positive / label Negative / hard negatives Source of labels
Wake word Utterances of "Alexa" / "Hey Siri" across accents and distances TV, music, similar words ("election", "Alexis") Accepted triggers + human audit, synthetic TTS [11]
ASR Audio -> verbatim transcript n/a Human transcription, pseudo-labels from a teacher, weak labels
NLU Utterance -> domain, intent, slot spans Out-of-domain utterances Annotators, grammar-generated data, user corrections
Endpointer End-of-query frame Mid-sentence pauses Forced alignment of transcripts
Implicit Task success, no rephrase within 30 s Barge-in, "no, I said..." Interaction logs (assumption)

Features

Stage Features
Frontend Log-mel filterbanks (80-dim), beamformed channel, AEC residual
Wake word Frame posteriors, speaker embedding (d-vector), device playback state
ASR context Contact list, recent media, installed skills, locale, device type (biasing)
NLU Tokens, ASR confidence, n-best, previous turn intent, device capabilities, time
Skill ranking Skill popularity, user history, entity match score, latency

Model choices

Component Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
Wake word GMM-HMM keyword / small DNN DS-CNN two-stage + speaker verification [1] [2] Size and power vs. false accepts
ASR Hybrid DNN-HMM + n-gram LM + WFST Streaming Conformer RNN-T + 2nd-pass rescorer [3] [4] [7] [13] E2E is smaller and fits on device but is harder to bias
ASR (offline) CTC encoder Attention enc-dec (Whisper) [8] Accuracy vs. no streaming
Unified Separate streaming / full models U2 / WeNet: one model, CTC + attention rescoring [9] One model to maintain
NLU Per-domain CRF + logistic regression Joint BERT intent + slot, multi-task [16] [19] Latency vs. accuracy
DM Rules + state machine Learned policy / LLM fallback Control vs. coverage
TTS Concatenative Neural (Tacotron/FastSpeech + vocoder) Naturalness vs. compute

Loss functions

Model Loss
Augmentation SpecAugment [14]; SSL pretraining (wav2vec 2.0 [15])
Wake word Frame-level cross-entropy, or max-pooling loss over the keyword window
ASR RNN-T loss (marginalizes over alignments). CTC as auxiliary. CE for the attention decoder. MWER fine-tuning
Distillation KL(teacher logits, student logits) + RNN-T
NLU CE(intent) + token CE or CRF NLL(slots), weighted sum
Speaker ID GE2E / triplet loss on embeddings

Offline metrics

Component Metric
Wake word FRR at a fixed FA/hour (DET curve), detection latency
ASR WER, entity/named-WER, sliced by accent, noise, far-field, domain. Real-time factor
Endpointer EP50/EP90 latency, early-cutoff rate
NLU Intent accuracy, slot F1, semantic error rate (SemER)
End-to-end Task completion on replayed golden set, latency p50/p90/p99

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Meaning
Task success / user satisfaction (predicted) North star. Model-estimated from implicit signals
Rephrase / repeat rate Proxy for ASR or NLU error
Barge-in / abandonment Wrong or slow response
False wake rate per device-day Privacy and annoyance guardrail
Latency (user-perceived) End-of-speech -> first audio
Engagement Daily active devices, queries/device

Serving & latency budget

Step Budget (assumption) Where
Wake word stage 1 + 2 50-200 ms after end of keyword Device DSP / AP
Network uplink 50-100 ms Edge PoP
Streaming ASR Partials in about 150 ms. Final 100-200 ms after endpoint GPU/CPU pool. Batched streams
Endpointing 200-500 ms of trailing silence (adaptive) Device or cloud
NLU + entity resolution 30-50 ms CPU
DM + skill call 100-300 ms (third-party skill timeout) Microservices
TTS first chunk 50-150 ms GPU, streaming
Total Under 1 s from end-of-speech to first audio
  • On-device ASR removes the network hop and works offline. Google shipped an all-neural on-device RNN-T recognizer for Gboard (2019, about 80 MB after quantization) [3] [4].
  • NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-ASR-Streaming (cache-aware FastConformer) exposes a tunable latency of 80 ms to 1 s and 240-2400 concurrent streams per H100 [10].

Monitoring

Signal Alert on
WER on daily human-transcribed sample Regression by locale or device
False wake rate Spikes. A TV ad saying "Alexa" causes mass false wakes
Rephrase rate per intent New intent failures or a catalog change
Latency p99 per stage Drift caused by a skill or GPU saturation
Input drift SNR distribution, language mix, new device firmware
Out-of-vocabulary entities New song or celebrity names (biasing lists need refresh)

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
False accepts from media / ads Cloud verifier, audio fingerprint blocklist of broadcast ads, speaker ID
Accent / dialect bias in WER Slice metrics, targeted data collection, per-locale models
Rare entity misrecognition Contextual biasing FST, personal LM, NLU fuzzy entity resolution
Early endpointing cuts the user off Learned endpointer with a semantic completeness signal
ASR error cascades into wrong action Pass n-best + confidence to NLU. Confirm destructive or purchase actions
Privacy incidents (accidental recordings) On-device processing, retention limits, opt-in review
Cold start for new language Multilingual pretrain + SSL, synthetic TTS data

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you keep false wakes under X per day without hurting recall? Where does each stage run?
  • Why use two-stage wake word detection instead of one larger model? What is the power budget?
  • What happens when a TV ad says the wake word to millions of devices at once?
  • Hybrid HMM vs. CTC vs. RNN-T vs. attention: which works for streaming, and why?
  • How do you recognize a user's contact names or a song released yesterday (contextual biasing)?
  • How do you decide the user has finished speaking (endpointing), and what does it trade off?
  • What runs on device and what in the cloud? Offline mode? Model compression (int8, pruning, distillation)?
  • How do you get labels at scale without transcribing everything? (Pseudo-labels, implicit feedback, SSL)
  • How do you evaluate fairness across accents and dialects?
  • How do you propagate ASR uncertainty into NLU?
  • How would you add a new language with only 100 hours of labeled data?
  • How do you A/B test an ASR model when the north-star metric is task success?
  • How do you personalize to a household's voices while protecting privacy (federated learning)?
  • Would you replace the cascade with a speech-LLM? Latency, cost and controllability?
  • How do you scale GPU serving for long-lived streaming connections (stickiness, batching)?

Components often missed

Component Why it matters Source
Device arbitration Several Echo devices hear one wake word; only the best-SNR device answers (assumption)
Device-directed speech detection Follow-up mode without the wake word needs a "talking to me?" classifier (assumption)
Language ID Picks the ASR model in multilingual homes [5] [8]
Voice activity detection Gates ASR compute and drives endpointing [8]
Punctuation, casing, inverse text normalization "set alarm for seven thirty" -> "7:30" before NLU and display [10] (assumption)
Acoustic features and HMM/CTC basics Portal syllabus asks for MFCCs, acoustic models, CTC [5]
Streaming GPU capacity Concurrent streams per GPU sets fleet size [10]

Extra follow-ups: How do you pick which device answers when three Echos hear "Alexa"? How do you support follow-up questions without the wake word and without false accepts?

Source Framing Distinctive emphasis
Apple ML Research (Hey Siri) [1] [2] Voice trigger as the core problem Two-pass on-device DNN, thresholds, speaker vector, false-trigger mitigation
Google Research / He et al. [3] [4] On-device streaming ASR RNN-T, quantization, latency vs. server models
OpenAI Whisper [8] Single multitask model Weak supervision at scale, robust offline transcription, not streaming
WeNet / NeMo [9] [10] Production toolkits Unified streaming/non-streaming, CTC + attention rescoring, latency knobs

alirezadir / generic MLSD portals [5] NLP topic list (speech recognition, chatbot, language ID) Feature extraction, acoustic modeling, HMM, CTC; no end-to-end assistant design

28. Design a Machine Translation System (Google Translate)

Prompt as usually given: "Design Google Translate: translate text between any two of N languages", or "Design a system that auto-translates user-generated content (reviews, posts, messages) into the viewer's language". Variants: "Translate a whole web page or document while keeping its formatting", "Add a low-resource language with almost no parallel data", "Real-time speech-to-speech translation", "Translate product listings for an e-commerce marketplace".

Compilation note: in both the drafting and review runs the shared web-search budget was used up and only github.com resolved (arxiv.org, research.google, blog hosts and portal sites did not). Sources marked (fetched) were read directly; the review run re-read [10][15][16][21][22][24][25][26][27]. Sources marked (ch-ref) were verified in earlier chapters of this atlas. Sources marked (known; not fetched) are well-known papers or posts cited from prior knowledge; check them before relying on exact numbers. Scale numbers marked "typical assumption" are interview estimates, not published figures.

Company tags

Company Basis Production system it mirrors
Google Builds Google Translate; published GNMT [1], zero-shot multilingual NMT [3], massively multilingual NMT [4] and the "next thousand languages" work [5] Single multilingual Transformer/hybrid model, wordpieces, TPU serving, quantized inference
Meta Builds feed/message translation; published M2M-100 [7] and NLLB-200 (200 languages, 54.5B MoE + distilled 1.3B/600M) [6][21] Many-to-many model, distilled for serving, used for Facebook/Instagram/Wikipedia content
Amazon (AWS Translate), Microsoft (Translator), Apple (Translate app, on-device), DeepL Ship MT products (tag reflects the product, not verified interview reports) Same cascade: lang-ID -> segment -> NMT -> post-process
Airbnb, LinkedIn, Booking.com Translate user-generated listings/reviews/posts in product (tag reflects the product; interview reports not verified) Batch + on-demand translation of UGC with caching

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Translate text (and docs/web pages) between any pair of N languages; auto-detect source language; alternatives per phrase; user feedback ("suggest an edit") [1][23]
Languages 100-250 languages -> 10k-60k directions; one model must cover all of them Google 133 (2022) + 110 via PaLM 2 (2024); NLLB 200 [5][6][31]
Traffic ~100B+ words/day reported for Google Translate (2016); assume ~50k-200k QPS peak of short segments known; not fetched / typical assumption
Latency p95 < 200-300 ms for a short sentence (interactive); documents can be async typical assumption
Quality Beat previous model on BLEU/chrF/COMET and human MQM/SxS per direction; no regressions on high-traffic pairs [1][16][17]
Robustness Keep named entities, numbers, markup, formatting; no hallucination; handle code-switching, typos [1][4]
Safety No added toxicity; gender-bias handling; profanity masking optional typical assumption
Cost GPU/TPU minutes dominate; cache hit rate 20-40% on popular segments typical assumption
Freshness New model monthly/quarterly; glossary/terminology updates live typical assumption

Data & labels

Source Volume (typical) Label quality Notes
Licensed / curated parallel (UN, EU, subtitles, books) 10M-1B pairs for high-resource pairs High Domain skew (legal, formal)
Web-mined bitext (sentence-embedding alignment) Billions of pairs Medium/noisy Needs alignment-score + lang-ID filtering [4][6]
Back-translated monolingual Unlimited Synthetic source, real target Sampled BT beats beam BT; tag <BT> [9]
Human post-edits / "suggest an edit" Small High but adversarial risk Use for eval + fine-tune after vetting
Implicit signals (copy, share, re-query, edit distance) Huge Weak Proxy labels for QE / online metrics
Human ratings (MQM, side-by-side) Thousands per direction Gold Eval only; expensive [17]
Benchmark sets (FLORES-200, NLLB-MD, Toxicity-200) ~1-3k sentences per language Gold Held-out eval; decontaminate web data against them [21]

Features / inputs

Input Use
Source subword tokens (BPE / SentencePiece) Encoder input [8][10]
Target-language token <2xx> Selects output language in one shared model [3]
Detected source language + confidence Routing; ambiguity handling
Domain / formality / glossary tags Controlled generation, terminology constraints
Document context (previous sentences) Pronouns, consistency (doc-level variant)
Markup / entity placeholders Preserved and restored after decode
User locale, app surface Routing, gender/formality defaults

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Model Pros Cons
Baseline 0 Phrase-based SMT Interpretable, small data ok Poor fluency; replaced by NMT [1]
Baseline 1 Seq2seq LSTM + attention (GNMT: 8+8 layers, wordpieces) [1] Big quality jump (~60% fewer errors vs PBMT on some pairs) Sequential, slow training
Standard Transformer encoder-decoder [2] Parallel training, SOTA quality; hybrids (Transformer enc + RNN dec) used in production [19] Quadratic attention on long docs
Scale One multilingual model with <2xx> token [3][4] Transfer to low-resource, zero-shot, one deployment Capacity dilution ("curse of multilinguality") for high-resource pairs
Capacity Sparse MoE (NLLB 54.5B) [6] More capacity at same FLOPs Serving memory, load balancing
Serving Distilled student, deep-encoder / shallow-decoder, int8 [11][20][22] 3-10x cheaper, small quality loss Extra training stage
Frontier LLM translation (prompted / fine-tuned); Google used PaLM 2 to add 110 languages [31] Doc context, style control, rare phenomena Cost, latency, hallucination/omission
Decoding QE re-rank or MBR over n-best/samples (COMET-MBR with CometKiwi QE) [15] Higher human-rated quality than beam top-1 N x scoring cost; metric overfitting

Loss / objectives

Objective Where Notes
Token cross-entropy, label smoothing 0.1 Main NMT training Teacher forcing [2]
MoE load-balance auxiliary loss MoE layers Prevents expert collapse [6]
Sequence-level KD (train on teacher beam output) Student Simpler targets, enables greedy decode [11]
Denoising / MASS-style objective Monolingual data, low-resource [5]
Minimum-risk training / RL on BLEU or COMET Optional fine-tune Watch metric gaming
QE regression (MSE vs DA/MQM scores) QE re-ranker CometKiwi-style [15]

Offline metrics

Metric Type Use / caveat
BLEU (sacreBLEU) n-gram overlap Standard, reproducible signatures; weak correlation at high quality [12][13]
chrF / chrF++ char n-gram Better for morphologically rich languages; FLORES/NLLB headline [6]
COMET Neural, reference-based Best correlation with humans in WMT; ship/no-ship [14][18]
BLEURT Neural, reference-based Google-trained metric [16]
CometKiwi / QE Reference-free Runtime re-rank, monitoring of live traffic [15]
MQM / side-by-side human eval Human Final gate on top directions [17]
Added-toxicity rate (Toxicity-200 word lists) Rules Catches toxicity introduced by the model, per language [21]
Targeted test suites Rules Numbers, named entities, gender, toxicity, hallucination, omission

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Signal
Copy / share rate of output Usefulness
Re-query / edit rate, "suggest edit" rate Dissatisfaction proxy
Thumbs up/down rate Explicit quality
Session length, follow-up searches Engagement
p50/p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k chars Guardrails
Live QE score distribution per pair Quality drift without references
UGC variant: engagement on translated posts/reviews Downstream value

Serving & latency budget (p95 ~250 ms short segment; typical assumption)

Step Budget Technique
Gateway + auth 10 ms
Lang-ID + segmentation + masking 5-10 ms fastText-style classifier, rules
Cache / translation memory lookup 5 ms Key includes model version
Queue + dynamic batching 10-30 ms Bucket by length and pair
Encoder 10-20 ms int8/fp16/bf16 or AWQ int4, layer fusion, padding removal, batch reordering [22]
Beam decode (k=4, ~20 tokens) 60-120 ms KV cache, shallow decoder, speculative decoding
QE re-rank n-best 15-30 ms Small QE model; skip for cached/high-confidence
Post-process + policy 5-10 ms Detok, restore entities, filters

Other: per-pair model tiers; on-device small models for offline mode (Apple/Google offline packs); async batch pipeline for documents and UGC backfills.

Monitoring

What How
Quality drift per language pair Live QE scores, sampled human eval weekly
Input drift Lang-ID mix, length, script, new slang/entities
Hallucination / omission Length-ratio alarms, attention coverage, QE outliers
Toxicity / bias incidents Classifier on outputs, user reports
Latency / cost p95 by pair and tier, GPU utilization, cache hit rate
Feedback poisoning Rate-limit and cluster suspicious "suggest edit" submissions

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Hallucination on short/odd input (repeats, unrelated text) QE gate, copy-through for untranslatable strings, length-ratio check
Omission of clauses Coverage checks, QE, MBR decoding
Wrong source language (code-switching, short text) Lang-ID confidence threshold, show "Detected X" with override
Named entities / numbers mistranslated Placeholder masking, constrained decoding
Gender bias ("the doctor" -> masculine) Gender-specific alternatives shown to user
Low-resource pairs poor quality Pivot through English, BT, multilingual transfer [4][5]
Off-target language (zero-shot outputs wrong language) Target-lang check on output, more direct-pair data [3][7]
Test-set contamination from web mining Decontaminate against FLORES/WMT sets
Toxic or adversarial training data Toxicity filtering in data pipeline [6]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • One multilingual model vs one model per pair: what breaks at 200 languages (N^2 models)?
  • How does the target-language token enable zero-shot translation, and when does it fail?
  • How do you get training data for a language with almost no parallel text?
  • Why sample (not beam) when generating back-translation data?
  • BLEU went up but users complain: which metrics and human evals do you trust and why?
  • How do you evaluate quality on live traffic with no reference translations?
  • How do you hit p95 < 250 ms at 100k QPS? Batching, distillation, quantization, caching.
  • How do you preserve HTML/markup, numbers and named entities?
  • How do you handle gender ambiguity and bias in the output?
  • How do you detect and prevent hallucinations and omissions?
  • When would you route to an LLM instead of the NMT model, and how do you cap cost?
  • How do you use "suggest an edit" feedback safely (spam, poisoning)?
  • How would you add document-level context or formality control?
  • How do you roll out a new model without regressing any of 10k+ directions?
  • Speech-to-speech variant: cascade (ASR -> MT -> TTS) vs direct model tradeoffs?
  • Offline mode: how do you fit a pair model on a phone (size, int8, vocab) and keep it fresh?
  • When is MBR / QE re-ranking worth N-times scoring cost, and how do you avoid metric gaming? [15]
  • How do you measure added toxicity across 200 languages? [21]

Generic MLSD frameworks (Hello Interview, Exponent, Educative) [28][29][30] 6-step framework Requirements -> data -> model -> eval -> serving -> monitoring No MT-specific depth

29. Design a Document Understanding / Invoice Extraction System (OCR + Layout + LLM)

How the prompt is usually worded: "Design a system that takes scanned or digital invoices (PDF, photo, email attachment) and returns structured fields (vendor, invoice number, dates, totals, tax, line items), then posts them to an ERP / accounts-payable system." Variants: "Receipt scanning for expense reports", "Intelligent document processing (IDP) like AWS Textract or UiPath Document Understanding", "KYC / ID-document extraction", "Parse PDFs into Markdown/JSON for an LLM pipeline", "Insurance-claim form digitization".

Source note (review pass, 2026-10): github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com resolved; uber.com, docs.aws.amazon.com, docs.uipath.com and arxiv.org were blocked by the proxy.

  • (fetched): read in a fetch run.
  • (listed in [n]): the URL appears in curated list [n], which was fetched.
  • (ch-ref): verified in ch. 01 or ch. 24 of this atlas.
  • (not opened): canonical URL cited from memory. Check before relying on it.

Numbers marked "approx." or "assumption" are typical values, not sourced figures.

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Ingest PDF, TIFF, JPG, email. Classify doc type. Extract header fields + line-item table. Normalize (dates, currency, vendor ID). Validate. Send low-confidence docs to human review. Post to ERP [9][10]
Output schema ~20-40 header fields + N line items (description, qty, unit price, amount, tax code) typical assumption; CORD has 5 superclasses / 42 subfields [12]
Volume 1M docs/day at a large enterprise or BPO. ~12 docs/s average, ~50/s peak. ~2-3 pages per doc assumption
Latency Async batch: p95 under 60 s end-to-end. Sync API (receipt app): p95 under 3-5 s per page assumption
Accuracy Field-level F1 of 0.95 or higher on key fields. Totals exact-match 99%+ after validation. Straight-through-processing (STP) rate 70-90% typical target
Vendors / templates 100k+ vendors, long-tail layouts. New layouts appear daily assumption
Languages 50-100+ scripts. Handwriting is a minority but real assumption; PP-OCR covers 50-109 languages [19]
Compliance PII and bank details: encryption, retention limits, audit trail, region pinning typical assumption
Cost Target under $0.01-0.05 per page. LLM calls only where needed assumption

Diagram 1 - Online serving path (ingest -> digitize -> classify -> extract -> validate -> route)

The ranking template maps as follows: candidate generation = OCR tokens and regions, ranking = field tagging / LLM extraction, re-ranking/policy = validation rules and confidence routing.

Figure 29.1 - End-to-end online architecture of an invoice extraction service

 +-----------+  upload / email  +--------------+ doc_id, tenant  +-------------------+
 | Sources   |----------------->| Ingest API   |---------------->| Queue (SQS/Kafka) |
 | portal,   |                  | dedupe(hash) |                 | per-tenant shards |
 | email,    |                  | virus scan   |                 +---------+---------+
 | scanner,  |                  +--------------+                           |
 | mobile    |                                                             v
 +-----------+                          +-----------------------------------------+
                                        | Pre-processing                          |
                                        | PDF split, render 300 dpi, deskew,      |
                                        | denoise, rotate, born-digital text grab |
                                        +--------------------+--------------------+
                                                             | page images (+ text)
                                                             v
 +--------------------+  model   +-------------------------------------------------+
 | Model registry     |--------->| Digitize: OCR + layout                          |
 | OCR / layout /     | versions | text detection -> recognition -> words + bboxes |
 | classifier / KIE / |          | layout: blocks, tables, key-value pairs         |
 | LLM prompts        |          +------------------------+------------------------+
 +---------+----------+                                   | tokens, boxes, page img
           |                                              v
           |                     +------------------------------------------------+
           +-------------------->| Classify & split                               |
           |                     | invoice / receipt / credit note / PO / other   |
           |                     | page-to-document boundaries in multi-doc PDFs  |
           |                     +------------------------+-----------------------+
           |                                              | doc type
           |                                              v
           |   +-------------------+     +------------------------------------------+
           |   | Vendor store      |---->| Extract (KIE)                            |
           |   | vendor master,    | hint| layout transformer (token tags) or       |
           |   | known templates,  |     | VLM / LLM -> JSON schema (+ bbox grounds)|
           |   | past corrections  |     | per-field confidence                     |
           |   +-------------------+     |                                          |
           +---------------------------->| models + prompts pinned by registry      |
                                         +---------------------+--------------------+
                                                               | fields + conf
                                                               v
                                         +------------------------------------------+
                                         | Normalize & validate                     |
                                         | dates, currency, VAT IDs, sum(lines) =   |
                                         | subtotal, subtotal + tax = total,        |
                                         | PO / receipt 3-way match, dup invoice    |
                                         +---------------------+--------------------+
                                                               |
                               +-------------------------------+--------------+
                               | all checks pass and conf >= threshold        | else
                               v                                              v
                   +-------------------------+                 +---------------------+
                   | Straight-through post   |                 | Human review queue  |
                   | ERP / AP system, webhook|<----------------| validation station, |
                   +------------+------------+  corrected doc  | bbox highlight, keys|
                                |                              +----------+----------+
                                v                                         | corrections
                   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
                   | Logging store: pages, OCR output, predictions, confidences,   |
                   | validation results, human corrections, latency, cost/page     |
                   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
  • The "feature store" of classic MLSD maps to the vendor store (vendor master data, per-vendor layout priors, past corrected values). The "model store" maps to the model registry + prompt store.
  • Confidence routing is the policy layer. Thresholds are set per field and per tenant to hit a target precision on auto-posted fields.
  • The AWS reference pipeline has the same stages: classification, extraction, enrichment, validation, human review (A2I) [9].

  • Human corrections are the main label source. This is UiPath's "Digitize -> Classify -> Extract -> Validate -> Train" loop [26] (not opened).
  • Split by vendor, not by document. A random split leaks layouts and inflates F1.

Diagram 3 - Model architecture: OCR + layout transformer, and the OCR-free / LLM variant

Figure 29.3 - Three extractor families and their inputs/outputs

 (A) Pipeline: OCR -> layout-aware transformer (LayoutLMv3-style) [3]
 +-------------+  words w_i   +-------------------------------------+
 | OCR engine  |------------->| Text embedding + 1D position        |
 | DB detector |  boxes b_i   | + 2D layout (x0,y0,x1,y1,w,h)       |
 | + CRNN/TrOCR|------------->| per token / segment                 |---+
 +-------------+              +-------------------------------------+   |
 +-------------+  patches     +-------------------------------------+   | concat
 | Page image  |------------->| Linear patch embedding (no CNN)     |---+
 +-------------+              +-------------------------------------+   |
                                                                        v
                                 +--------------------------------------------------+
                                 | Multimodal transformer (12 or 24 layers)         |
                                 | pretrain: MLM + masked image model + word-patch  |
                                 | alignment                                        |
                                 +--------------------------+-----------------------+
                                                            |
                                  +-------------------------+-------+
                                  v                                 v
                    +---------------------------+   +---------------------------+
                    | Token head: BIO tags      |   | Relation head: key<->value|
                    | B-TOTAL, I-VENDOR, ...    |   | line-item row grouping    |
                    +-------------+-------------+   +-------------+-------------+
                                  +---------------+---------------+
                                                  v
                                 fields + bboxes + softmax confidence

 (B) OCR-free encoder-decoder (Donut-style) [4]
 +-------------+  pixels  +---------------------+  tokens  +---------------------------+
 | Page image  |--------->| Swin vision encoder |--------->| Text decoder -> JSON-like |
 +-------------+          +---------------------+          | <s_total>12.50</s_total>  |
                                                           +---------------------------+

 (C) VLM / LLM with schema (GenAI answer)
 +-------------+  +--------------+  +------------------+  +---------------------------+
 | Page image  |  | OCR text +   |  | JSON schema +    |  | VLM / LLM                 |
 | (optional)  |->| layout as MD |->| vendor few-shot  |->| constrained JSON decoding |
 +-------------+  +--------------+  +------------------+  | + cite bbox / source span |
                                                          +-------------+-------------+
                                                                        v
                                     fields + evidence; confidence from logprobs,
                                     self-consistency, or OCR-span match
  • (A) is cheap, fast and well calibrated. It needs labeled token data per field.
  • (B) avoids OCR errors and is a single model. Reported CORD score about 91 (91.3 TED accuracy for the v2 checkpoint) and 0.7-1.2 s per image [4] (fetched).
  • (C) is zero/few-shot and handles new vendors and fields. It costs more per page, can hallucinate values, and its confidence is harder to calibrate.

AnalyzeExpense output contract (what to mirror in your own schema) [10]

Element Content
Summary fields Normalized Type per field (e.g. TOTAL, VENDOR_NAME); unmatched keys returned as OTHER with the raw label
Line-item groups Each row is an EXPENSE_ROW with ITEM, QUANTITY, PRICE, UNIT_PRICE, PRODUCT_CODE
Grounding Page number + bounding box + polygon for every label and value
Confidence Per label and per value; drives the A2I routing threshold
Sibling APIs AnalyzeID for ID documents (KYC variant); analyze_expense / analyze_id wrappers in Textractor [31]
  • Keep the raw key text next to the normalized type. Reviewers and the label builder need it.
  • The AWS repo also ships an agentic variant on Bedrock AgentCore with Analyzer, Matcher, Extractor, Validator and Troubleshooter agents, plus a Bedrock Prompt Flows variant with per-document flows and A2I review [9] (fetched).
  • Uber's GenAI invoice post [11] (not opened) describes the same shape: OCR -> LLM extraction -> human-in-the-loop UI. Its numbers are not verified here.

Data & labels

Source Label type Notes
Human review corrections Gold field values (+ bbox) Best signal. Biased toward low-confidence docs
ERP posted values Weak labels (value only) Map to OCR tokens with fuzzy match. Noisy for repeated numbers
Annotation campaigns Boxes + field + relation labels Costly. Spend on new vendors and active-learning samples
Public sets FUNSD [27], CORD [12], SROIE [28], DocVQA [29], RVL-CDIP Pretraining / benchmarks. Domain shift vs real AP invoices
Synthetic Rendered templates, SynthDoG [4] Cold start, rare fields, new languages

Features / signals

Group Examples
Text OCR tokens, subword embeddings, OCR confidence per word
Layout Normalized bbox, reading order, block/table/cell IDs, distance to keywords ("Total", "IVA")
Visual Page patches, font size/bold, lines and table rulings, logos, stamps
Document Doc type, page index, language, born-digital vs scanned, DPI / blur score
Vendor priors Vendor ID (from VAT ID / IBAN / logo), known field positions, past values, currency
Context PO data for matching, tenant schema, expected tax rates

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
OCR Tesseract / cloud OCR DB detector + CRNN / TrOCR [6], PP-OCRv5 (109-language rec) / PP-OCRv6 (1.5M-34.5M params, 50 langs) [19] Accuracy on noisy scans vs cost; handwriting needs TrOCR-class models
Layout / tables Heuristic line detection DiT / LayoutLMv3 layout, table-structure model, PP-StructureV3 [19] Better tables vs GPU cost
Classifier TF-IDF + logistic regression on OCR text DiT / LayoutLMv3 fine-tuned [5][3] Visual cues matter for look-alike docs
KIE Regex + per-vendor templates LayoutLMv2/v3 token tagging [3][5]; graph models [8] Templates break on layout drift; learned models generalize
End-to-end n/a Donut (OCR-free) [4]; PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, 0.9B params [19] One model, but harder grounding and long-page limits
GenAI Prompted LLM on OCR text VLM with JSON schema + few-shot from vendor store; fine-tuned small VLM Zero-shot new fields vs hallucination, cost, latency
Router Single model Cheap model first, escalate low-confidence docs to LLM Cuts cost; adds complexity

Loss functions

Model Loss
Text detector (DB) BCE / dice on probability + threshold maps
Text recognizer CTC (CRNN) or cross-entropy (TrOCR seq2seq)
Classifier Cross-entropy, class-weighted for rare doc types
Token tagger Token-level cross-entropy over BIO tags (+ CRF optional)
Relation head Binary cross-entropy over key-value / row-membership pairs
Donut / VLM SFT Next-token cross-entropy on the serialized JSON
Pretraining (LayoutLMv3) MLM + masked image modeling + word-patch alignment [3]

Offline metrics

Metric Use
CER / WER OCR quality, sliced by scan quality and language
Field-level precision / recall / F1, exact match Core KIE metric. Report per field (total matters more than memo)
Normalized edit distance / ANLS Partial credit for strings (DocVQA style)
Line-item table F1 (row + cell) Hardest part of invoices
Tree edit distance accuracy Donut-style JSON output [4]
STP rate at precision >= 99% Business-aligned: share of docs that skip review
Calibration (ECE), coverage-risk curve Needed to set routing thresholds
Unseen-vendor slice Generalization to new layouts

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Notes
Straight-through-processing rate Primary. Docs auto-posted without human touch
Human touch time per doc, fields corrected per doc Reviewer effort
Post-posting error rate Errors found later in ERP (payment errors, duplicate payments)
End-to-end latency, backlog age SLA
Cost per page OCR + GPU + LLM tokens
  • A-B by tenant or by document hash. Shadow mode first: compare to the champion on the same docs.
  • Guardrail: auto-posted precision must not drop, even if STP rises.

Serving & latency budget (async, p95 under 60 s per 3-page doc; sync receipt p95 under 5 s)

Step Budget (approx.) Notes
Ingest, split, render 0.5-2 s CPU pool
OCR + layout 0.3-1 s / page GPU batch; skip OCR for born-digital text
Classify 50-100 ms Small model
KIE layout transformer 100-300 ms / page GPU, batch by page
LLM / VLM extraction (if routed) 2-10 s Only for low-conf or new vendors; constrained JSON
Validate + normalize under 100 ms Rules + vendor lookups
Queueing slack rest Autoscale on queue depth

Monitoring

Signal Alert on
OCR confidence distribution, blank-page rate Scanner or upload change
Per-field confidence and review rate Drift for a vendor or tenant
Correction rate per field / vendor New layout or model regression
Validation failure rate (sum checks) Line-item extraction breaking
Doc-type mix, language mix New document types arriving
LLM: JSON parse failures, invented values (not in OCR text), token cost GenAI-specific
Latency, queue depth, GPU use SLA risk

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Poor scans, skew, stamps over text Pre-processing, quality score, ask for re-upload
Multi-page tables, line items spanning pages Page-level context, table stitching, sum validation
Look-alike numbers (invoice # vs PO # vs order #) Key-value relation head, vendor priors, LLM with bbox citation
Locale formats (1.234,56 vs 1,234.56; DD/MM vs MM/DD) Locale from vendor country, currency, validation
LLM hallucinated fields Require the value to appear in OCR text; abstain; route to review
Prompt injection in document text Treat doc text as data; schema-constrained output; no tool calls from doc content
New vendor layouts VLM fallback, active learning, fast few-shot via vendor store
Duplicate / fraudulent invoices Hash + fuzzy dedupe, bank-detail-change alerts
Label noise from weak ERP labels Confidence-weighted loss, audit samples

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you get training labels without a big annotation budget? (review corrections, ERP weak labels, synthetic data)
  • OCR + layout model vs OCR-free (Donut) vs VLM/LLM: which do you pick and why?
  • How do you extract line-item tables, including tables that span pages?
  • How do you produce a calibrated per-field confidence from an LLM?
  • How do you set thresholds for auto-posting vs human review? What is the business metric?
  • How do you handle a vendor never seen before?
  • How do you stop the LLM from inventing a total or a bank account number?
  • How do you split train/test to avoid layout leakage?
  • How do you handle multi-document PDFs (invoice + PO + delivery note in one file)?
  • How would you cut cost per page by 10x?
  • How do you support 50+ languages and handwriting?
  • How do you detect drift when a big vendor changes its template?
  • How do you protect PII and bank details, and meet data-residency rules?
  • What do you log so reviewer corrections become training data?
  • Buy (Textract / Document AI style API) or build? When does a managed API's fixed schema (OTHER fields) stop being enough?
  • How do you keep raw key text, normalized type and bbox together so every field is auditable? [10]

30. Design Demand Forecasting for Inventory (Amazon Supply Chain, Instacart)

Sourcing note: web search was exhausted and company-blog / portal domains were blocked in this review run. Every company tag and portal row below was re-checked against cloned copies of the GitHub indexes [23]-[27], which list the cited posts and papers ([1]-[22], [30], [31]) under forecasting or availability. Rows marked "typical" are standard interview assumptions, not quoted numbers.

Company tags

Company (reported / mirrored) Evidence Ref
Amazon Multi-horizon quantile forecaster (MQ-RNN -> MQ-CNN -> MQ-Transformer) feeds buying; RL ordering policy research [1][2][4][5]
Amazon (AWS) DeepAR, GluonTS, Chronos: open probabilistic forecasting models [3][6][8]
Instacart Real-time item availability (P(in stock)) for hundreds of millions of items; lost-demand modeling [9][10][11][30][31]
DoorDash Ensemble time-series forecasting; holiday cascade model; supply/demand balance [12][13][14][15]
Uber Forecasting platform; LSTM extreme-event forecasting [16][17]
Zalando, Ocado, Mercado Libre, Grubhub, Lyft Item / order-volume demand forecasting in production [18][19][20][21][22]

Portals that cover the problem:

Portal Coverage Ref
eugeneyan/applied-ml "Forecasting" section: Amazon, Uber, DoorDash, Grubhub, Lyft, LinkedIn Greykite [23]
Engineer1999 ML case-study list Zalando, DoorDash (ensemble, holiday), Grubhub, Ocado, Mercado Libre, Lyft forecasting; 4 Instacart availability posts; Instacart lost demand [24]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Forecast demand per (SKU, location, day) for horizon 1-52 weeks; output quantiles (P10/P50/P90) [1][2]
Functional (downstream) Turn forecast into order quantity / safety stock; flag stock-outs [5]
Functional (Instacart) P(item in stock at store now) for every item-store, used at search/checkout [9][10]
Scale (Amazon) Hundreds of millions of products, many fulfillment centers [1] typical
Scale (Instacart) Hundreds of millions of item-store pairs [9]
Freshness Batch: daily/weekly reforecast; availability: minutes typical
Latency Batch job hours (SLA before buying run); availability lookup < 10 ms from cache typical
Non-functional Calibrated uncertainty, cold-start for new SKUs, robustness to holidays/shocks (COVID) [1][13][15]
Business objective Minimize holding + lost-sales cost; maximize in-stock rate [5]

Data & labels

Item Choice Note
Label Units demanded per SKU x location x day/week Sales are censored when out of stock
Censoring Mask stock-out periods, or impute via availability model Instacart availability doubles as a censoring signal [9]
Lost demand Estimate demand never observed (searches / carts for out-of-stock items) and add back to labels Instacart "Modeling the unseen" [31]
Hierarchy SKU -> category -> dept; store -> region -> national Reconcile (top-down / MinT)
Splits Rolling-origin backtests by time, never random [26]
Cold start New SKUs: attribute/text embeddings, similar-item priors [18]
Anomalies Remove one-off bulk orders, data outages; tag holidays [13]

Features

Group Examples
Lags / windows Demand lag 1/7/14/28/364, rolling mean/std, trend, days since last sale
Calendar Day of week, holidays, paydays, seasonality Fourier terms
Price & promo Current/planned price, discount depth, promo flag, competitor price
Inventory On-hand, stock-out flags, in-transit, vendor lead time
Item static Category, brand, size, embeddings, life-cycle stage
Location Store/FC id embedding, region, demographics, weather
Real-time (availability) Shopper "found / not found", last restock time, store feed recency [9][10]

Model choices

Stage Model Pros Cons
Baseline Seasonal naive, moving avg, ETS/ARIMA per series Simple, interpretable No cross-series learning, poor on sparse SKUs
Classic ML GBDT (LightGBM) on lag features, quantile objective Strong on tabular (M5 winners [28]) Separate model per horizon/quantile
Deep global DeepAR (autoregressive, likelihood) Probabilistic, cold-start via sharing [3] Error accumulation over long horizons
Deep multi-horizon MQ-RNN / MQ-CNN / MQ-Transformer Direct multi-horizon quantiles, Amazon prod [1][2][4] Larger infra
Attention Temporal Fusion Transformer Interpretable variable selection [7] Heavier training
Foundation Chronos (pretrained on many series) Zero-shot for new series [6] Less domain covariates
Ensemble Stack of above (DoorDash ELITE-style) Robust Ops complexity [12]
Decision Newsvendor / RL policy Optimizes cost directly [5] Needs simulator

Loss

Loss When
Pinball (quantile) loss, summed over horizons Default for inventory (asymmetric costs) [2]
Negative log-likelihood (neg. binomial / Tweedie) Count, intermittent demand (DeepAR) [3]
Tweedie / Poisson in GBDT Zero-inflated SKUs
Cost-weighted loss (holding vs lost-sale) Align with business critical ratio
Policy reward (RL) End-to-end buying [5]

Offline metrics

Metric Why
wQL / CRPS Quality of full distribution
WAPE / MAPE / sMAPE Point accuracy, volume-weighted
Bias (mean error) Systematic over/under-forecasting
Quantile coverage (P90 hit rate ~ 90%) Calibration
Simulated in-stock rate & holding cost Decision-level backtest
Sliced: new SKUs, holidays, promos, long tail Catch hidden failures

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Note
In-stock rate / fill rate Primary customer outcome
Lost sales, substitution rate Instacart: items not found [9]
Inventory holding cost, days of supply Over-stock signal
Waste / spoilage (perishables) Grocery
Delivery promise accuracy Downstream
Test design Store/FC-level or SKU-cluster randomization, switchback; long tests (weeks)

Serving & latency budget

Path Budget Mechanism
Nightly forecast run ~2-4 h for all series Distributed batch (Spark/Ray), partition by SKU (typical)
Policy / order generation ~1 h Vectorized newsvendor per SKU-node
Availability lookup < 10 ms p99 Precomputed scores in KV cache [10]
Availability refresh Minutes Stream updates from shopper events [10]
What-if planner query ~1 s Cached forecasts + on-demand re-solve

Monitoring

Signal Action
Rolling WAPE / bias vs backtest Alert, roll back champion
Input drift (price feed, missing stores) Block run, fallback to last forecast
Regime shift (COVID, viral item) Event-triggered retrain, shorter windows [15]
Override rate by planners Proxy for trust
Stock-out and overstock outliers Root-cause by SKU

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Censored demand -> forecast spiral down Stock-out masking, availability-aware labels
Holiday / promo spikes Holiday features, cascade model [13]
New SKU cold start Hierarchical priors, similar-item embeddings, foundation model [6]
Intermittent demand Count likelihoods, Croston-style baselines
Feedback loop (forecast drives stock drives sales) Treat as causal; simulate policy [5][22]
Data outages Freshness checks, last-good fallback
Overconfident intervals Calibrate quantiles, conformal adjustment

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you get true demand when sales are censored by stock-outs?
  • Point vs probabilistic forecast: why quantiles for inventory? Which quantile to order at?
  • One global model vs per-series models: tradeoffs at 100M+ series?
  • How do you forecast for a brand-new SKU or a new store?
  • How do you handle promotions and price changes you plan in the future (known covariates)?
  • How would you reconcile forecasts across SKU / category / region hierarchy?
  • How do you backtest correctly without leakage?
  • How did COVID-like shocks break models, and how would you retrain? [15]
  • How do lead time and vendor uncertainty enter the order quantity?
  • How do you A/B test a forecasting model when inventory takes weeks to react?
  • How does forecasting interact with pricing (forecast depends on price)? [22]
  • Batch vs real-time: when would Instacart-style availability need streaming? [10]
  • How would you use an RL policy instead of forecast-then-optimize? [5]
  • How do you handle intermittent, long-tail SKUs?
  • How do you estimate demand you never observed (lost demand from out-of-stock searches)? [31]
  • How do you keep the availability score fresh for 200M+ item-store pairs without rescoring everything? [30]
  • What latency/compute budget for the nightly run, and how to parallelize?

DoorDash engineering [12][13][14] Order/supply volume forecasting Ensemble stacking, holiday cascade Ensemble ops, holiday handling

31. Design Anomaly Detection for Metrics/Monitoring and Transactions

References marked "(not fetched)" are well-known engineering posts/papers whose URLs were not re-checked. A later review pass also found every external host blocked (proxy 403), so no URL was re-fetched in that pass either; unverifiable company tags and portal claims were removed or marked. Rows marked "typical assumption" are interview-standard estimates.

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional Ingest millions of time series (KPIs, infra metrics); flag anomalous points/windows [1][3]
Functional Severity score + anomaly window + peak timestamp (not just a binary flag) [5]
Functional Group related alerts; root-cause hints (dimension drill-down, correlated metrics) [3][5]
Functional Transaction mode: score each event, route to block / review / allow [7][18]
Functional User feedback (true/false alert) and per-metric sensitivity tuning [1][3]
Non-functional Detection delay: seconds-1 min (infra), <100 ms per event (transactions) [2] / typical
Non-functional Low alert fatigue: precision prioritized for paging; recall for fraud typical
Scale 1M-100M series, 1-60 s granularity => 100k-10M points/s typical assumption
Scale (Microsoft) Service handles millions of time series across Microsoft products [2] (not fetched)
Labels Very sparse (<0.1-1% anomalous); mostly unlabeled; delayed fraud labels [2][7]
Seasonality Daily/weekly cycles, holidays, deploy-driven level shifts [8][10]

Data & labels

Source Label type Notes
Incident tickets / postmortems Weak positive windows Coarse timing; map to affected series
On-call ack / "not an anomaly" clicks Explicit feedback Biased to alerted points only (no FN signal) [3]
Synthetic injection (spikes, level shifts, dips) Strong, free Used to train SR-CNN without manual labels [1][2]
Chargebacks, analyst reviews Delayed positive (fraud) 30-90 day delay; censoring for recent data [7]
Public benchmarks (NAB, Yahoo S5) Labelled windows NAB: 58 series, real + artificial [25][10]

Features

Group Examples Path
Raw window Last w points, normalized Metrics
Decomposition Trend, seasonal, residual (STL); spectral saliency Metrics
Calendar Hour-of-day, day-of-week, holiday, deploy flag Both
Cross-series Sibling dimension values, correlated metric deltas Metrics / RCA
Multivariate window N correlated metrics x w steps (input to MTAD-GAT) Metrics [27]
Velocity Txns per card/device/IP in 1m/1h/24h Transactions
Entity history Typical amount, merchant category, geo distance Transactions
Graph Shared device/payment instrument, community anomaly Transactions [14]

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Stage Model Pros Cons
0 Static thresholds / rules Simple, explainable Breaks with seasonality, high fatigue
1 Rolling mean + k-sigma, week-over-week Cheap, per-series Sensitive to outliers in baseline
2 Robust stats: median/MAD, S-H-ESD Handles seasonality, robust [8][9] Batch-ish, tuning max_anoms
3 Forecast + residual (Holt-Winters, Prophet, EGADS TMM/ADM) Interpretable band [10] One model per series; cold start
4 Robust PCA (RAD), isolation forest Multivariate, unlabeled [12][4] Hard to explain per point
5 SR-CNN (global, trained on synthetic) No labels, one model for millions [1][2] Needs good injection design
6 LSTM/Transformer AE or forecaster Complex patterns, multivariate Cost, drift, needs GPUs
7 Supervised GBDT/DNN on events (fraud) Best precision with labels [18] Label delay, misses novel attacks
8 Meta-learner choosing algo per series Scales tuning [13] Extra system complexity
9 Multivariate GAT (MTAD-GAT: feature + time attention, forecast + reconstruction) Catches cross-metric anomalies; per-variable attribution [27] Group of metrics must be pre-defined; GPU training

Loss

Model Loss / objective
Forecaster MSE or quantile (pinball) loss for prediction band
SR-CNN Cross-entropy on injected-anomaly labels per point [2]
Autoencoder Reconstruction MSE on (mostly) normal data
Isolation forest None (path length => score)
Supervised fraud Weighted BCE / focal loss for class imbalance; cost-sensitive threshold

Offline metrics

Metric Why
Precision / recall / F1 on points Baseline [1]
Point-adjusted or delay-aware F1 Segment counts if detected within delay k of start [1][30]
Caveat: point-adjust inflation PA can make random scores look strong; report PA%K or raw F1 too [29]
NAB score (Standard, Low-FP, Low-FN profiles) Rewards early detection, penalizes FP [25]
Detection delay (median, p95) Time-to-detect matters for outages
Alerts per series per week Proxy for alert fatigue
PR-AUC, recall @ fixed FPR, $ loss caught Transaction / fraud mode

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Notes
MTTD (mean time to detect) vs. incidents discovered by humans/customers
% incidents caught by detector first Coverage of real outages
Alert precision (ack rate as true) From on-call feedback [3]
Pages per on-call shift Fatigue guardrail
Fraud $ loss, false decline rate, review queue size Transaction mode
A-B design Shadow mode + interleaved alert rules; can't randomize outages, so backtest + shadow

Serving & latency budget

Step Metrics path Transaction path
Ingest + aggregate 10-60 s roll-up window 5 ms
Feature fetch Window from in-memory state 10-20 ms (online store)
Model scoring <1 ms per series per tick (vectorized) 5-20 ms
Threshold + post-process ~1 s batching 2 ms
Total under 1-2 min point-to-alert under 50-100 ms
Scaling trick Partition by series id; batch thousands of series per CPU call Cache entity aggregates

Monitoring (of the detector itself)

Signal Action
Alert volume spike across many series Likely upstream data issue; global suppression
Missing data / late points Distinguish "no data" from "drop to zero" (no-data check in aggregator, Diagram 1)
Score distribution drift Recalibrate thresholds
Feedback FP rate per series Auto-lower sensitivity or switch algo
Fraud: score PSI, approval rate Rollback model

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Alert storms from one root cause Group by topology/dimension; RCA [3][5]
Seasonality / holiday false positives Seasonal decomposition, holiday calendar, wo1w/wo2w baselines
Level shift after deploy keeps alerting Change-point detection, adapt baseline quickly [13]
Anomaly contaminates baseline Robust stats (median/MAD), exclude flagged points from fit [8]
Cold-start series Global model (SR-CNN), borrow from sibling series
Sparse / low-volume metrics Poisson models, larger windows, minimum-volume gates
Adversaries adapt (fraud) Unsupervised + supervised hybrid; graph features [14]
Feedback only on alerted points Periodic random audits for false negatives

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you handle daily/weekly seasonality and holidays without per-series manual tuning?
  • Supervised vs unsupervised: what if you have almost no labels?
  • How do you generate training labels (synthetic injection, incident logs) and avoid leakage?
  • How do you evaluate when anomalies are segments, not points (point-adjusted F1, delay)?
  • How do you reduce alert fatigue and group alerts from one root cause?
  • How would you do root-cause analysis across dimensions (country x platform x version)?
  • How do you scale to 10M series with one model vs one model per series?
  • How do you distinguish a real drop from missing/late data?
  • What happens after a deploy causes a permanent level shift?
  • How do you set thresholds per series; how do you let users tune sensitivity?
  • For transactions: how do you combine rules, supervised model and anomaly score?
  • How do you handle delayed fraud labels and feedback loops from blocked transactions?
  • How do you monitor the detector itself (meta-monitoring)?
  • Multivariate: detect anomalies across correlated metrics jointly, and attribute to a variable? [27]
  • Why can point-adjusted F1 overstate a detector, and what would you report instead? [29]
  • Build vs buy: what if the managed service you depend on is retired? [28]
  • Can an LLM help summarize incidents / suggest root causes? [26]

32. Design Fake Review Detection and Review Ranking (Amazon, Yelp)

Prompt as usually given: "Design a system that detects fake / incentivized / spam reviews on an e-commerce or local-business platform, and ranks the remaining reviews so the most helpful ones appear first." Variants: opinion-spam detection, fake reviewer / review-ring detection, "Most helpful" review ordering, Yelp "recommended vs. not recommended" reviews, app-store review fraud, LLM-generated review detection.

Sourcing note: non-GitHub hosts (arxiv.org, acm.org, aaai.org, aboutamazon.com, yelp.com) could not be reached from the review sandbox and web search was exhausted. Tags: (fetched) = page read and claim checked. (repo-link) = URL listed verbatim in a fetched GitHub page. (ch-ref) = URL verified in another chapter. (known) = canonical page cited from memory, not re-fetched. No portal lists this exact prompt; company tags below are evidence of the system, not interview reports. "Typical assumption" numbers are interview estimates, not company disclosures.

Company tags

Company Evidence Notes Source
Amazon Mirrors it: Amazon review graph (upu, usu, uvu relations) is a standard fake-reviewer benchmark (CARE-GNN, DGL FraudAmazon) Product reviews + "Most helpful" ordering; no Amazon production paper verified here [1][3][28]
Yelp Mirrors it: YelpChi labels come from Yelp's own review filter ("not recommended") Filter behavior studied externally [4]; embeddings blog is adjacent (not spam) [4][5][7][28]
Alibaba (Xianyu) Built it: GAS - GCN-based spam review detection deployed on Xianyu second-hand marketplace Best documented production "review spam" GNN [8][9]
App-store review systems Academic: FdGars detects fraudsters in an online app review system (WWW 2019 workshop) No company tag claimed [10]
Meta, LinkedIn, Pinterest Adjacent only: integrity / spam systems cited by ByteByteGo ch. 5 and case-study lists, not review prompts Same actor-graph + content-classifier pattern [12][13][29][30]

safe-graph paper lists (academic) Canonical graph-based review-spam methods (GAS, CARE-GNN, GraphConsis, FdGars) [8][10][25]

Requirements & scale

Dimension Requirement Source / note
Functional 1 Score every new review for fake / spam / incentivized / LLM-generated; actions: publish, hide ("not recommended"), hold for human review, remove + penalize account Typical assumption
Functional 2 Detect fake reviewers and review rings (groups), retroactively remove reviews [3][11]
Functional 3 Rank surviving reviews per product/business ("Most helpful", "Recommended") with recency, diversity, personalization [4][6]
Non-functional Precision first on removal (false removal hurts trust, legal risk); recall on rings; explainable decisions for appeals Typical assumption
Review write QPS ~50-500 reviews/s peak (tens of millions/year) Typical assumption
Review read QPS ~50k-200k review-page renders/s (ranking served from cache) Typical assumption
Latency Sync pre-publish check p99 < 200 ms; deep graph/LLM checks async in minutes; ranking read p99 < 50 ms Typical assumption
Catalog / users 100M-1B products/businesses, 100M-500M reviewers, 1B+ historical reviews Typical assumption
Label prevalence Fake rate ~5-20% of submissions, highly skewed; YelpChi ~14.5% spam (commonly reported) [5][7] (known)
