 Benchmark review graphs used in papers (CARE-GNN [1]):
   YelpChi: review nodes; relations rur (same user), rtr (same product+month,
            same star), rsr (same product+star)    label sim: rur 0.91, others ~0.18
   Amazon:  user nodes; relations upu (same product), usu (same star in a week),
            uvu (similar review text)              label sim: upu 0.17, others ~0.05
   (label similarity over fraud nodes only, per CARE-GNN README 06/2021 update)
  • Lesson: user-linked edges (rur) are highly homophilous; product-linked edges are mostly camouflaged, so relation-aware neighbor filtering (CARE-GNN) matters [1].

Data & labels

Source Label type Issue Mitigation
Moderator decisions Hard, high precision Expensive, biased to flagged items Active learning, uncertainty sampling
Platform filter output (e.g. Yelp not-recommended) Proxy Model learns its own past filter Hold-out random audits
Paid-review stings / leaked review-farm lists Hard positives, rings Rare, bursty Label propagation over graph
Account bans, deleted accounts Weak, delayed Label leakage, delay Point-in-time joins
Helpful / unhelpful votes Ranker label Position bias, rich-get-richer IPW, Bayesian smoothing, exploration slots
Synthetic LLM fakes Augmentation Distribution mismatch Red-team generation per release

Features

Group Examples
Text Encoder embedding, length, sentiment extremity, duplicate/near-dup hash (MinHash), template phrases, LLM-perplexity / detector score
Reviewer behavior Account age, review count, review burst per day, rating deviation from item mean, fraction 5-star, verified-purchase ratio
Item behavior Review velocity spikes, rating distribution shift, seller-linked accounts
Network / device Shared IP, device fingerprint, payment instrument, geo mismatch with business
Graph GNN embeddings over review-user-item-device graph, co-review group density, ring membership
Ranking Helpfulness votes (smoothed), media present, detail/aspect coverage, recency, reviewer reputation

Model choices

Stage Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
Rules Blocklists, velocity caps Auto-generated rules from clusters Fast, explainable; brittle
Review detector Logistic regression / GBDT on behavior + n-grams Transformer text + GBDT fusion, multi-task Text alone weak vs. skilled writers
Reviewer / ring Co-review frequent itemset mining Hetero GNN (GAS, CARE-GNN, GraphConsis), dense-subgraph detection Graph catches coordination; costly, async
LLM-generated Perplexity heuristics Fine-tuned detector + LM-embedding + GNN Arms race, false positives on non-native writers
Actor-level Per-account aggregates Temporal interaction embeddings over account action sequences (Facebook TIES) Catches fake accounts before they review; needs event history [29]
Moderation assist Manual queue triage LLM classifier/explainer for queue items (Whatnot GenAI T&S pattern) Faster triage + rationale for appeals; cost, prompt drift [30]
Ranker Sort by helpful votes / Wilson score LambdaMART / DNN with quality + trust features Votes biased by position

Loss

Model Loss
Detector Weighted BCE or focal loss per head; multi-task sum with head weights
GNN Node/edge BCE with relation-aware neighbor sampling; class-balanced sampling
Ring Unsupervised density / clustering score, or contrastive loss on group embeddings
Ranker Pairwise / listwise (LambdaRank) on helpful-vote preferences, debiased with IPW

Offline metrics

Model Metric
Detector PR-AUC, recall at fixed precision (e.g. 95%), calibration (ECE)
Ring Ring recall, precision of top-K suspicious groups
Ranker NDCG@5/10, MAP on held-out vote data
Fairness slices FPR by locale, language, new vs. tenured user, small business
Benchmarks AUC / recall on YelpChi and Amazon fraud graphs (DGL FraudYelp / FraudAmazon) [1][28]

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Direction
Fake prevalence on served reviews (audited sample) Down
Appeal overturn rate, false takedown rate Down
Moderator queue size / time-to-action Down
Helpful-vote rate, review-section CTR, scroll depth Up
Conversion / return rate (e-commerce), booking rate (local) Up / neutral
Seller / business complaints Down
  • A-B caveat: adversaries adapt; use holdout audit samples and per-market rollouts rather than user-level split for enforcement.

Serving & latency budget

Step Budget (p99)
Rules + rate limit 10 ms
Online feature fetch 30 ms
Text encoder (distilled) 60 ms
GBDT + fusion head 20 ms
Decision + write 30 ms
Total sync write path < 200 ms
GNN / ring / LLM async minutes-hours
Ranked review read (cached) < 50 ms

Monitoring

Signal Alert on
Score distribution drift per locale/category PSI shift
Sudden review velocity on item/seller Burst attack
Hold/reject rate Spike or collapse
Appeal overturn rate Precision drop
Label delay / moderator agreement Label quality
LLM-text detector hit rate New generator release

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Camouflaged fraudsters (aged accounts, mixed honest reviews) Relation-aware GNN, behavior over long windows
LLM-written fakes evade text models Behavior + graph signals over text-only; red-team retraining
Competitor "review bombing" negative fakes Item-level anomaly detection, temporary lock
Honest bursts (viral event, launch) flagged Context features (traffic, sales), human review
Feedback loop: ranker hides reviews -> no votes Exploration slots, IPW
Over-removal hurts small businesses / non-native writers Slice metrics, high-precision removal, soft demotion

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you get labels when ground truth is mostly unobservable?
  • Fake review vs. fake reviewer vs. review ring: which entity do you model and why?
  • How would you detect coordinated review groups that individually look normal?
  • How do you handle LLM-generated reviews that are fluent and unique?
  • Sync vs. async: what must be decided before the review is visible?
  • How do you set thresholds for hide vs. remove vs. human review?
  • How do you avoid penalizing non-native speakers or new legitimate users?
  • How do you recompute the star average once fakes are removed retroactively?
  • How do you debias helpful votes for position and age in the ranker?
  • How would you diversify top reviews across positive and negative ratings?
  • How do you evaluate a detector when the adversary adapts to it?
  • What graph would you build, and how do you scale GNN inference to 1B reviews?
  • How do you handle incentivized reviews (free product) vs. outright fake?
  • How do you explain decisions for appeals and legal compliance?
  • Would you model accounts (action sequences) before they post, not just reviews? [29]
  • Where can an LLM help (queue triage, rationale) without becoming the sole judge? [30]

33. Design Semantic Search and Duplicate Question Detection (Quora, Stack Overflow)

Prompt as usually given: "When a user types a new question on Quora or Stack Overflow, show similar existing questions and flag likely duplicates before they post." Variants: "merge duplicate questions offline", "semantic search over a Q&A corpus", and "related questions" in the side panel. Chip Huyen's exercise #11 asks it almost verbatim [7].

Sourcing note: in the review pass the web-search budget was used up and arxiv.org, stackoverflow.blog, quora.com, kaggle.com and huggingface.co were unreachable from the sandbox. GitHub pages were fetched and read (exercise numbers re-checked against the raw file). Each reference carries a tag. (fetched) means the page was read for this chapter. (ch-ref) means the URL was verified in another chapter of this atlas. (known) means a canonical paper or post cited by its stable URL but not re-read for this chapter. The "asked it" evidence for company tags is thin, so treat it as indicative only.

Company tags

Company Evidence Notes Source
Quora Built it: the Question Pairs dataset (2017), a Kaggle competition, and an engineering post on deep-learning question matching The canonical version of this problem [10][11][12]
Stack Overflow / Stack Exchange Built it: "similar questions" while you type, the "close as duplicate" workflow, and semantic search (2023). Asked it: Chip Huyen exercise #11 frames it as "StackOverflow similar questions" Moderator duplicate closures give free labels [7][13]
Meta Built it: embedding-based retrieval in Facebook Search. Asked it (indicative): MLE loops cover search and retrieval design The same two-tower and ANN template [16][24]
Google, Amazon, LinkedIn Asked it (indicative): text search and semantic search appear in MLSD question banks for these loops. No interview report was confirmed in this run Treat as likely, not confirmed [2][5][25][26]
Reddit, Zendesk-style support desks, Discourse forums Same pattern: deflecting a ticket or post to an existing answer. No interview report was confirmed Variant: "suggest a help-centre article" assumption

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Source
Functional (online) As the user types a title or body, return the top-k similar questions (k is about 5-10) [7]
Functional (dup flag) Show a "possible duplicate" banner when P(dup) is at least a threshold. Moderators can close or merge [13], assumption
Functional (offline) Mine duplicate clusters across the corpus and merge them into a canonical question [9]
Functional (search) Natural-language search box over questions and answers, using lexical and semantic retrieval [13]
Corpus Stack Overflow has about 24M questions, Quora has hundreds of millions assumption (typical)
Labelled pairs Quora QQP: 404,290 labelled pairs [8]; about 37% positive [8][10][11]
QPS Search plus typeahead-similar: about 1-5k QPS average, about 15k peak assumption
Latency p99 under 150 ms for the similar-questions panel. Can be debounced to every 300-500 ms of typing assumption
Freshness New question searchable within a minute or two through a streaming embed-and-upsert assumption
Precision need The dup banner needs high precision, about 0.9 or higher. A false "duplicate" frustrates new users assumption
Languages Usually English-first. The multilingual follow-up uses a multilingual encoder assumption
Business goal Fewer duplicate posts, more answers reused, faster time-to-answer, less moderator load assumption

Data & labels

Source Label type Volume / note Pitfall
Moderator "closed as duplicate" links Strong positive (a, b) Stack Overflow-scale, millions; used as labels in early forum work [15] Biased to popular canonical targets
Reopened after dup-close Negative or hard negative Small Noisy, depends on the moderator
Quora QQP Binary human label 404k pairs, about 37% positive Sampling bias. Not random pairs [11]
Panel click plus "this answers my question" Weak positive Very large Position bias. Needs debiasing or IPS
Posted anyway after the panel was shown Weak negative Large User may not have read it
Random pairs Easy negative Unlimited Too easy on its own
BM25 and ANN top-k non-dups Hard negative Mined per epoch False negatives (unlabelled dups)
Human raters Gold eval set 5-20k pairs, stratified Cost. Keep a fresh monthly sample

Features

Group Features Used by
Text (dense) Bi-encoder cos(u, v), cross-encoder logit Retrieval, ranker
Text (lexical) BM25, TF-IDF cos, word or char n-gram Jaccard, edit distance, length diff Blend, baseline
Entity / code Shared tags, library names, error strings, code-block overlap (Stack Overflow) Blend
Candidate quality Has accepted answer, answer count, score, views, closed or locked Blend, policy
Temporal Candidate age, age gap, tag-version drift (for example Python 2 vs 3) Blend
User / context Asker reputation, site, language, entry surface (ask page vs search) Policy, threshold

Model choices

Stage Baseline Advanced Trade-off
Retrieval BM25 over title and body Fine-tuned bi-encoder plus ANN, hybrid with BM25 through RRF Dense covers paraphrase. BM25 covers exact error strings and code [14][16][22][32]
Query understanding Lower-case, strip code noise Spell-check, normalisation, expansion, tag/intent prediction Front of the funnel in the portal search template [1]
Pair scoring LR or RF on lexical features Cross-encoder (BERT/DeBERTa) fine-tuned on dup pairs About 100x the compute per pair. Limit to the top ~100 [23][29]
Late interaction n/a ColBERT (token-level MaxSim) Better than a bi-encoder, but a larger index [20]
Blend Cross-encoder score alone GBDT on CE logit plus quality and meta Lets you push answered or accepted canonical questions up
LLM n/a LLM judge for borderline P in [0.4, 0.7], or a rewrite of the query Latency and cost. Use offline or async
Clustering Threshold on pairs Connected components with cluster-size caps Transitive chains drift. Cap size and re-verify

Loss functions

Model Loss Notes
Bi-encoder MultipleNegativesRankingLoss (in-batch softmax, InfoNCE) Needs positives only. Larger batches help [8][19]
Bi-encoder (pairs) OnlineContrastiveLoss (margin 0.5) Uses labelled 0/1 pairs and focuses on hard pairs [8]
Multi-task MNRL plus ContrastiveLoss, alternating batches One for ranking, one for classification [8]
Cross-encoder Binary cross-entropy on (q, c, y) Calibrate afterwards with Platt or isotonic
Blend ranker LambdaMART (nDCG) or logloss Pairwise if graded labels exist
Distillation MSE or KL from cross-encoder to bi-encoder scores Improves recall without serving cost

Offline metrics

Stage Metric Target example
Retrieval Recall@100 of the known dup target 0.95 or higher
Ranking MRR, nDCG@10, Hit@5 Report by slice
Dup classifier PR-AUC, precision at the threshold, recall at precision 0.9 Precision at tau of 0.9 or higher
Calibration ECE or a reliability plot Needed for a stable tau
Benchmarks QQP accuracy and F1; BEIR Quora (10k queries, 523k docs) and CQADupStack (13,145 queries, 457k docs) nDCG@10 Sanity check vs public models [11][21][33]
Slices New tags, low-resource languages, code-heavy questions, very short titles No slice regresses more than 2%

Online metrics & A/B

Metric Direction Note
Duplicate post rate (later closed as dup) Down Primary north star
Ask-flow deflection: user leaves satisfied after clicking a similar Q Up Guard against it suppressing genuinely new questions
Time to first useful answer Down Includes deflected sessions
Similar-panel CTR, search success rate Up Session-level
Successful-session rate, dwell on the clicked question Up CTR alone can reward clickbait titles [1]
Wrongly closed-as-dup or reopen rate Down (guardrail) Hurts new users
New-question volume and answerer engagement Not down (guardrail) Too much deflection starves the community
Latency p99, error rate Within SLO Infrastructure guardrail

Serving & latency

Step Budget (p99) Notes
Debounce and query cleaning about 5 ms Client debounce of 300-500 ms is not counted
Bi-encoder query embed (CPU/ONNX or GPU) about 10-15 ms Distilled MiniLM, int8
ANN (HNSW, sharded) plus BM25 in parallel about 15-20 ms k about 200 each
Fusion, filters, feature fetch about 15 ms Batched feature-store read
Cross-encoder on ~50-100 pairs (GPU, batched) about 40-60 ms Truncate bodies. Cache popular candidates
GBDT, policy, response about 10 ms
Total about 120-150 ms Search path. The dup check at submit can take longer

Monitoring

Signal Alert on
Embedding drift (mean cos to centroid, new-tag share) Shift beyond a baseline band
P(dup) score distribution and banner rate Sudden jump or drop (threshold or calibration broke)
Reopen rate after an auto-suggested dup Rise above the guardrail
ANN recall vs exact kNN, measured on a sample (HNSW / IVF-PQ) [30][31][34] Recall@100 below 0.95
Index freshness lag (post to searchable) More than 5 min
Latency p99 and GPU queue depth SLO breach

Failure modes

Failure Example Mitigation
Near-miss paraphrase "How to sort a list in Python" vs "...in Java" Entity and tag features, cross-encoder, hard negatives
Version drift Python 2 vs 3 answers now wrong Recency and version features. Prefer canonical questions with recent edits
Over-deflection New edge-case questions get marked dup High tau, "not a dup" button, guardrail metric
Transitive chain drift A~B~C~D but A is not D Cap cluster size, re-verify edges with the CE
Label bias Moderators favour popular targets Human audit set, IPS on click labels
Lexical-only blind spot Exact error string missed by dense retrieval Hybrid BM25 plus dense with RRF
Spam and SEO copies Copied questions cluster with real ones Spam classifier upstream, author features
Cold index after model swap New embeddings are not comparable with the old index Full re-embed, blue/green index swap
Asymmetric neighbours in mining B is A's top match but A is not B's, so (A,B),(B,C) chains appear Symmetrise pairs, re-score with the CE, then cluster [9]
Quadratic mining cost All-pairs compare is impractical beyond about 10k questions Chunked top-k mining (query_chunk_size, corpus_chunk_size, max_pairs) or ANN [9]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Is "similar" the same as "duplicate"? How do the two surfaces differ in threshold and metric?
  • Where do labels come from, and how do you handle false negatives among mined hard negatives?
  • Bi-encoder vs cross-encoder: why use both, and where does each run?
  • How do you set and maintain the duplicate threshold tau? What happens when the calibration drifts?
  • How do you prevent leakage when splitting pairs (the same question in train and test)?
  • How do you handle code snippets, stack traces and exact error messages?
  • How do you re-index 20M+ questions when the embedding model changes, without downtime?
  • How do you make a new question searchable within a minute?
  • How do you evaluate offline vs online? Which metric is the north star?
  • How do you stop over-deflection that discourages new questions?
  • How do you handle multilingual sites (for example, Stack Overflow in Portuguese)?
  • How would you mine and merge duplicate clusters offline? Why not use pure transitive closure?
  • Where would an LLM help (query rewrite, borderline judging, answer synthesis), and at what cost?
  • How do you debias click labels from the similar-questions panel?
  • How do you scale ANN to 10^8 vectors (PQ, sharding, memory per vector)?
  • Paraphrase mining returns asymmetric pairs: how do you turn them into stable clusters? [9]
  • How many candidates should the cross-encoder see (about 100 is the common default), and why? [29]
  • Which public benchmark would you sanity-check on (BEIR Quora, CQADupStack)? [33]

34. Design a Text-to-Image Generation Service (Midjourney, DALL-E) with Safety and Serving

Turn a text prompt (plus optional reference image, style, or aspect ratio) into 1-4 high-quality images in seconds. The service must stay safe at both the prompt and the pixel level, and cost cannot run away. In this design the "candidates" are N sampled images. "Ranking" means choosing among them by aesthetic and alignment scores, and "policy" covers safety classifiers, watermarking and provenance.

Research note: pages re-fetched in review: [1] [2] [3] [31] [32] [36] [37]. arXiv, openai.com, bytebytego.com and c2pa.org were unreachable from the sandbox; those entries are well-known papers or pages cited from prior knowledge and marked as such.

Requirements & scale

Dimension Requirement Note / source
Functional Text prompt -> 1-4 images. Options: aspect ratio, style, seed, negative prompt, variations, upscale, inpaint / outpaint with a mask, image prompt DALL-E 2 offered inpainting and variations [1]. Others are typical
Resolution 1024x1024 native, 2-4x upscale optional SDXL trained at 1024^2, multi-aspect [3] [7]
Latency Interactive: p50 ~5-10 s for 4 images, preview at ~1 s. Turbo mode: under 1 s Assumption. 1-4 step distilled models [12] [13]
Throughput 10M images/day ~ 115 img/s average, ~3-5x at peak Typical assumption
Users 10-20M MAU, heavy-tailed usage, paid tiers Assumption
Safety Block CSAM, sexual, violent, hateful, public-figure and deceptive content at prompt and output [1]
Provenance Invisible watermark plus C2PA metadata on every image [2] [3] [28] [40]
Cost GPU-seconds per image is the main cost lever. Sell GPU time by tier (fast / relax / turbo style queues) Assumption (Midjourney-style tiers)
Availability 99.9%. Degrade to fewer steps or images under load Assumption
Abuse Per-user rate limits, anomaly detection, account enforcement [1]

  • Steps 1 and 6 follow the DALL-E pattern: input filters on prompts and uploads, then output filters, with independent filters as a known gap [1]. The SD reference script also ships a post-hoc safety checker [2]
  • Step 2 (LLM prompt rewrite) is the DALL-E 3 pattern: descriptive captions at training time, upsampled prompts at inference [8]
  • Step 3 only hits for an identical prompt + seed + options + model version; diffusion is deterministic given the seed
  • Step 8: the SD reference stack applies an invisible watermark to every output [2] [3]; C2PA adds a signed manifest [28]

  • Data filtering: NSFW/violence classifiers plus hate-symbol caption filters. Filtering is tuned to avoid demographic skew (DALL-E 2 found the filter reduced images of women) [1]
  • SD v1.2-1.4 trained on LAION-Aesthetics (aesthetic > 5.0, size >= 512, low watermark prob.) and dropped the text 10% of the time to enable CFG [2] [16]
  • Recaptioning: DALL-E 3 trained on synthetic descriptive captions [8]. Quality tuning on a small curated set: Meta Emu [41]

DIAGRAM 3: Model architecture (latent diffusion with cross-attention)

Figure 34.3: Latent diffusion / DiT generator with classifier-free guidance

 prompt "a corgi astronaut, oil painting"       negative prompt, or "" (null)
            |                                            |
            v                                            v
 +-------------------------+                  +-------------------------+
 | TEXT ENCODER (frozen)   |                  | same text encoder       |
 | CLIP ViT-L / OpenCLIP   |                  +------------+------------+
 | ViT-G, and/or T5-XXL    |                               | c_null
 +------------+------------+                               |
              | c_text (L tokens x d)                      |
              v                                            v
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | DENOISER eps_theta(z_t, t, c)                 (repeat for t = T ... 1)   |
 |   U-Net (~860M in SD1) or DiT / MM-DiT transformer                       |
 |   z_t (4 x 128 x 128) -> ResBlocks + self-attn                           |
 |                       -> CROSS-ATTN (Q = image latents, K/V = text)      |
 |   CFG: eps = eps(z, c_null) + w * (eps(z, c_text) - eps(z, c_null))      |
 |        w ~ 5-8 ; sampler = DDIM / DPM-Solver / flow ODE                  |
 +-------+------------------------------------+-----------------------------+
         ^                                    |
         | z_T ~ N(0, I) from seed            | z_0 (clean latent)
         |                                    v
 +-------+--------+              +--------------------------+   +-------------+
 | noise sampler  |              | VAE DECODER (8x upsample)|-->| image       |
 | (seeded RNG)   |              | 4x128x128 -> 3x1024x1024 |   | 1024 x 1024 |
 +----------------+              +--------------------------+   +------+------+
                                                                       |
                                                                       v
                          optional: refiner (img2img, low noise), super-res
                          diffusion, ControlNet branch, LoRA style adapters

 TRAINING: x -> VAE encoder -> z_0 ;  z_t = a_t * z_0 + s_t * eps ;
           loss = || eps - eps_theta(z_t, t, c) ||^2   (or v / flow target)
  • LDM: diffusion in an 8x-downsampled VAE latent with cross-attention conditioning [2] [4]. SD1 uses an ~860M U-Net and a ~123M frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 [2]
  • SDXL: two text encoders (OpenCLIP ViT-G + CLIP ViT-L), 1024^2 multi-aspect training, plus a refiner used only as img2img [3] [7]
  • CFG [9]; DDPM/DDIM [10] [11]; DiT [14]; MM-DiT with rectified flow (SD3) [15]

DIAGRAM 4: Alternatives (pixel cascade vs latent vs distilled)

Figure 34.4: Three production generator families and where each one fits

 A) PIXEL CASCADE (Imagen; DALL-E 2 decoder)
 +------------+   +----------------+   +-----------------+   +------------------+
 | T5-XXL or  |-->| base diffusion |-->| SR diffusion    |-->| SR diffusion     |
 | CLIP prior |   | 64 x 64        |   | 64 -> 256       |   | 256 -> 1024      |
 +------------+   +----------------+   +-----------------+   +------------------+
   + strong text understanding (big LM encoder)   - 3 models, high latency/cost

 B) LATENT (Stable Diffusion / SDXL / SD3)
 +------------+   +-------------------------------+   +----------------+
 | CLIP / T5  |-->| U-Net / MM-DiT in VAE latent  |-->| VAE decode     |--> 1024^2
 +------------+   | 20-50 steps                   |   | (+ refiner)    |
                  +-------------------------------+   +----------------+
   + ~48x fewer values per step, one model   - VAE artifacts (small text, faces)

 C) DISTILLED / TURBO (SDXL-Turbo via ADD, LCM)
 +------------+   +-------------------------------+
 | teacher    |-->| student: 1-4 steps, no CFG    |--> real-time preview, free tier
 | (B)        |   | adversarial / consistency     |
 +------------+   +-------------------------------+
   + order-of-magnitude fewer steps   - lower diversity, weaker prompt following
  • Imagen: frozen T5-XXL plus a 64 -> 256 -> 1024 cascade [6]. DALL-E 2: CLIP prior plus diffusion decoder plus 2 upsamplers [5]
  • SDXL-Turbo uses adversarial diffusion distillation [3] [12]. LCM [13]. Guided distillation [39]

Stage Option Pros Cons

Metric Type
Download / upscale / share rate per generation Primary engagement
Reroll rate, prompt edit rate Dissatisfaction (lower is better)
Pairwise pick rate (new vs old model shown side by side) Model preference
p50/p95 time-to-first-image, queue wait Latency guardrail
GPU-seconds per kept image Cost guardrail

Serving & latency budget (4 images, 1024^2, standard mode)

Stage Budget Technique
Gateway, auth, quota 20 ms Edge
Prompt safety (blocklist + classifier + LLM judge) 100-300 ms Small models, cached verdicts
LLM prompt rewrite 300-800 ms Small LLM, run in parallel with safety, cancel on block
Queue wait 0-several s Priority queues by tier, autoscale on queue depth
Text encode 10-30 ms Cache by prompt hash
Denoise (25-30 steps, batch 4, CFG batched x2) 2-6 s on A100/H100 class GPUs fp16/bf16, FlashAttention, TensorRT/torch.compile, DPM-Solver
VAE decode 100-300 ms Tiled decode
Output safety + re-rank 50-150 ms Batched CLIP-based heads
Watermark + C2PA + upload 50-100 ms Async upload to CDN
Streaming previews Every k steps Latent preview decoder for perceived latency
  • Cost levers: fewer steps (distilled model for free tier), shared-batch CFG, feature caching across steps (DeepCache [44]), scale-to-zero LoRA adapters, result cache for repeated prompt+seed
  • Fleet: separate pools for base, upscale and inpaint. Preemptible GPUs for the "relax" tier

Monitoring

Signal Alert on
Safety filter block rate by category and locale Spikes (new jailbreak) or drops (classifier broken)
User reports per 1k images Above SLO
Output-classifier vs human-review disagreement Drift in safety models
Prompt distribution (embedding clusters) New trend or attack campaign
Aesthetic / CLIPScore of served images Quality regression after deploy
GPU utilization, queue depth, OOMs Capacity
Watermark detection rate on sampled outputs Provenance pipeline broken

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation Ref
Jailbreak via "visual synonyms" (ketchup for blood), misspellings, other languages Output classifiers, LLM judge, adversarial red-teaming loop [1] [22]
Benign prompt + benign upload = harmful combination Joint multimodal safety check [1]
Safety filter bypass on open weights In-model safety guidance, concept erasure [21] [22] [43]
Over-filtering silences groups / demographic skew Bias audits, calibrated thresholds [1]
Deepfakes of public figures, non-consensual imagery Face-match block, name stripping in rewrite, provenance [1] [28]
Copyright / living-artist style mimicry Artist-name filters, training opt-outs, data licensing [8]
Watermark removal (cropping a visible signature) Invisible watermark plus C2PA plus server-side lookup [1] [3] [40]
Poor text rendering, hands, counting T5 encoder, DiT, recaption, reward fine-tuning [6] [8] [15]
Low diversity after distillation or DPO Mix of teacher outputs, diversity metrics [12] [27]
GPU queue blowup at launch Tiered queues, degrade steps, waitlist [1]
Memorization / training-image extraction Dedupe training data, near-dup check on outputs [45]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why diffusion over GANs or autoregressive token models? What does each trade off in quality, diversity and latency?
  • Why run diffusion in latent space? What do you lose (VAE artifacts on text and faces)?
  • Explain classifier-free guidance. What happens as w goes up, and how do you train for it (null-text dropout)?
  • How would you get ~10 s generation time for 4 images down to under 1 s? (Distillation, schedulers, batching, caching, hardware.)
  • Web captions are noisy. How do you improve prompt following? (Recaptioning, LLM prompt rewrite.)
  • Where do safety filters go, and why is a prompt filter alone not enough?
  • How do you measure "quality" offline when FID disagrees with humans?
  • Design the human evaluation: side-by-side protocol, rater agreement, prompt set (PartiPrompts/DrawBench-style).
  • How would you use implicit user feedback (upscale and download picks) to improve the model? What are the bias risks?
  • How do you stop deepfakes of public figures and generation of copyrighted characters?
  • How do you watermark outputs, and how robust is the watermark to crops, compression and screenshots?
  • How do you schedule GPUs across free and paid tiers and handle a 10x launch spike?
  • How do you support personalization (DreamBooth/LoRA) at scale without one GPU per user?
  • How would you detect a new jailbreak campaign in production?
  • How do you check that the model is not reproducing memorized training images?
  • How do you design inpainting / outpainting (mask channel, masked-latent conditioning) and image prompts?
  • Which offline benchmark would you gate on (GenEval, T2I-CompBench, PartiPrompts), and why not FID alone?

35. Design a ChatGPT-like LLM Chatbot Platform: Serving, Safety, Evaluation & Feedback Loop

Prompt as usually given: "Design ChatGPT", "Design a personal-assistant chatbot", "Design an LLM chatbot at scale (1M+ DAU)", "Design a large-scale LLM inference / serving platform", "Design a multi-tenant LLM inference API". Deep-dive variants: KV cache and continuous batching, small/large model routing, guardrails, RLHF/DPO feedback loop, eval harness.

Compilation note (re-reviewed 2026-10-14): web search was exhausted and arxiv.org, openai.com, bytebytego.com, huyenchip.com and igotanoffer.com did not resolve from the build environment. GitHub pages marked "fetched" were re-read in this review. (ch-ref) = verified in an earlier chapter; (known; not fetched) = standard paper cited from prior knowledge. Numbers marked "typical assumption" are interview-style estimates.

Dimension Requirement / number Source

Users 100M WAU, 10M DAU-concurrent peak sessions ~1M typical assumption
QPS ~10 msgs/user/day x 50M DAU = 5e8/day -> ~6k avg, ~20k peak req/s typical assumption
Tokens ~1.5k input (history+system) + ~400 output per turn -> ~8M output tok/s peak typical assumption
GPU math ~2.5k-5k output tok/s per 8-GPU node (70B, batched) -> 2k-3k nodes at peak typical assumption
Context 8k-128k window (typical assumption); token budgeting + history compression [3]
Cost Cost per request / per 1M tokens; route by query difficulty [3]
Tenancy Charge est. input + max_tokens to per-org token bucket; 429 + Retry-After; separate interactive vs bulk queues [5]

DIAGRAM 3: Decoder-only chat LLM (inference view) plus the reward / safety classifier heads that share the same backbone family

  chat template:  <sys>...</sys> <user>...</user> <asst>  (token ids, len T)
                                   |
                                   v
                  +-------------------------------+
                  | Token embedding (vocab ~100k+)|
                  +---------------+---------------+
                                  v
          +---------------------------------------------------+
          |  N x Transformer decoder block                    |
          |  +---------------------------------------------+  |
          |  | RMSNorm -> causal self-attention            |  |
          |  |   RoPE positions, GQA heads,                |  |
          |  |   FlashAttention kernel                     |  |
          |  |   K,V --write/read--> [ paged KV cache ]    |  |
          |  | + residual                                  |  |
          |  | RMSNorm -> FFN (SwiGLU) or MoE (top-2 of E) |  |
          |  | + residual                                  |  |
          |  +---------------------------------------------+  |
          +-------------------------+-------------------------+
                                    v
                     +--------------+--------------+
                     | final norm                  |
                     +------+---------------+------+
                            |               |
            LM head (vocab) v               v scalar head
          +--------------------+     +-------------------------------+
          | logits -> temp,    |     | Reward model: r(prompt, resp) |
          | top-p sampling ->  |     | Safety clf: P(unsafe | cat_i) |
          | next token         |     | (separate small models, e.g.  |
          +---------+----------+     |  8B Llama-Guard-style)        |
                    |                +-------------------------------+
                    | append token, reuse KV (decode step, 1 tok)
                    +-----> loop until <eos> or max_tokens

  phases:  PREFILL  = all T prompt tokens in parallel  (compute-bound, sets TTFT)
           DECODE   = 1 token / step / sequence        (memory-bw bound, sets TPOT)

Data & labels

Data Use Label / signal Notes
Web crawl (Common Crawl, C4), code, books Pretraining Next token (self-supervised) Dedup, lang-id (fastText/langid), quality + toxicity filters [1]
Human demonstrations SFT Ideal response per prompt ~10k-100k high-quality; plus Alpaca/Dolly/FLAN-style sets [1][15]
Pairwise comparisons Reward model / DPO A > B (+ ties) Labeler rankings of K samples [15][16][18]
Production implicit feedback Preference mining, eval sets Thumbs, regenerate (= reject), edit, copy, abandon Noisy, biased toward vocal users; needs consent + de-id [13]
Arena / side-by-side votes Model ranking Elo / Bradley-Terry 1.5M+ votes in Chatbot Arena [9][37]
Red-team prompts Safety RM, refusal SFT, eval Harm category, should-refuse Human + automated red-teaming [25]
Moderation dataset Input/output classifiers Hazard taxonomy (MLCommons) Llama Guard 3 categories [11][22]

Features / context signals

Group Examples Where used
Conversation System prompt, last N turns, rolling summary, current leaf of branch Context builder [5]
User Memory facts, language, locale, custom instructions, tier Context builder, router, rate limit
Retrieved Web search / file / RAG chunks, tool results Context builder [12]
Request Est. input tokens + max_tokens, priority, tenant Gateway token bucket, scheduler [5]
Router signals Query length, domain, difficulty-clf score, prefix-cache locality Small vs large routing [3]
Safety Moderation scores per category, jailbreak score, PII spans Input/output rails [11][12]

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Component Baseline Advanced Tradeoff
Chat model Hosted API (one model) Own SFT + RLHF/DPO model family (small/large, MoE) Control + cost at scale vs time-to-market
Alignment SFT only RLHF (RM + PPO) [15] -> DPO [18] / Constitutional AI [17] PPO: strong but unstable/costly; DPO: simple, offline
Routing Single model Difficulty classifier / cascade small->large Cost down 2-5x; risk of misroutes
Serving engine HF generate, static batch vLLM / SGLang: continuous batching, PagedAttention / RadixAttention, prefix cache, chunked prefill (TGI archived 2026, points to vLLM/SGLang) [6][8][38] 2-4x+ throughput from memory efficiency [7]
Caching None Prefix/KV cache for shared system prompt; exact + semantic response cache for repeated queries [6][13][14] Semantic-cache false hits; never cache personalised answers
Model gateway Direct calls to one backend Unified gateway: auth, quotas, model-version routing, canary, fallback to other model/provider [3][13][14] Extra hop; fallback model may differ in safety behaviour
Latency tricks FP16 GQA, FlashAttention, FP8/INT4 quant, speculative decoding, P/D disaggregation [19][21][27][28] Quality regressions from quant must be gated
Input safety Keyword list + moderation API Prompt Guard 2 + Llama-Guard-style clf + NeMo input/dialog rails; retrieval + execution rails for RAG/tools [11][12] Latency + over-refusal vs coverage
Output safety Post-hoc full-response check Streaming chunk check + stop/replace Must not add per-token latency
Eval Static benchmarks LLM-as-judge win-rate, MT-Bench, arena, red-team suites [10][37] Judge bias (position, verbosity)

Loss / objectives

Stage Objective
Pretraining Cross-entropy next-token: -sum log p(x_t | x_<t)
SFT Same CE, masked to assistant tokens only
Reward model Bradley-Terry: -log sigmoid(r(x, y_w) - r(x, y_l)) [15]
RLHF (PPO) max E[r(x, y)] - beta * KL(pi || pi_SFT) (+ pretrain mix) [15]
DPO -log sigmoid(beta * [log pi(y_w)/pi_ref(y_w) - log pi(y_l)/pi_ref(y_l)]) [18]
Safety classifier Multi-label BCE over hazard categories [22]
Router BCE: P(small model answer is acceptable) from judge labels

Offline metrics

Area Metrics
Capability MMLU, GSM8K/MATH, HumanEval/MBPP, TriviaQA, HellaSwag, MT-Bench [1][10]
Preference LLM-as-judge pairwise win-rate vs prod model; arena Elo [10][37]
Safety Attack success rate on jailbreak suites (AdvBench), toxicity (RealToxicityPrompts), bias (BBQ), TruthfulQA, over-refusal rate [1]
Classifiers Precision / recall / F1 per harm category, latency
Serving TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99, tokens/s/GPU, cost per 1M tokens [3]

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Type Note
Thumbs-up rate, thumbs-down rate Quality (explicit) Sparse (<1-2% of turns rate); typical assumption
Regenerate rate, edit-and-resend rate Quality (implicit) Strong negative signal
Conversation length, D1/D7 retention, sessions/user Engagement Long convo can also mean failure
Side-by-side pick rate Preference Shown occasionally ("which response do you prefer?")
Safety incident rate, refusal rate, user reports Guardrail Both directions: harm and over-refusal
TTFT/TPOT p95, error + fallback rate, cost/conv System Guardrail metrics for every A-B [3]

Serving & latency budget (typical assumption, p95)

Step Budget
Gateway auth + rate limit 10 ms
Load history + memory 20-40 ms
Retrieval / web tool (optional) 100-800 ms
Input guardrails (parallel clf) 20-50 ms
Router 5-10 ms
Queue + prefill (2k tokens) 100-400 ms -> TTFT ~0.3-1 s
Decode 20-50 ms / token (TPOT)
Output guardrail per chunk (async, lagging window) ~0 added TTFT, small buffer

Monitoring

What Signal / alert
Capacity Queue depth, KV-cache utilisation, preemption rate, GPU util
Latency TTFT / TPOT p95/p99 per model, per region
Quality drift Daily judge win-rate on sampled prod traffic, thumbs-down spike, regenerate spike
Safety Block rate per category, new jailbreak clusters, user reports
Cost $/1M tokens, router small-model share, cache hit rate
Reliability Error rate, stream disconnects, fallback-to-other-provider count

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
KV-cache OOM under long contexts Paged KV, admission control, preempt/swap, max context per tier [7]
Head-of-line blocking by long prompts Chunked prefill, P/D disaggregation, separate interactive/batch queues [21][39]
Jailbreak / prompt injection via tools Prompt Guard, retrieval/execution rails, least-privilege tools [11][12]
Hallucination RAG with citations, refusal training, judge-based monitoring
Over-refusal after safety tuning Track over-refusal eval; safety RM separate from helpfulness RM [24]
Reward hacking (verbosity, sycophancy) KL penalty, length-controlled judges, fresh human evals
Feedback loop bias Sample beyond thumbs; stratify; human review before training
Stream drop mid-generation Resumable SSE: client resends Last-Event-ID and reattaches to the same generation; persist partial output [5]
User presses Stop but GPU keeps decoding Abort upstream request so the sequence leaves the batch and frees KV blocks [5]
Cancel races completion One atomic state transition decides outcome; edge-assigned request id owns the work [5]
Bad rollout (quality/latency regression) Shadow + canary + automatic rollback on guardrail metrics

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How does the KV cache work, and how much GPU memory does it need for 70B at 32k context?
  • When would you use static vs continuous batching, quantization, or speculative decoding? [3]
  • How would you route between a small and a large model, and how do you label the router? [3]
  • How do you reduce p99 latency without hurting answer quality? [3]
  • Why separate prefill and decode? What metric does each one control?
  • How do you rate-limit fairly by tokens per org when output length is unknown? [5]
  • How do you handle stop, regenerate, edit (branching), and a client reconnecting mid-stream? [5]
  • How do you keep a conversation sticky to a replica (consistent hashing with bounded load) and what happens once output has started? [5]
  • Where would you cache (prefix KV, exact, semantic), and what must never be cached? [13][14]
  • How do you manage context beyond the window (truncate, summarise, memory)?
  • RLHF vs DPO: tradeoffs, and how do you prevent reward hacking?
  • How do you turn thumbs and regenerations into training data without bias or privacy issues?
  • How do you evaluate a new model before launch? Benchmarks vs LLM-as-judge vs arena vs A-B.
  • Where do guardrails sit, and how do you moderate a stream without adding latency?
  • How do you defend against jailbreaks and prompt injection from retrieved pages?
  • Capacity math: how many GPUs for 20k req/s peak, and how do you autoscale?
  • Multi-region and provider failover: what state must be replicated?

Chip Huyen, "Designing ML Systems" (Ch. 9) Shadow, A/B, canary, interleaving, bandits [16]
ByteByteGo (Xu & Aminian) Online metrics and A/B test step in every chapter [17]
Kohavi, Tang, Xu book The reference text on platform architecture [9]
GrowthBook (open source) Reference implementation: flags + SDK, warehouse-native stats [12][13]

Requirements & scale

Category Requirement Value (typical assumption unless cited)
Functional Define experiment: variants, targeting, allocation %, metrics, duration -
Functional Deterministic, sticky assignment (user, device, session, or cluster unit) hash(unit_id, salt) [7]
Functional Route traffic to model variants (A = prod ranker, B = new ranker) -
Functional Concurrent overlapping experiments without collisions layers/domains [7]
Functional Automated scorecards: lift, CI, p-value, guardrails, SRM [1][4][8]
Functional Ramp, stop, ship; kill-switch -
Functional Feature flags as the delivery vehicle; SDK fires a tracking callback on exposure [12][13]
Functional Warehouse-native analysis: stats from aggregates (sums, sums of squares), no row-level PII leaves the warehouse [13]
Functional Frequentist or Bayesian engine, custom priors, multi-armed bandits [13]
Non-functional Assignment latency < 1-5 ms p99 (local SDK eval)
Non-functional Availability 99.99%; fail-open to control
Non-functional Trustworthiness SRM checks, A/A tests, pre-registered metrics [9]
Scale Concurrent experiments 1k-10k+ (Microsoft, Booking, Google scale [9])
Scale Assignment / exposure events 100k-1M QPS; 10-100B events/day
Scale Users 100M-1B units
Scale Metrics per scorecard 100s-1000s; daily batch plus near-real-time guardrails
Freshness Scorecard refresh Daily batch (ERF [1]); minutes for guardrails

Data & labels

Data Source Notes
Assignment/exposure SDK log at decision time Log only when the user is actually exposed (trigger analysis)
Outcome events Product logs (click, book, play, revenue) Joined after first exposure
Pre-period data Same metrics, 1-4 weeks before Covariates for CUPED [8]
Experiment metadata Config service Hypothesis, owner, OEC, guardrails, MDE

Features (unit-level covariates)

Feature Use
Pre-experiment metric value CUPED variance reduction (about 50% variance cut on Bing metrics [8])
Platform, country, tenure Stratification and slices
New vs returning Novelty/primacy checks
Bot / internal flags Exclusion

Model choices (statistical method)

Level Method Tradeoff
Baseline Fixed-horizon t-test, 50/50 split Simple, but invalid if people peek at results
+ CUPED / regression adjustment Smaller CI, needs pre-period data
+ Sequential testing (mSPRT, always-valid p) [14] Safe to peek; slightly wider CI
+ Bayesian (posterior P(B>A), expected loss) Intuitive; prior choice matters
+ Interleaving for rankers (Netflix reports ~100x fewer users needed) [5] Very sensitive, but only gives a preference, not business lift
Advanced Multi-armed / contextual bandits Less regret; harder inference, biased estimates
Advanced Switchback / cluster randomization (marketplaces) [6] Handles interference; less power

Loss / objective

Item Definition
OEC One pre-registered primary metric (e.g. bookings per user) [9]
Decision rule Ship if OEC CI > 0, no guardrail breach, SRM pass
Bandit objective Minimize cumulative regret

Offline metrics (platform health)

Metric Target
A/A false-positive rate about alpha (5%)
SRM rate across experiments < 1-2% of experiments
Bucketing uniformity chi-square pass
Offline-to-online correlation Track for each model family

Online metrics / A-B

Type Examples
OEC / primary Bookings/user, watch hours, GMV/user
Guardrails Latency p99, errors, crash rate, unsubscribes, revenue
Model-specific CTR, NDCG@k from logs, coverage, diversity
Platform Time to decision, % experiments that are well-powered

Serving & latency budget

Step Budget
SDK hash + config lookup (in memory) < 0.5 ms
Config refresh (push/poll) 10-60 s staleness OK
Model router to variant endpoint + 0 ms (pre-loaded)
Async exposure logging Off the critical path
Shadow model Async; never blocks response

Monitoring

Signal Action
SRM (p < 0.001) Invalidate scorecard, alert owner
Guardrail breach (near-real-time) Auto-ramp-down or kill-switch
Logging drop or delay Pipeline SLA alert
Interaction between concurrent experiments Pairwise interaction detection
Novelty decay Plot daily lift trend

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Peeking leads to false positives Sequential tests or fixed horizon [14]
SRM from bot filtering or redirects Exposure-based logging, SRM gate
Network effects / interference (marketplace) Cluster or switchback randomization, two-sided tests
Feedback loop: B model trains on A's data Train per-variant or use a holdout; flag data leakage
Carryover from reused buckets Re-salt per experiment, cooldown
Too many metrics, false discoveries FDR control, pre-registered OEC
Long-term vs short-term mismatch Long-running holdouts, surrogate metrics

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you guarantee sticky assignment across devices and logged-out users?
  • How do you run 1,000 concurrent experiments without collisions (layers/domains)?
  • What is SRM, how do you detect it, and what causes it?
  • How do you compute sample size / MDE, and what if traffic is too low?
  • Explain CUPED. Why does it reduce variance and not bias?
  • How do you handle peeking? Sequential vs Bayesian?
  • How do you compute variance for ratio metrics like CTR (delta method)?
  • How do you A/B test a ranking model: interleaving vs A/B?
  • Marketplace interference (Airbnb, Uber): how do you randomize?
  • How do you avoid the feedback loop where the new model trains on logs from the old model?
  • How do you pick the OEC and guardrails? What if metrics disagree?
  • Offline metrics improved but online did not. Why?
  • How do you measure long-term effects and novelty or primacy effects?
  • When would you use bandits instead of A/B?
  • How do you make the platform fail open, and what is the latency impact?
  • Warehouse-native (query the customer warehouse) vs a streaming metrics pipeline: tradeoffs in freshness, cost, privacy? [13]
  • Why compute every test from sufficient statistics (n, sum, sum of squares) per variant, and how does that scale to 1000s of metrics? [13]

37. Design an ML Platform: Feature Store + Training + Model Serving (Uber Michelangelo, Meta FBLearner)

Sourcing note (review, 2026-10): non-GitHub hosts (uber.com, engineering.fb.com, doordash.engineering, infoq.com, arxiv.org) did not resolve from this environment, and the web-search budget was exhausted. Fetched and read: GitHub sources [5][20][21][22][23][30]. The curated lists [20][21] confirm titles, years, and URLs for [1][2][4][6]-[10][14][15][18][31][33][34]. Platform numbers for Michelangelo and FBLearner are quoted from those posts and were not re-read in this pass. Tags below name the company whose published system the framing comes from. How often each company asks this question was not verified.

Company tags

Company (system the framing comes from) Typical framing Ref
Uber "Design Michelangelo": self-serve feature store, training, deploy, and online predictions for ETA, pricing, and fraud [1][4][35]
Meta "Design FBLearner": feature store, Flow (training DAGs), Predictor (serving); also "design a training data pipeline for recsys" [2][3][11][19]
Airbnb "Design a feature platform with point-in-time-correct backfills" (Zipline, open-sourced as Chronon) [10][23]
DoorDash "Design a low-latency online feature store" (Redis, billions of features); declarative real-time features (Riviera, Fabricator) [8][18][34]
LinkedIn "Design a feature store / feature registry" (Feathr) [9][30]
Netflix, Lyft, Shopify "Design an ML platform for data scientists"; fact store / time travel (Netflix), feature serving (Lyft) [15][16][17][31][33]
Google "Design a TFX-style pipeline": data validation, training, model analysis, push to serving [12]

Requirements & scale

Category Requirement Value (typical assumption unless cited)
Functional Register features once and reuse them in training and serving Michelangelo: about 10k shared features (2017) [1]
Functional Point-in-time-correct training sets (no label leakage) [5][10]
Functional Batch, streaming, and on-demand (request-time) features Hive + Kafka/Flink + request [1][4]
Functional Reproducible training workflows (DAGs), hyperparameter search, experiment tracking FBLearner Flow [2]
Functional Model registry, evaluation reports, one-click deploy, rollback [1]
Functional Online, batch, and embedded (library) prediction; shadow/A-B [1][11]
Functional Monitoring: prediction logging, joining with outcomes, drift [1]
Non-functional Online feature read latency p99 under 5-10 ms for a batch of about 100 features
Non-functional Prediction latency Michelangelo: P95 under 5 ms (no Cassandra features), under 10 ms with Cassandra [1]
Scale Prediction QPS Michelangelo: 250k+ pred/s for the top model (2017) [1]; about 10M pred/s at peak (2024) [35]; FBLearner: 6M+ pred/s (2016) [2]
Scale Models / users Thousands of models in production; 25%+ of FB engineering used FBLearner Flow [2]
Scale Online store size TB-scale key-value; DoorDash stores billions of feature values in Redis [8]
Non-functional Freshness Batch: daily; streaming: seconds to minutes
Non-functional Availability 99.99% serving; fall back to default or last-known feature values
Governance Lineage, ownership, ACLs, PII tagging, feature deprecation [9][14][30]
Functional Online/offline consistency measured, not assumed: log online fetches, replay as a backfill, compare [23]
Functional Input data validation before training (schema, ranges, missing values) [12]

                    | offline values                           | online values (logged)
                    |                                          |
                    |                                          |
                    v                                          v
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | Consistency monitor: log online fetches, replay offline, compare per key/ts    |
 | -> training-serving skew alerts; freshness lag per feature; null rate; drift   |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Diagram 4. Point-in-time (AS-OF) join, which prevents leakage when the spine is built

 time ---------------------------------------------------------------------->
 driver_42 feature "trips_24h":  v=10 @t1      v=14 @t3           v=20 @t6
 label event (spine row):                 ts=t4, label=late_eta=1
 AS-OF join picks latest value with feature_ts <= t4    --> 14  (correct)
 naive join on "latest" picks                           --> 20  (LEAKAGE)
 ttl check: if t4 - t3 > ttl                            --> null / default

Data & labels

Data Source Notes
Entity snapshots DB CDC dumps into the lake Daily partitions; keyed by entity_id
Events Kafka topics Feed both stream features and the offline log
Request context Prediction request Only available at serve time; it must be logged so training can use it
Labels Outcome tables (trip ETA actual, chargeback, click) Delayed; label window and maturity cutoff per use case
Prediction logs Serving fleet Features-as-served give skew-free training data ("log and wait")

Features (platform-level feature types)

Type Example Store / compute Freshness
Batch aggregate restaurant avg prep time over 30d Spark to offline, then copied online Daily
Streaming aggregate restaurant prep time, last 1h Flink to online and offline log Seconds to minutes
On-demand / request distance(pickup, dropoff), hour-of-day Computed in the serving container (DSL) Real time
Embeddings user / item vectors Batch job to the online KV or a vector index Daily
Cross / derived ratio of two features DSL transform, shared code for training and serving Inherits from inputs

Model choices (platform design choices, baseline to advanced)

Decision Baseline Advanced Trade-off
Feature store Shared tables + ad-hoc Redis Registry + dual store + PIT joins (Feast, Palette, Feathr) Consistency and reuse vs build cost
Transform logic Separate SQL (train) and Java (serve) One DSL compiled for both [1] Removes skew; DSL expressiveness is limited
Training orchestration Cron + notebooks DAG workflows (FBLearner Flow, Airflow, Kubeflow, Flyte) [2][16] Reproducibility vs flexibility
Model formats Per-team servers Standard artifact + feature spec; GBDT/DNN runtimes Simpler ops; harder for exotic models
Serving One service per model Multi-tenant prediction service with routing by tag Efficiency vs noisy neighbors
Online store Redis Cassandra / ScyllaDB / custom KV with compression [8] Latency vs cost per TB
Scope Platform for ML engineers Self-serve for analysts (Looper-style AutoML) [11] Adoption vs guardrails

Loss / objective

Level Objective
Per model Defined by the team (log-loss, MAE, ranking loss); the platform supplies standard evaluators
Platform Minimize time-to-production and skew incidents; maximize feature reuse and serving efficiency (cost per 1k predictions)

Offline metrics

Metric Target (typical)
Model quality vs champion (AUC, MAE, NDCG) by slice Gate: no regression above threshold
Training-serving skew (feature value mismatch rate) Under 0.1% of sampled keys
PIT-join correctness tests (no feature_ts > label_ts) 0 violations
Backfill time for a new feature (1 year of history) Hours, not days
Pipeline success rate / reproducibility (same snapshot gives same metrics) Above 99%

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Use
Business KPI of each model (ETA error, fraud loss, CTR) A/B of challenger vs champion, routed by the platform
Shadow-mode score diff Safety check before any user exposure
Platform KPIs: models shipped/week, time idea to prod, % features reused Platform-team success
Serving p50/p99, error rate, cost per prediction SLO dashboards

Serving & latency budget

Stage (online prediction, about 10 ms p99) Budget
Gateway + routing 1 ms
Online feature multi-get (batched, local-AZ KV) 3-4 ms
On-demand transforms 0.5 ms
Inference (GBDT on CPU, or a small DNN) 2-4 ms
Post-processing + async logging 0.5 ms
Options Batch prediction precomputed into the KV for slow-changing outputs; library mode (in-process) for ultra-low latency; GPU servers with dynamic batching for large DNNs

Monitoring

Signal How
Feature freshness lag Per-feature watermark vs SLA; page the owner
Feature distribution drift (PSI, null %) Compare online samples with training stats from the registry
Prediction drift / calibration Logged predictions joined with delayed outcomes [1]
Skew Log online fetches, replay them as an offline backfill, compare per key and ts (Chronon-style) [23]; Diagram 3
Data validation Schema and distribution checks on every training snapshot; block the run on anomalies [12]
Serving health p99, QPS, timeouts, fallback rate, per-tenant quotas
Lineage / audit Model to features to data sources, for incidents and deprecation

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Training-serving skew (different code paths) Single DSL, logging of features-as-served, skew monitors [1][23]
Hidden pipeline debt (glue code, undeclared consumers, feedback loops) Registry of consumers, typed feature contracts, ownership [13]
Label leakage from non-PIT joins AS-OF join API by default; tests that flag future timestamps
Stale online features (stream job down) TTLs, freshness alerts, fallback to batch values
Hot keys / KV overload Caching, request coalescing, replicas, compression [8]
Bad model pushed Eval gate, shadow, canary, auto-rollback on SLO or KPI breach
Feature deleted or changed under a live model Versioned features, consumer registry, deprecation workflow
Cost explosion (unused features) Usage tracking, auto-expire unused features, tiered storage
Noisy neighbor in a multi-tenant serving fleet Per-model resource isolation, quotas, separate pools for tier-0 models

Interviewer follow-ups

  • How do you guarantee a training row never sees a feature value from after its label timestamp?
  • Why keep both an offline and an online store? Could one store serve both?
  • How do you make the transform code identical in training and serving (DSL, shared library, or logging features-as-served)?
  • A new streaming feature needs 1 year of history to train on. How do you backfill it?
  • How would you bring p99 online feature reads under 5 ms with 300 features per request at 1M QPS?
  • How do you detect and debug training-serving skew in production?
  • How do you deploy and roll back a model safely (shadow, canary, A/B by tag)?
  • Batch vs online vs embedded prediction: when would you choose each?
  • How do you support thousands of per-city or partitioned models without thousands of services?
  • What metadata goes into the model registry, and how do you reproduce a model from 6 months ago?
  • How do you handle delayed labels (fraud chargebacks after 60 days) in retraining and monitoring?
  • How would you make the platform self-serve for non-ML engineers (Looper / AutoML)?
  • How do you manage GPU training capacity across teams (quotas, preemption, priority)?
  • How do you govern PII features (ACLs, retention, deletion requests)?
  • How does the platform change for LLMs (prompt/model registry, gateway, evaluation)? [35]
  • How do you prove online and offline features match (log-and-replay consistency score) and alert on it? [23]
  • How do you backfill a windowed aggregate for a new feature over a year of events without recomputing the world (tiled / incremental aggregation)? [23][33]
  • Where would you put data validation, and what happens to a scheduled retrain when it fails? [12]

38. Design Exploration for Cold-Start Items and Users (Bandits) in a Recommender

How the prompt is usually worded: "Netflix shows one artwork per title. Pick the best image for each member" [1], or "New creators and new items never get impressions. Fix the cold start" [16][17]. It also comes up as a follow-up to any recommendation question: "How do you balance exploration and exploitation?" [16][17][18]. Variants: Spotify Home shelves (BaRT) [3], DoorDash homepage explore/exploit [5], best merchant image [6], Twitter deep Bayesian bandits [7], Expedia cascade ranking [8].

Sourcing note: written and reviewed after the shared web-search budget ran out; non-GitHub hosts returned 403 through the proxy. (fetched) = read from GitHub for this chapter. (list) = URL, title and company confirmed in a fetched curated list [19][22] but the page itself not re-read. (known) = canonical paper cited from memory. Details from (list) or (known) sources are flagged as such.

Company tags

Company What is reported Source
Netflix The original product: per-member artwork chosen with contextual bandits. Netflix also published slate-bandit research [1][2] (list)
Spotify BaRT bandits for Home shelves and explanations. RL used to shift listening toward diverse content [3][4] (list)
DoorDash Homepage explore/exploit for new or rarely seen stores (UCB-style). Exploration to pick each merchant's image [5][6] (list)
Expedia, Stitch Fix Cascade bandits for ranking; a bandit experimentation platform [8][9] (list)
Twitter Meta-learning for cold-start items. Deep Bayesian bandits (dropout / bootstrap uncertainty) for exploration in ad recommendations [10][7] (list)
Yahoo! LinUCB news-article bandit and replay evaluation, the classic references [11][12] (known)
Google/YouTube Top-K off-policy REINFORCE recommender. Zero-shot transfer from recsys to cold-start search [27] (known), [31] (list)
ByteDance/TikTok For You feed deliberately mixes in videos outside a user's shown interests [32] (list)
Coveo Content-based inference of embeddings for new and rare products [33] (list)

Meta, LinkedIn and others ask cold start and explore/exploit as generic recsys follow-ups (alirezadir and ByteByteGo templates [16][17][21]), but no company-specific source was verified, so they are not tagged.

Portal / source Treatment Link
alirezadir / Machine-Learning-Interviews The video and game recommendation templates each have a "Cold start problem" and an "Exploration exploitation trade-off (multi-armed bandit)" section. The MLSD template lists bandits under online testing [16][17][18] (fetched)
ByteByteGo (Aminian & Xu) Ch. 6 (video recs) cites the multi-armed bandit as its explore/exploit reference. Ch. 10 (news feed) cites cold start [21] (fetched)

Requirements & scale

Dimension Value Basis
Functional Pick an arm (artwork, new item, new creator) for each user and slot. Give new items a guaranteed but bounded number of impressions. Learn quickly from feedback [1][5]
Arms per decision Artwork: about 5-20 images per title. Item exploration: 10^2-10^4 cold candidates assumption
Catalog 10^4 titles (Netflix-like) up to 10^8 items or creators (UGC) assumption
Users 10^8 MAU. Interactions arrive in a stream assumption
QPS 10^5 page requests/s at peak, each needing 10-100 bandit decisions assumption
Latency Policy step p99 under 10-20 ms inside a 150-200 ms page budget assumption
Freshness Posteriors and counts updated in minutes, and the model retrained daily assumption
Exploration budget 1-10% of impressions, or a bounded regret target. Guardrails on watch time and retention assumption
Non-functional Log the propensity for every decision. Assign arms per session without flicker. Stay fair to new creators [1][12]

Data & labels

Item Choice
Unit of logging (context x, arm a, propensity p(a given x), reward r, slot, timestamp) [1][12]
Reward Artwork: play within the session or quality plays (exclude quick aborts) [1]. Items: click, then long dwell, save or follow
Delayed reward Join within an attribution window (for example 24 h). Count late rewards as positives when joined
Negatives Impressed but not engaged. Skipped arms count only if actually viewed (viewport)
Explore data Keep a uniformly randomized slice for unbiased evaluation [1][11][12]
Bias Position and presentation bias. Trust only data that carries logged propensities

Features

Group Examples Cold-start relevance
User Embedding, genre affinity, recency, device New user: onboarding picks, geo/locale, device, popular prior
Item / arm content Image embedding, text, genre, cast, creator follower count Only signal on day 0 [10][13]
Item stats Impressions, CTR posterior (alpha, beta), age Low counts mean high uncertainty and a bigger bonus
Context Time, row/shelf, page position, country Artwork effect varies by context [1]
Cross User genre x artwork theme, user x creator category Personalized explore

Model choices (baseline -> advanced)

Level Model Pros Cons
0 Popularity + fixed new-item boost Simple Not personalized; can be gamed
1 Epsilon-greedy over the ranker Easy, gives propensities Wastes traffic uniformly [3]
2 Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling per arm [14] Efficient for few arms No context; slow for long tail
3 LinUCB / linear TS, contextual [11] Personalized, closed-form update Linear; feature engineering
4 Neural bandit (NN + Bayesian last layer, ensembles) [15] Rich features, shared learning Calibration of sigma, cost
4b Deep Bayesian bandit at production scale: MC dropout or bootstrapped heads on the ranker [7] Reuses the existing ranker; cheap sigma Uncertainty is approximate; needs tuning
5 Slate / cascade bandits, top-K off-policy RL [2][8][27] Handles whole page Complex, high variance
Cold-start add-on Content tower, DropoutNet, meta-learning, content-to-embedding inference [10][13][33] Day-0 scores Needs good content features
Cold-start transfer Zero-shot transfer of recsys embeddings to a new surface with no logs [31] Launch a surface without data Domain mismatch

Loss functions

Component Loss
Reward model Binary cross-entropy on r, weighted by 1/p(a given x) (IPS), clipped
Watch time MSE or weighted logistic on log-duration
Cold tower BCE plus an alignment loss: content embed close to learned ID embed (DropoutNet-style) [13]
Policy (RL variant) REINFORCE with off-policy correction and a top-K correction [27]
Objective Minimize cumulative regret, the sum over t of r(best arm) - r(chosen arm)

Offline metrics

Metric Use
Replay / rejection-sampling estimate Unbiased on uniformly random logs. Used for Netflix artwork and Yahoo! news [1][12]
IPS, SNIPS, doubly robust Off-policy value with logged propensities [28]
AUC / log loss of reward model Sanity check, sliced by cold vs warm
Calibration of sigma Coverage of credible intervals
Simulated regret Bandit simulator on historical data before launch

Online metrics / A-B

Metric Goal
Take rate / play rate per impression Primary for artwork [1]
New-item coverage Percent of new items reaching N impressions within T hours
Time to first signal Hours until a new item's posterior is confident
Creator retention Percent of new creators posting again (supply side)
Diversity / filter bubble Share of impressions outside a user's top interests; catalog coverage [4][32]
Guardrails Session watch time, retention, complaints, latency
Test design Bandit vs control A/B with user-level randomization. Keep an always-on random-explore bucket [9]

Serving & latency budget (assumption, page p99 about 200 ms)

Stage Budget
Retrieval (warm ANN + cold pool + popular) 30 ms
Feature fetch 20 ms
Ranker with uncertainty head 50 ms
Bandit sampling (TS draw per arm, caps) 5-10 ms
Re-rank and artwork selection 10 ms
Logging (async) 0 ms on the critical path
Param store reads Cached in-process and refreshed every 1-5 min

Monitoring

Signal Alert on
Exploration rate Drift from the target band (for example 5% plus or minus 1%)
Propensity logging Missing or zero propensities (breaks OPE)
Posterior health Arms stuck at the prior; variance collapse
Cold-item funnel Drop in new items reaching the impression threshold
Reward delay Rising join latency; reward-pipeline lag
Business guardrails Watch-time regression in explore buckets

Failure modes

Failure Mitigation
Over-exploration hurts users Cap the explore share; explore only in low-cost slots; use TS, not uniform
Clickbait artwork wins on clicks Reward quality plays, not clicks [1]
Feedback loop / rich-get-richer Guaranteed impression budget for new items; diversity re-rank [4]
Non-stationarity (trends, novelty) Discounted posteriors or sliding windows
Artwork flicker across sessions Sticky per-member assignment for a period
Spam creators farming the boost Quality and integrity gates before cold-pool entry
Delayed rewards bias the posterior Pending-reward handling; batch updates after the window
Biased offline evaluation Log propensities; keep a random bucket; use doubly robust estimators [28]

Interviewer follow-ups

  • Why use a bandit instead of an A/B test for choosing artwork? What regret does A/B pay? [1][22]
  • Thompson sampling vs UCB vs epsilon-greedy: which do you pick and why? [11][14]
  • How do you evaluate a new policy offline without deploying it (replay, IPS, DR)? [12][28]
  • What do you log so that off-policy evaluation is possible later?
  • How do you get a sigma (uncertainty) out of a deep ranker? [15]
  • A new creator uploads a video. Walk through its first 24 hours of impressions.
  • A new user has no history. What do you show first, and how fast do you personalize?
  • How do you pick the explore budget, and who pays for it (which users or slots)?
  • Rewards arrive hours later. How do you update the bandit?
  • How do you stop clickbait thumbnails from winning? [1]
  • How do you explore over a slate or whole page rather than one slot? [2][8]
  • How do you handle non-stationary arm rewards (seasonality, trending)?
  • How would you balance fairness to new creators against user engagement? [4]
  • When would you move from bandits to full RL (long-term value)? [27]
  • Your ranker is a deep net. How do you add exploration without a separate bandit model (dropout or bootstrap heads)? [7]
  • You launch a new surface or market with no logs. How do you bootstrap it? [31]
  • How do you keep users out of a filter bubble without hurting engagement? [4][32]

Portal comparison

Source Framing Cold-start answer Exploration answer Gap
alirezadir video/game recs [16][17] Section inside the recsys template Two-tower with profile features; show new items to random users, then fine-tune Multi-armed bandit, defined briefly No policy, logging or OPE detail
ByteByteGo ch. 6 / ch. 10 [21] Follow-up in video and feed recs Content features and popular prior MAB reference only No serving design for bandits
Chip Huyen DMLS ch. 9 [22] Testing in production n/a Bandits vs A/B; contextual bandits as exploration Not a full recsys design
Netflix artwork blog [1] Real production system Per-title image pool Contextual bandit, randomized explore, replay metric Not an interview script
DoorDash / Spotify blogs [3][5] Real production systems UCB bonus for rarely seen stores Epsilon-greedy (BaRT), UCB (DoorDash) Company-specific constraints
